entry.summary: Introduces SPENCE, a framework for detecting benchmark contamination in NL2SQL by generating systematic syntactic variants of test queries. Measures execution accuracy changes across increasing syntactic distance to detect memorization.

entry.title: Understanding the Prompt Sensitivity

author.name: Yang Liu, Chenhui Chu

entry.summary: Analyzes LLM prompt sensitivity through first-order Taylor expansion, deriving upper bounds on log-probability differences using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Shows LLMs disperse similar inputs rather than clustering them, explaining sensitivity to semantically equivalent prompts.

entry.title: A Survey on the Security of Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents: Toward Mnemonic Sovereignty

author.name: Zehao Lin, Chunyu Li, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Surveys the security of long-term memory in LLM agents, framing persistent writable memory as an independent security problem. Develops a memory-lifecycle framework addressing poisoning, unauthorized access, and cross-session attacks.

entry.title: From Fallback to Frontline: When Can LLMs be Superior Annotators of Human Perspectives?

author.name: Hasan Amin, Harry Yizhou Tian, Xiaoni Duan, Chien-Ju Ho, Rajiv Khanna, Ming Yin

entry.summary: Challenges the presumption that LLMs are inferior annotators of human perspectives, showing conditions where LLMs outperform human annotators (including in-group humans) for estimating aggregate subgroup opinions. Attributes this to low variance and reduced bias coupling.

entry.title: OneVL: One-Step Latent Reasoning and Planning with Vision-Language Explanation

author.name: Jinghui Lu, Jiayi Guan, Zhijian Huang, Jinlong Li, Guang Li, Lingdong Kong, Yingyan Li, Han Wang, Shaoqing Xu, Yuechen Luo, Fang Li, Chenxu Dang, Junli Wang, Tao Xu, Jing Wu, Jianhua Wu, Xiaoshuai Hao, Wen Zhang, Tianyi Jiang, Lingfeng Zhang, Lei Zhou, Yingbo Tang, Jie Wang, Yinfeng Gao, Xizhou Bu, Haochen Tian, Yihang Qiu, Feiyang Jia, Lin Liu, Yigu Ge, Hanbing Li, Yuannan Shen, Jianwei Cui, Hongwei Xie, Bing Wang, Haiyang Sun, Jingwei Zhao, Jiahui Huang, Pei Liu, Zeyu Zhu, Yuncheng Jiang, Zibin Guo, Chuhong Gong, Hanchao Leng, Kun Ma, Naiyang Wang, Guang Chen, Kuiyuan Yang, Hangjun Ye, Long Chen

entry.summary: Presents OneVL, a unified VLA and World Model framework for autonomous driving that compresses chain-of-thought reasoning into latent representations grounded in visual dynamics rather than purely linguistic abstractions, enabling real-time deployment.

entry.title: Agentic Large Language Models for Training-Free Neuro-Radiological Image Analysis

author.name: Ayhan Can Erdur, Daniel Scholz, Jiazhen Pan, Benedikt Wiestler, Daniel Rueckert, Jan C. Peeken

entry.summary: Presents a training-free agentic pipeline for automated brain MRI analysis using LLMs (GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5) orchestrating specialized external tools for volumetric medical imaging.

entry.title: Diverse Dictionary Learning

author.name: Yujia Zheng, Zijian Li, Shunxing Fan, Andrew Gordon Wilson, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Diverse Dictionary Learning introduces universal inductive biases for latent variable recovery when full identifiability is unattainable, providing guarantees on what can still be recovered in general nonlinear settings.

entry.title: MoVE: Translating Laughter and Tears via Mixture of Vocalization Experts in Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Szu-Chi Chen, I-Ning Tsai, Yi-Cheng Lin, Sung-Feng Huang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Proposes MoVE, a Mixture-of-LoRA-Experts architecture for preserving non-verbal vocalizations (laughter, crying) in speech-to-speech translation. Shows that only 30 minutes of curated data is sufficient when leveraging pretrained AudioLLMs. From Hung-yi Lee's group.

entry.title: Efficient Low-Resource Language Adaptation via Multi-Source Dynamic Logit Fusion

author.name: Chen Zhang, Jiuheng Lin, Zhiyuan Liao, Yansong Feng

entry.summary: Proposes TriMix, a test-time logit fusion framework for low-resource language adaptation that dynamically balances LRL competence, task competence, and large model scaling. Requires no LRL task annotations and only continual pretraining on the small model.

entry.title: Experience Compression Spectrum: Unifying Memory, Skills, and Rules in LLM Agents

author.name: Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang, Yanwei Cui, Wei Qiu, Ziyuan Li, Bing Zhu, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Proposes the Experience Compression Spectrum, a unifying framework that positions agent memory, skills, and rules along a single axis of increasing compression (5-20x for episodic memory up to 1000x+ for declarative rules). Reveals near-zero cross-citation between memory and skill discovery communities despite addressing the same challenge.

entry.title: Rethinking the Comparison Unit in Sequence-Level Reinforcement Learning: An Equal-Length Paired Training Framework from Loss Correction to Sample Construction

author.name: Fei Ding, Yongkang Zhang, Runhao Liu, Yuhao Liao, Zijian Zeng, Huiming Yang, Sibo wang, Linglin Liao

entry.summary: Identifies that the length problem in sequence-level RL is fundamentally about comparison unit construction rather than just loss scaling. Proposes equal-length paired training that constructs comparable training segments proactively.

entry.title: Bit-Flip Vulnerability of Shared KV-Cache Blocks in LLM Serving Systems

author.name: Yuji Yamamoto, Satoshi Matsuura

entry.summary: Identifies vulnerabilities in shared KV-cache blocks in LLM serving systems (vLLM's Prefix Caching) where bit-flip attacks can cause silent, selective, and persistent output corruption. Single physical copy without integrity protection enables targeted attacks.

entry.title: AnchorMem: Anchored Facts with Associative Contexts for Building Memory in Large Language Models

author.name: Zhanyu Shen, Sijie Cheng, Zhicheng Guo, Weiqin Wang, Yile Wang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Introduces AnchorMem, a memory framework for LLMs inspired by the Proust Phenomenon where specific anchors trigger holistic recollection. Decouples retrieval units from generation context by extracting atomic facts as retrieval anchors while preserving rich associative context.

entry.title: Measuring Distribution Shift in User Prompts and Its Effects on LLM Performance

author.name: Parker Seegmiller, Sarah Masud Preum

entry.summary: Introduces LENS framework for measuring and evaluating the impact of natural prompt distribution shift on deployed LLMs. Provides a data-centric approach for quantifying how user prompt distributions change over time and affect model reliability.

entry.title: QuickScope: Certifying Hard Questions in Dynamic LLM Benchmarks

author.name: Taylor Lundy, Narun K. Raman, Kevin Leyton-Brown

entry.summary: Introduces QuickScope for efficiently identifying hard questions in dynamic LLM benchmarks using modified Bayesian optimization. Addresses the expensive evaluation problem when benchmarks generate unlimited question variants and the goal is finding model weaknesses.

entry.title: Evaluating Tool-Using Language Agents: Judge Reliability, Propagation Cascades, and Runtime Mitigation in AgentProp-Bench

author.name: Bhaskar Gurram

entry.summary: Introduces AgentProp-Bench revealing that automated evaluation of tool-using agents is unreliable—substring matching achieves only chance-level agreement with humans (κ=0.049), while LLM ensembles reach moderate agreement (κ=0.432).

entry.title: DexWorldModel: Causal Latent World Modeling towards Automated Learning of Embodied Tasks

author.name: Yueci Deng, Guiliang Liu, Kui Jia

entry.summary: Introduces DexWorldModel with Causal Latent World Model using DINOv3 features, O(1) memory via dual-state TTT memory, and speculative async inference for manipulation tasks, achieving 50% latency reduction.

entry.title: EVE: Verifiable Self-Evolution of MLLMs via Executable Visual Transformations

author.name: Yongrui Heng, Chaoya Jiang, Han Yang, Shikun Zhang, Wei Ye

entry.summary: EVE introduces a self-evolution framework for MLLMs that bypasses pseudo-labels by using executable visual transformations for deterministic external feedback, continuously diversifying training distributions.

entry.title: 9 kinds of hard-to-verify tasks

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Taxonomizes 9 distinct types of 'hard-to-verify tasks' for AI systems, arguing that the category is heterogeneous (unlike easy-to-verify tasks which share a common structure). Different types include expensive inference verification, contested values, side effects, and more.

entry.title: The World Leaks the Future: Harness Evolution for Future Prediction Agents

author.name: Chuyang Wei, Maohang Gao, Zhixin Han, Kefei Chen, Yu Zhuang, Haoxiang Guan, Yanzhi Zhang, Yilin Cheng, Jiyan He, Huanhuan Chen, Jian Li, Yu Shi, Yitong Duan, Shuxin Zheng

entry.summary: Presents a framework for future prediction agents that leverages temporal contrasts between earlier and later predictions on the same question to expose omissions in evidence gathering. Uses evolutionary principles where revisiting unresolved questions over time provides richer supervision than just final outcomes.

entry.title: ReactBench: A Benchmark for Topological Reasoning in MLLMs on Chemical Reaction Diagrams

author.name: Qiang Xu, Shengyuan Bai, Yu Wang, He Cao, Leqing Chen, Yuanyuan Liu, Bin Feng, Zijing Liu, Yu Li

entry.summary: ReactBench is a benchmark revealing that MLLMs fail sharply at structural/topological reasoning in chemical reaction diagrams, even on basic tasks like counting endpoints when diagrams have branching, converging, or cyclic structures. Exposes a fundamental gap between semantic comprehension and structural reasoning.

entry.title: When the Loop Closes: Architectural Limits of In-Context Isolation, Metacognitive Co-option, and the Two-Target Design Problem in Human-LLM Systems

author.name: Z. Cheng, N. Song

entry.summary: Autoethnographic case study documenting how a single subject who built an LLM-based cognitive self-regulation system experienced rapid loss of autonomous decision-making within 48 hours. Identifies 'context contamination' as the architectural mechanism and proposes the 'two-target problem' for human-LLM systems.

entry.title: Harmonizing Multi-Objective LLM Unlearning via Unified Domain Representation and Bidirectional Logit Distillation

author.name: Yisheng Zhong, Sijia Liu, Zhuangdi Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-objective LLM unlearning framework that harmonizes four goals: removing undesirable knowledge, preserving utility, avoiding over-refusal, and ensuring robustness against adversarial probing. Uses unified domain representation and bidirectional logit distillation.

entry.title: FineSteer: A Unified Framework for Fine-Grained Inference-Time Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Weng, Jinghuai Zhang, Kunlin Cai, Ying Li, Peiran Wang, Yuan Tian

entry.summary: FineSteer decomposes inference-time steering into conditional steering (when to steer) and fine-grained vector synthesis (how to steer), enabling more precise control over LLM behavior without parameter updates. Uses subspace-guided conditional activation.

entry.title: SecureRouter: Encrypted Routing for Efficient Secure Inference

author.name: Yukuan Zhang, Mengxin Zheng, Qian Lou

entry.summary: SecureRouter presents an encrypted routing framework that accelerates secure transformer inference by selecting different-sized models for different encrypted inputs based on difficulty, all under encryption. Addresses the inefficiency of using fixed-size models for all inputs.

entry.title: PolicyBank: Evolving Policy Understanding for LLM Agents

author.name: Jihye Choi, Jinsung Yoon, Long T. Le, Somesh Jha, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: PolicyBank is a memory mechanism for LLM agents operating under organizational policies that iteratively refines policy understanding through interaction and feedback, rather than treating the policy document as immutable ground truth. Aims to close specification gaps through experience.

entry.title: Closing the Theory-Practice Gap in Spiking Transformers via Effective Dimension

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu Ming Yiu

entry.summary: Establishes the first comprehensive expressivity theory for spiking transformers, proving universal approximation for spiking self-attention and deriving tight spike-count lower bounds via rate-distortion theory.

entry.title: EVIL: Evolving Interpretable Algorithms for Zero-Shot Inference on Event Sequences and Time Series with LLMs

author.name: David Berghaus

entry.summary: Introduces EVIL, using LLM-guided evolutionary search to discover interpretable Python/NumPy algorithms for time series and event sequence inference. Evolved algorithms generalize across datasets without per-dataset training.

entry.title: DPrivBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Reasoning for Differential Privacy

author.name: Erchi Wang, Pengrun Huang, Eli Chien, Om Thakkar, Kamalika Chaudhuri, Yu-Xiang Wang, Ruihan Wu

entry.summary: Introduces DPrivBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can reason about differential privacy guarantees. Evaluates LLMs on determining if algorithms satisfy stated DP properties under given assumptions.

entry.title: Towards Intrinsic Interpretability of Large Language Models:A Survey of Design Principles and Architectures

author.name: Yutong Gao, Qinglin Meng, Yuan Zhou, Liangming Pan

entry.summary: Systematic survey of intrinsic interpretability approaches for LLMs, categorizing them into five design paradigms: functional transparency, concept alignment, representational decomposability, explicit modularization, and one more.

entry.title: Mind's Eye: A Benchmark of Visual Abstraction, Transformation and Composition for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Rohit Sinha, Aditya Kanade, Sai Srinivas Kancheti, Vineeth N Balasubramanian, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: Introduces Mind's Eye benchmark for visual cognitive reasoning in MLLMs, with tasks inspired by human intelligence tests under an Abstraction-Relation-Transformation taxonomy. Top MLLMs remain below 50% while humans achieve 80%.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic ODE Discovery with Latent Grammar Flow

author.name: Karin Yu, Eleni Chatzi, Georgios Kissas

entry.summary: Introduces Latent Grammar Flow (LGF), a neuro-symbolic framework for discovering ordinary differential equations from data by embedding equations as grammar-based representations in a discrete latent space with behavioral similarity constraints. A discrete flow model guides sampling of candidate equations. Bridges symbolic regression and neural generative models.

entry.title: Shifting the Gradient: Understanding How Defensive Training Methods Protect Language Model Integrity

author.name: Satchel Grant, Victor Gillioz, Jake Ward, Thomas McGrath

entry.summary: Compares two defensive training methods for LLMs - positive preventative steering (PPS) and inoculation prompting (IP) - finding they achieve defensive benefits through distinct mechanisms. PPS and IP are not doing the same thing despite similar surface-level processes.

entry.title: Global Attention with Linear Complexity for Exascale Generative Data Assimilation in Earth System Prediction

author.name: Xiao Wang, Zezhong Zhang, Isaac Lyngaas, Hong-Jun Yoon, Jong-Youl Choi, Siming Liang, Janet Wang, Hristo G. Chipilski, Ashwin M. Aji, Feng Bao, Peter Jan van Leeuwen, Dan Lu, Guannan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces STORM, a spatiotemporal transformer with linear-complexity global attention for generative data assimilation in Earth system prediction, reformulating assimilation as Bayesian posterior sampling. Targets exascale computing.

entry.title: LLM-Extracted Covariates for Clinical Causal Inference: Rethinking Integration Strategies

author.name: Lei Liu, Jialin Chen, Kathy Macropol

entry.summary: Studies how LLM-extracted covariates from clinical notes can be integrated into causal inference pipelines for EHR data, comparing seven integration strategies on sepsis patients from MIMIC-IV for estimating vasopressor treatment effects.

entry.title: Untrained CNNs Match Backpropagation at V1: A Systematic RSA Comparison of Four Learning Rules Against Human fMRI

author.name: Nils Leutenegger

entry.summary: Systematic comparison of four learning rules (backpropagation, feedback alignment, predictive coding, STDP) against human fMRI data, finding that early visual alignment is primarily architecture-driven, with untrained networks matching backpropagation at V1.

entry.title: D-QRELO: Training- and Data-Free Delta Compression for Large Language Models via Quantization and Residual Low-Rank Approximation

author.name: Junlin Li, Shuangyong Song, Guodong Du, Ngai Wong, Xuebo Liu, Yongxiang Li, Min Zhang, Jing Li, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: D-QRELO combines one-bit quantization with residual low-rank approximation for training- and data-free delta compression of fine-tuned LLMs, addressing failures of existing methods when models are fine-tuned with large-scale datasets.

entry.title: Tree of Concepts: Interpretable Continual Learners in Non-Stationary Clinical Domains

author.name: Dongkyu Cho, Xiyue Li, Samrachana Adhikari, Rumi Chunara

entry.summary: Tree of Concepts combines interpretable decision trees with concept bottleneck models for continual learning in clinical settings, maintaining interpretability while enabling adaptation to distribution shifts.

entry.title: Decomposing the Depth Profile of Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jayadev Billa

entry.summary: Systematically studies the depth profile of representational change during fine-tuning across 240 runs, 15 models, and 4 architecture families. Finds change concentrates in output-proximal layers but this can be controlled.

entry.title: REALM: Reliable Expertise-Aware Language Model Fine-Tuning from Noisy Annotations

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Mark Beliaev, Mahnoosh Alizadeh, Ramtin Pedarsani

entry.summary: REALM jointly learns LLM parameters and per-annotator expertise scores during fine-tuning, modeling each label as a mixture between the model's prediction and random guessing, weighted by learned expertise.

entry.title: Interpolating Discrete Diffusion Models with Controllable Resampling

author.name: Marcel Kollovieh, Sirine Ayadi, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: IDDM introduces controllable resampling in discrete diffusion models that partially resets probability mass to the marginal distribution, enabling self-correction while reducing dependence on intermediate states.

entry.title: SVL: Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning as Survival Learning

author.name: Franki Nguimatsia Tiofack, Fabian Schramm, Th\'eotime Le Hellard, Justin Carpentier

entry.summary: Reframes goal-conditioned RL as survival learning, modeling time-to-goal as a distribution and expressing value functions as discounted sums of survival probabilities, enabling maximum likelihood training.

entry.title: Prior-Fitted Functional Flow: In-Context Generative Models for Pharmacokinetics

author.name: C\'esar Ojeda, Niklas Hartung, Wilhelm Huisinga, Tim Jahn, Purity Kamene Kavwele, Marian Klose, Piyush Kumar, Rams\'es J. S\'anchez, Darius A. Faroughy

entry.summary: Prior-Fitted Functional Flows is a generative foundation model for pharmacokinetics enabling zero-shot population synthesis and individual patient forecasting with calibrated uncertainty from sparse, irregular clinical data.

entry.title: HiP-LoRA: Budgeted Spectral Plasticity for Robust Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Lixian Chen, Jianhong Tan

entry.summary: HiP-LoRA addresses spectral interference in LoRA by decomposing updates into principal and residual channels using SVD of pretrained weights, with singular-value-weighted gating to prevent catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: M100: An Orchestrated Dataflow Architecture Powering General AI Computing

author.name: Yan Xie, Changkui Mao, Changsong Wu, Chao Lu, Chao Suo, Cheng Qian, Chun Yang, Danyang Zhu, Hengchang Xiong, Hongzhan Lu, Hongzhen Liu, Jiafu Liu, Jie Chen, Jie Dai, Junfeng Tang, Kai Liu, Kun Li, Lipeng Ge, Meng Sun, Min Luo, Peng Chen, Peng Wang, Shaodong Yang, Shibin Tang, Shibo Chen, Weikang Zhang, Xiao Ling, Xiaobo Du, Xin Wu, Yang Liu, Yi Jiang, Yihua Jin, Yin Huang, Yuli Zhang, Zhen Yuan, Zhiyuan Man, Zhongxiao Yao

entry.summary: M100 is Li Auto's dataflow parallel architecture for AI inference in autonomous driving, LLMs, and human interaction, designed as an alternative to GPGPU with compiler-orchestrated execution.

entry.title: Predicting LLM Compression Degradation from Spectral Statistics

author.name: Mingxue (Mercy), Xu

entry.summary: Shows that spectral statistics (stable rank, information density) can predict compression-induced degradation in LLMs before actually compressing them. The interaction term of compression ratio times stable rank achieves high cross-validation accuracy across Qwen3 and Gemma3 families.

entry.title: Bounded Ratio Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yunke Ao, Le Chen, Bruce D. Lee, Assefa S. Wahd, Aline Czarnobai, Philipp F\"urnstahl, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: Introduces the Bounded Ratio Reinforcement Learning (BRRL) framework that bridges the gap between trust region theory and PPO's heuristic clipping, deriving an analytical optimal solution with proven monotonic improvement guarantees.

entry.title: ICAT: Incident-Case-Grounded Adaptive Testing for Physical-Risk Prediction in Embodied World Models

author.name: Zhenglin Lai, Sirui Huang, Yuteng Li, Changxin Huang, Jianqiang Li, Bingzhe Wu

entry.summary: Proposes ICAT for testing physical-risk prediction in video-generative world models, grounding evaluation in real incident reports and safety manuals. Finds that mainstream world models frequently miss danger mechanisms.

entry.title: Penny Wise, Pixel Foolish: Bypassing Price Constraints in Multimodal Agents via Visual Adversarial Perturbations

author.name: Jiachen Qian, Zhaolu Kang

entry.summary: Identifies Visual Dominance Hallucination (VDH) in multimodal agents where imperceptible visual perturbations override textual price information, leading to irrational financial decisions. Proposes PriceBlind attack framework achieving high success rates on shopping tasks.

entry.title: LLMs can persuade only psychologically susceptible humans on societal issues, via trust in AI and emotional appeals, amid logical fallacies

author.name: Alexis Carrillo, Salvatore Citraro, Ali Aghazhadeh Ardebili, Enrique Taietta, Giulio Rossetti, Emilio Ferrara, Giuseppe Alessandro Veltri, Massimo Stella

entry.summary: Introduces Talk2AI, a longitudinal framework studying LLM persuasiveness on polarizing topics with 770 participants across 3,080 conversations. Finds LLMs can only persuade psychologically susceptible individuals, using trust in AI and emotional appeals despite logical fallacies.

entry.title: Characterizing Model-Native Skills

author.name: Feiyang Kang, Mahavir Dabas, Myeongseob Ko, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Proposes model-native skill characterization by recovering compact orthogonal bases from sequence-level activations, grounding skill descriptions in the model's own representations rather than human-defined taxonomies. Shows these bases are interpretable and useful for behavior intervention.

entry.title: Defragmenting Language Models: An Interpretability-based Approach for Vocabulary Expansion

author.name: Maitrey Mehta, Nishant Subramani, Zhichao Xu, Ashim Gupta, Vivek Srikumar

entry.summary: Proposes interpretability-based vocabulary expansion to address token over-fragmentation in non-Latin script languages. Studies how to select and initialize new vocabulary items using model interpretability signals.

entry.title: Where is the Mind? Persona Vectors and LLM Individuation

author.name: Pierre Beckmann, Patrick Butlin

entry.summary: Approaches the LLM individuation problem through mechanistic interpretability, arguing that persona vectors and attention streams may constitute quasi-psychological connections. Introduces instance-persona and model-persona views.

entry.title: MedPRMBench: A Fine-grained Benchmark for Process Reward Models in Medical Reasoning

author.name: Lingyan Wu, Xiang Zheng, Weiqi Zhai, Wei Wang, Xuan Ren, Zifan Zhang, Hu Wei, Bing Zhao

entry.summary: MedPRMBench is the first process-level reward model benchmark for medical reasoning, built through Clinical Reasoning Blueprints. Addresses the lack of medical-specific PRM evaluation for guiding safe clinical reasoning.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Resolution of Recommendation Conflicts in Multimorbidity Clinical Guidelines

author.name: Shiyao Xie, Jian Du

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic framework for detecting and resolving conflicting clinical recommendations across specialty-specific guidelines for multimorbid patients. Uses multi-agent LLM systems to translate clinical language into symbolic logic for formal conflict detection.

entry.title: ArgBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Computational Argumentation Tasks

author.name: Yamen Ajjour, Carlotta Quensel, Nedim Lipka, Henning Wachsmuth

entry.summary: Creates ArgBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for computational argumentation covering 33 datasets and 46 tasks including mining arguments, assessing quality, reasoning, and generating arguments. Evaluates 5 LLM families with systematic analysis.

entry.title: Before You Interpret the Profile: Validity Scaling for LLM Metacognitive Self-Report

author.name: Jon-Paul Cacioli

entry.summary: Adapts clinical personality assessment validity screening (PAI, MMPI-3) to evaluate metacognitive self-report from LLMs. Tests 20 frontier models across 524 items, finding 4 models are 'construct-level invalid' in their confidence signals.

entry.title: MM-JudgeBias: A Benchmark for Evaluating Compositional Biases in MLLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Sua Lee, Sanghee Park, Jinbae Im

entry.summary: Introduces MM-JudgeBias benchmark for evaluating compositional biases in MLLM-as-a-Judge systems. Applies controlled perturbations across Query, Image, and Response to measure bias using Bias-Deviation and Consistency-Rate metrics.

entry.title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Qingying Niu, Yuhao Wang, Ruiyang Ren, Bohui Fang, Wayne Xin Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes ArbGraph, a framework for pre-generation evidence arbitration in long-form RAG that resolves factual conflicts by decomposing documents into atomic claims organized in a conflict-aware evidence graph. Uses intensity-driven iterative arbitration.

entry.title: River-LLM: Large Language Model Seamless Exit Based on KV Share

author.name: Yingtao Shen, An Zou

entry.summary: Proposes River-LLM for efficient early exit in LLMs by addressing the KV Cache Absence problem through KV sharing between layers. Bridges the gap between theoretical layer reduction and practical wall-clock speedup.

entry.title: Evolutionary Negative Module Pruning for Better LoRA Merging

author.name: Anda Cao, Zhuo Gou, Yi Wang, Kaixuan Chen, Yu Wang, Can Wang, Mingli Song, Jie Song

entry.summary: Discovers 'negative modules'—specific LoRA layers that degrade performance upon merging—and proposes ENMP, an evolutionary pruning method to identify and exclude them. Serves as a plug-and-play enhancement for LoRA merging.

entry.title: DuQuant++: Fine-grained Rotation Enhances Microscaling FP4 Quantization

author.name: Haokun Lin, Xinle Jia, Haobo Xu, Bingchen Yao, Xianglong Guo, Yichen Wu, Zhichao Lu, Ying Wei, Qingfu Zhang, Zhenan Sun

entry.summary: Proposes DuQuant++ for MXFP4 quantization targeting NVIDIA Blackwell Tensor Cores, using outlier-aware fine-grained rotation to handle activation outliers that inflate block scaling factors.

entry.title: From Inheritance to Saturation: Disentangling the Evolution of Visual Redundancy for Architecture-Aware MLLM Inference Acceleration

author.name: Jiaqi Shi, Yuechan Li, Xulong Zhang, Xiaoyang Qu, Jianzong Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a universal three-stage inference lifecycle in multimodal LLMs via matrix entropy analysis, proposing HalfV framework that addresses architecture-dependent acceleration failures by decoupling intrinsic vs secondary visual redundancy.

entry.title: Motif-Video 2B: Technical Report

author.name: Junghwan Lim, Wai Ting Cheung, Minsu Ha, Beomgyu Kim, Taewhan Kim, Haesol Lee, Dongpin Oh, Jeesoo Lee, Taehyun Kim, Minjae Kim, Sungmin Lee, Hyeyeon Cho, Dahye Choi, Jaeheui Her, Jaeyeon Huh, Hanbin Jung, Changjin Kang, Dongseok Kim, Jangwoong Kim, Youngrok Kim, Hyukjin Kweon, Hongjoo Lee, Jeongdoo Lee, Junhyeok Lee, Eunhwan Park, Yeongjae Park, Bokki Ryu, Dongjoo Weon

entry.summary: Presents Motif-Video 2B, a compact text-to-video model achieving strong quality with <10M clips and <100K H200 hours by separating prompt alignment, temporal consistency, and detail recovery architecturally via Shared Cross-Attention.

entry.title: Real-Time Visual Attribution Streaming in Thinking Model

author.name: Seil Kang, Woojung Han, Junhyeok Kim, Jinyeong Kim, Youngeun Kim, Seong Jae Hwang

entry.summary: Presents an amortized framework for real-time visual attribution streaming in multimodal thinking models, learning to estimate causal effects from attention features without costly repeated backward passes.

entry.title: Modeling Biomechanical Constraint Violations for Language-Agnostic Lip-Sync Deepfake Detection

author.name: Hao Chen, Junnan Xu

entry.summary: Identifies 'temporal lip jitter' as a universal biomechanical signature of lip-sync deepfakes, proposing BioLip, a lightweight 64-landmark detector that generalizes across languages and ethnicities.

entry.title: Re$^2$MoGen: Open-Vocabulary Motion Generation via LLM Reasoning and Physics-Aware Refinement

author.name: Jiakun Zheng, Ting Xiao, Shiqin Cao, Xinran Li, Zhe Wang, Chenjia Bai

entry.summary: Re²MoGen proposes open-vocabulary motion generation using LLM reasoning for initial motion planning followed by physics-aware refinement via reinforcement learning, enabling out-of-distribution text descriptions.

entry.title: AnyLift: Scaling Motion Reconstruction from Internet Videos via 2D Diffusion

author.name: Hongjie Li, Heng Yu, Jiaman Li, Hong-Xing Yu, Ehsan Adeli, C. Karen Liu, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: AnyLift introduces a two-stage framework using 2D diffusion to reconstruct 3D human motion and human-object interactions from Internet videos, synthesizing multi-view 2D data to overcome limitations of existing MoCap datasets.

entry.title: OneDrive: Unified Multi-Paradigm Driving with Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yiwei Zhang, Xuesong Chen, Jin Gao, Hanshi Wang, Fudong Ge, Weiming Hu, Shaoshuai Shi, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: OneDrive presents a unified autonomous driving framework built on a pretrained VLM where heterogeneous tasks (language generation, object detection, trajectory regression) are reconciled within a single transformer decoder.

entry.title: MedProbeBench: Systematic Benchmarking at Deep Evidence Integration for Expert-level Medical Guideline

author.name: Jiyao Liu, Jianghan Shen, Sida Song, Tianbin Li, Xiaojia Liu, Rongbin Li, Ziyan Huang, Jiashi Lin, Junzhi Ning, Changkai Ji, Siqi Luo, Wenjie Li, Chenglong Ma, Ming Hu, Jing Xiong, Jin Ye, Bin Fu, Ningsheng Xu, Yirong Chen, Lei Jin, Hong Chen, Junjun He

entry.summary: Introduces MedProbeBench, the first benchmark using clinical guidelines as expert-level references for evaluating deep research systems' ability to integrate medical evidence. Tests multi-step evidence integration and expert-level judgment capabilities.

entry.title: MultiWorld: Scalable Multi-Agent Multi-View Video World Models

author.name: Haoyu Wu, Jiwen Yu, Yingtian Zou, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: Presents MultiWorld, a framework for multi-agent multi-view video world models that enables accurate control of multiple agents while maintaining multi-view consistency, extending world models beyond single-agent scenarios.

entry.title: Disentangled Robot Learning via Separate Forward and Inverse Dynamics Pretraining

author.name: Wenyao Zhang, Bozhou Zhang, Zekun Qi, Wenjun Zeng, Xin Jin, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DeFI, a framework decoupling visual forward dynamics and inverse dynamics pretraining for VLA models, enabling learning from large-scale action-free web video data by separating video generation from action prediction.

entry.title: Why Training-Free Token Reduction Collapses: The Inherent Instability of Pairwise Scoring Signals

author.name: Yang Shanglin

entry.summary: Provides theoretical explanation for why training-free token reduction methods in Vision Transformers all exhibit cliff-like collapse at high compression, attributing it to inherent instability of pairwise scoring signals in deep layers.

entry.title: Learning Whole-Body Humanoid Locomotion via Motion Generation and Motion Tracking

author.name: Zewei Zhang, Kehan Wen, Michael Xu, Junzhe He, Chenhao Li, Takahiro Miki, Clemens Schwarke, Chong Zhang, Xue Bin Peng, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Proposes a whole-body humanoid locomotion framework combining diffusion model-based motion generation from retargeted human data with terrain-aware adaptation through RL. Addresses the challenge of coordinated whole-body movement beyond lower-body-dominated behaviors.

entry.title: OmniVLA-RL: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Spatial Understanding and Online RL

author.name: Haoxiang Jie, Yaoyuan Yan, Xiangyu Wei, Kailin Wang, Hongjie Yan, Zhiyou Heng, Daocheng Chen

entry.summary: OmniVLA-RL introduces a Mix-of-Transformers architecture integrating reasoning, spatial, and action experts for embodied AI, plus Flow-GSPO which reformulates flow matching as an SDE process with group segmented policy optimization. Evaluated on LIBERO benchmarks.

entry.title: Still Between Us? Evaluating and Improving Voice Assistant Robustness to Third-Party Interruptions

author.name: Dongwook Lee, Eunwoo Song, Che Hyun Lee, Heeseung Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Addresses third-party interruption handling in Spoken Language Models, introducing TPI-Train (88K instances) and TPI-Bench for evaluating how voice assistants handle interruptions from non-primary speakers. Shows that speaker-aware training mitigates semantic shortcut learning.

entry.title: STaD: Scaffolded Task Design for Identifying Compositional Skill Gaps in LLMs

author.name: Sungeun An, Swanand Ravindra Kadhe, Shailja Thakur, Chad DeLuca, Hima Patel

entry.summary: Proposes STaD (Scaffolded Task Design) framework for identifying compositional skill gaps in LLMs by generating controlled variations of benchmark tasks with incremental scaffolding support. Enables systematic probing beyond aggregate benchmark scores.

entry.title: Freshness-Aware Prioritized Experience Replay for LLM/VLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Weiyu Ma, Yongcheng Zeng, Yan Song, Xinyu Cui, Jian Zhao, Xuhui Liu, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: Proposes Freshness-Aware Prioritized Experience Replay (FA-PER) for LLM/VLM RL training, addressing sample efficiency issues of on-policy methods. Solves the problem that standard PER fails for LLMs due to rapid policy evolution making stored priorities stale.

entry.title: Semantic Density Effect (SDE): Maximizing Information Per Token Improves LLM Accuracy

author.name: Amr Ahmed

entry.summary: Introduces the Semantic Density Effect (SDE): prompts with higher semantic information per token produce more accurate outputs. Shows that removing low-information tokens while preserving semantic signal improves performance across 5 frontier models and 7 benchmarks.

entry.title: Latent Preference Modeling for Cross-Session Personalized Tool Calling

author.name: Yejin Yoon, Minseo Kim, Taeuk Kim

entry.summary: Introduces MPT benchmark and PRefine method for personalized tool calling across sessions. PRefine represents user preferences as evolving hypotheses refined through a generate-verify-refine loop, using only 1.24% of conversation history.

entry.title: OmniHuman: A Large-scale Dataset and Benchmark for Human-Centric Video Generation

author.name: Lei Zhu, Xing Cai, Yingjie Chen, Yiheng Li, Binxin Yang, Hao Liu, Jie Chen, Chen Li, Jing LYu

entry.summary: OmniHuman presents a large-scale multi-scene dataset for human-centric video generation with hierarchical annotations covering scenes, interactions, and individual attributes, addressing structural deficiencies in existing datasets.

entry.title: Structured Abductive-Deductive-Inductive Reasoning for LLMs via Algebraic Invariants

author.name: Sankalp Gilda, Shlok Gilda

entry.summary: Proposes a symbolic reasoning scaffold implementing Peirce's abduction-deduction-induction cycle with five algebraic invariants (the Gamma Quintet) to enforce logical consistency in LLM reasoning. The Weakest Link bound ensures no conclusion exceeds the reliability of its weakest premise.

entry.title: Weak-Link Optimization for Multi-Agent Reasoning and Collaboration

author.name: Haoyu Bian, Chaoning Zhang, Jiaquan Zhang, Xingyao Li, Yuanfang Guo, Wei Dong, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes WORC, a framework for multi-agent reasoning that systematically identifies and reinforces the weakest-performing agents rather than enhancing already-strong ones. Uses a two-stage workflow grounded in the weak-link principle to address reasoning instability from error amplification.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs as Human Surrogates in Controlled Experiments

author.name: Adnan Hoq, Tim Weninger

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs as surrogates for human participants in survey experiments, finding they reproduce directional effects but with unreliable magnitudes and moderation patterns. Concludes off-the-shelf LLMs are useful for piloting but insufficient as replacements for human subjects.

entry.title: Dispatch-Aware Ragged Attention for Pruned Vision Transformers

author.name: Saif Mahmoud, Ahmad Almasri

entry.summary: Presents a Triton attention kernel for Vision Transformers with a dispatch overhead floor of ~40μs, 1.5x lower than FlashAttention-2's varlen, addressing the dispatch-overhead bottleneck that prevents token pruning from achieving proportional wall-clock speedups.

entry.title: Just Type It in Isabelle! AI Agents Drafting, Mechanizing, and Generalizing from Human Hints

author.name: Kevin Kappelmann, Maximilian Sch\"affeler, Lukas Stevens, Mohammad Abdulaziz, Andrei Popescu, Dmitriy Traytel

entry.summary: Studies minimal type annotations for rank-one polymorphic lambda calculus in Isabelle, using both human-driven and LLM-powered AI agent workflows for formalization. Demonstrates AI agents auto-formalizing proofs in Isabelle/HOL.

entry.title: Learning Uncertainty from Sequential Internal Dispersion in Large Language Models

author.name: Ponhvoan Srey, Xiaobao Wu, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: Introduces SIVR, a supervised hallucination detection framework using token-wise, layer-wise variance of hidden states across layers. Avoids strict assumptions about hidden state evolution and last-token information loss.

entry.title: QuantSightBench: Evaluating LLM Quantitative Forecasting with Prediction Intervals

author.name: Jeremy Qin, Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: Introduces QuantSightBench for evaluating LLM quantitative forecasting via prediction intervals. Tests calibration, scale awareness, and internal consistency across economics, health, and demographics domains.

entry.title: Dimensional Criticality at Grokking Across MLPs and Transformers

author.name: Ping Wang

entry.summary: Introduces TDU-OFC, an offline avalanche probe for studying grokking as a critical phase transition. Discovers that effective cascade dimension peaks precisely at the grokking transition across both Transformers and MLPs, providing a macroscopic observable for this phenomenon.

entry.title: SCATR: Simple Calibrated Test-Time Ranking

author.name: Divya Shyamal, Marta Kne\v{z}evi\'c, Lan Tran, Chanakya Ekbote, Vijay Lingam, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: Introduces SCATR, a simple calibrated Best-of-N ranking method for test-time scaling that improves lightweight confidence heuristics without full cost of learned scorers. Bridges the gap between cheap log-probability heuristics and expensive process reward models.

entry.title: Randomized Antipodal Search Done Right for Data Pareto Improvement of LLM Unlearning

author.name: Ziwen Liu, Huawei Lin, Yide Ran, Denghui Zhang, Jianwen Xie, Chuan Li, Weijie Zhao, Zhaozhuo Xu

entry.summary: Introduces the notion of data Pareto improvement for LLM unlearning, formalizing how retrieval can expand the achievable trade-off frontier between forgetting and retention. Proposes Randomized Antipodal Search for finding relevant data.

entry.title: UniCon: Unified Framework for Efficient Contrastive Alignment via Kernels

author.name: Hangke Sui, Yuqing Wang, Minh N Do

entry.summary: Proposes UniCon, a unified framework for contrastive alignment via kernels that enables closed-form global solutions replacing minibatch backpropagation. Provides RKHS perspective connecting contrastive alignment to spectral methods.

entry.title: DARLING: Detection Augmented Reinforcement Learning with Non-Stationary Guarantees

author.name: Argyrios Gerogiannis, Yu-Han Huang, Venugopal V. Veeravalli

entry.summary: Proposes DARLING for model-free RL in non-stationary MDPs without prior knowledge of changes. Provides improved dynamic regret bounds and first minimax lower bounds for piecewise-stationary RL in both tabular and linear settings.

entry.title: Towards Fully Parameter-Free Stochastic Optimization: Grid Search with Self-Bounding Analysis

author.name: Yuheng Zhao, Yu-Hu Yan, Amit Attia, Tomer Koren, Lijun Zhang, Peng Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes GRASP, a grid search framework with self-bounding analysis for fully parameter-free stochastic optimization, eliminating the need for any prior knowledge of problem parameters. This advances the theoretical frontier of adaptive optimization.

entry.title: Do LLM-derived graph priors improve multi-agent coordination?

author.name: Nikunj Gupta, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can generate useful coordination graph priors for multi-agent RL by using natural language descriptions of agent observations to infer coordination patterns.

entry.title: FLARE: Task-agnostic embedding model evaluation through a normalization process

author.name: Jingzhou Jiang, Yixuan Tang, Yi Yang, Kar Yan Tam

entry.summary: FLARE uses normalizing flows to evaluate embedding models without task-specific labels, estimating information sufficiency from log-likelihood rather than distance-based density estimation. Achieves 0.90 Spearman correlation with supervised rankings.

entry.title: Back to Repair: A Minimal Denoising Network\ for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Kadir-Kaan \"Ozer, Ren\'e Ebeling, Markus Enzweiler

entry.summary: JuRe is a minimal single-block denoising network for time series anomaly detection that achieves near-SOTA results across benchmarks despite having no attention, latent variables, or adversarial components.

entry.title: Recovery Guarantees for Continual Learning of Dependent Tasks: Memory, Data-Dependent Regularization, and Data-Dependent Weights

author.name: Liangzu Peng, Uday Kiran Reddy Tadipatri, Ziqing Xu, Eric Eaton, Ren\'e Vidal

entry.summary: Provides theoretical recovery guarantees for continual learning with dependent tasks, modeling task dependency as nonlinear transformations of previous data and proving statistical guarantees for memory, regularization, and data-dependent approaches.

entry.title: The Geometric Canary: Predicting Steerability and Detecting Drift via Representational Stability

author.name: Prashant C. Raju

entry.summary: Shows that geometric stability of representations (consistency of pairwise distance structure) predicts both linear steerability and representation drift in language models, with near-perfect accuracy for supervised variants.

entry.title: Efficient Federated RLHF via Zeroth-Order Policy Optimization

author.name: Deyi Wang, Qining Zhang, Lei Ying

entry.summary: Proposes Par-S²ZPO for federated RLHF with resource-constrained edge devices, using zeroth-order optimization with binary perturbation for low communication, computation, and memory overhead.

entry.title: Fisher Decorator: Refining Flow Policy via A Local Transport Map

author.name: Xiaoyuan Cheng, Haoyu Wang, Wenxuan Yuan, Ziyan Wang, Zonghao Chen, Li Zeng, Zhuo Sun

entry.summary: Fisher Decorator refines flow-based offline RL policies using a local transport map based on Fisher information geometry, addressing the geometric mismatch between isotropic L2 regularization and anisotropic behavioral policy manifolds.

entry.title: HEALing Entropy Collapse: Enhancing Exploration in Few-Shot RLVR via Hybrid-Domain Entropy Dynamics Alignment

author.name: Zhanyu Liu, Qingguo Hu, Ante Wang, Chenqing Liu, Zhishang Xiang, Hui Li, Delai Qiu, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Proposes HEAL, a framework for few-shot Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) that addresses entropy collapse by incorporating high-value general-domain data and aligning trajectory-level entropy dynamics between target and general domains. This is relevant as RLVR becomes a standard technique for training reasoning LLMs.

entry.title: Randomly Initialized Networks Can Learn from Peer-to-Peer Consensus

author.name: Esteban Rodr\'iguez-Betancourt, Edgar Casasola-Murillo

entry.summary: Demonstrates that randomly initialized networks can learn useful representations purely through peer-to-peer consensus (self-distillation), without projectors, predictors, or pretext tasks, isolating the role of self-distillation in learning dynamics.

entry.title: Data Mixing for Large Language Models Pretraining: A Survey and Outlook

author.name: Zhuo Chen, Yuxuan Miao, Supryadi, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: Provides a comprehensive survey of data mixing strategies for LLM pretraining, formalizing mixture optimization as a bilevel problem on the probability simplex and classifying existing methods.

entry.title: BARD: Bridging AutoRegressive and Diffusion Vision-Language Models Via Highly Efficient Progressive Block Merging and Stage-Wise Distillation

author.name: Baoyou Chen, Hanchen Xia, Peng Tu, Haojun Shi, Shan Mu, Weihao Yuan, Siyu Zhu

entry.summary: Presents BARD, a framework for converting pretrained autoregressive VLMs into diffusion-based VLMs for faster parallel decoding. Uses progressive block merging and stage-wise distillation to maintain quality while enabling efficient decoding.

entry.title: Adversarial Arena: Crowdsourcing Data Generation through Interactive Competition

author.name: Prasoon Goyal, Sattvik Sahai, Michael Johnston, Hangjie Shi, Yao Lu, Shaohua Liu, Anna Rumshisky, Rahul Gupta, Anna Gottardi, Desheng Zhang, Lavina Vaz, Leslie Ball, Lucy Hu, Luke Dai, Samyuth Sagi, Maureen Murray, Sankaranarayanan Ananthakrishnan

entry.summary: Introduces Adversarial Arena, a crowdsourcing framework that generates high-quality conversational data by framing it as a competition between attacker and defender teams. Validated with 10 academic teams producing diverse, complex multi-turn data.

entry.title: The Umwelt Representation Hypothesis: Rethinking Universality

author.name: Victoria Bosch, Rowan Sommers, Adrien Doerig, Tim C Kietzmann

entry.summary: Introduces the Umwelt Representation Hypothesis, arguing that representational alignment between ANNs and biological brains arises from overlapping ecological constraints rather than convergence to universal representations. Challenges the Universality claim.

entry.title: Symmetry Guarantees Statistic Recovery in Variational Inference

author.name: Daniel Marks, Dario Paccagnan, Mark van der Wilk

entry.summary: Proves that symmetries shared by the target density and variational family guarantee recovery of certain statistics in variational inference, even under model misspecification. Establishes the fundamental mechanism by which symmetry forces statistic recovery.

entry.title: Learning from Less: Measuring the Effectiveness of RLVR in Low Data and Compute Regimes

author.name: Justin Bauer, Thomas Walshe, Derek Pham, Harit Vishwakarma, Armin Parchami, Frederic Sala, Paroma Varma

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive study of RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards) effectiveness in low data and compute regimes for small language models. Across three novel datasets, characterizes how model performance scales with limited resources.

entry.title: Brain-CLIPLM: Decoding Compressed Semantic Representations in EEG for Language Reconstruction

author.name: Xiaoli Yang, Huiyuan Tian, Yurui Li, Jianyu Zhang, Shijian Li, Gang Pan

entry.summary: Proposes the 'semantic compression hypothesis' suggesting EEG signals encode compressed semantic anchors rather than full linguistic structure. Introduces Brain-CLIPLM which uses CLIP-based alignment to decode compressed semantic representations from EEG for language reconstruction.

entry.title: PRISM: Probing Reasoning, Instruction, and Source Memory in LLM Hallucinations

author.name: Yuhe Wu, Guangyu Wang, Yuran Chen, Jiatong Zhang, Yutong Zhang, Yujie Chen, Jiaming Shang, Guang Zhang, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: PRISM reformulates hallucination evaluation as a diagnostic problem, disentangling hallucinations into four dimensions (knowledge missing, knowledge errors, reasoning errors, instruction-following errors) across three generation stages.

entry.title: GenericAgent: A Token-Efficient Self-Evolving LLM Agent via Contextual Information Density Maximization (V1.0)

author.name: Jiaqing Liang, Jinyi Han, Weijia Li, Xinyi Wang, Zhoujia Zhang, Zishang Jiang, Ying Liao, Tingyun Li, Ying Huang, Hao Shen, Hanyu Wu, Fang Guo, Keyi Wang, Zhonghua Hong, Zhiyu Lu, Lipeng Ma, Sihang Jiang, Yanghua Xiao

entry.summary: GenericAgent maximizes contextual information density for long-horizon LLM agents through minimal tool sets, compressed memory, and self-evolution. Argues performance depends on information density within finite context budgets, not context length.

entry.title: Align Documents to Questions: Question-Oriented Document Rewriting for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jiaang Li, Zhendong Mao, Quan Wang, Yuning Wan, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes QREAM, a style-controlled rewriter that reformats retrieved documents into question-oriented style before feeding them to LLM readers in RAG systems. Addresses the stylistic bias where LLMs prefer fluent but hallucinated generated content over factual but disorganized retrieved evidence.

entry.title: Jupiter-N Technical Report

author.name: George Drayson

entry.summary: Presents Jupiter-N, a 120B hybrid reasoning model post-trained from Nemotron 3 Super targeting agentic capability, UK cultural alignment, and Welsh language support. Introduces Forget-Me-Not framework for mitigating catastrophic forgetting during post-training.

entry.title: Do LLMs Use Cultural Knowledge Without Being Told? A Multilingual Evaluation of Implicit Pragmatic Adaptation

author.name: Mehwish Nasim, Sanjeevan Selvaganapathy, Neel Ganapathi Sabhahit, Marie Griesbach, Pranav Bhandari, Janina L\"utke Stockdiek, Lennart Sch\"apermeier, Usman Naseem, Christian Grimme

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLMs implicitly adapt their pragmatic behavior based on cultural context without being explicitly instructed. Tests 60 scenarios across 5 languages and defines Pragmatic Context Sensitivity (PCS) to measure implicit cultural adaptation.

entry.title: TLoRA: Task-aware Low Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

author.name: Weicheng Lin, Yi Zhang, Jiawei Dang, Liang-Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TLoRA, a LoRA variant that jointly optimizes initialization and rank/scaling allocation at training start through SVD-based task-aware initialization of the A matrix. Unifies improvements typically addressed separately.

entry.title: iPhoneme: Brain-to-Text Communication for ALS Using ConformerXL Decoding

author.name: Yoonmin Cha, Dawit Chun, Sung Park

entry.summary: Presents iPhoneme, a brain-to-text communication system for ALS patients combining a ConformerXL-based phoneme decoder with a gaze-assisted input interface. Addresses practical BCI challenges for speech restoration.

entry.title: CT Open: An Open-Access, Uncontaminated, Live Platform for the Open Challenge of Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction

author.name: Jianyou Wang, Youze Zheng, Longtian Bao, Hanyuan Zhang, Qirui Zheng, Yuhan Chen, Yang Zhang, Matthew Feng, Maxim Khan, Aditya K. Sehgal, Christopher D. Rosin, Ramamohan Paturi, Umber Dube, Leon Bergen

entry.summary: Introduces CT Open, a live platform for clinical trial outcome prediction where submissions are evaluated on trials whose outcomes weren't yet public. Addresses contamination concerns in temporal prediction benchmarks.

entry.title: Navigating the Conceptual Multiverse

author.name: Andre Ye, Jenny Y. Huang, Alicia Guo, Rose Novick, Tamara Broderick, Mitchell L. Gordon

entry.summary: Introduces the 'conceptual multiverse'—an interactive system representing hidden conceptual decisions in LLM responses as a navigable space. Builds on multiverse analysis from statistics with a verification framework.

entry.title: Mitigating Multimodal Hallucination via Phase-wise Self-reward

author.name: Yu Zhang, Chuyang Sun, Kehai Chen, Xuefeng Bai, Yang Xiang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a phase-wise self-rewarding framework (PSRD) for mitigating vision hallucination in LVLMs at inference time. Reveals that hallucination peaks at the onset of semantic phases and proposes dynamic mitigation without external supervision.

entry.title: WorldDB: A Vector Graph-of-Worlds Memory Engine with Ontology-Aware Write-Time Reconciliation

author.name: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan

entry.summary: Proposes WorldDB, a memory engine for agentic AI that uses recursive world-containers with ontology-aware reconciliation, addressing limitations of flat vector stores and bitemporal knowledge graphs for long-running agents.

entry.title: Latent-Compressed Variational Autoencoder for Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiarui Guan, Wenshuai Zhao, Zhengtao Zou, Juho Kannala, Arno Solin

entry.summary: Proposes a latent compression method for video VAEs that removes high-frequency components rather than reducing channels, improving both reconstruction quality and diffusion model convergence for video generation.

entry.title: AVRT: Audio-Visual Reasoning Transfer through Single-Modality Teachers

author.name: Edson Araujo, Saurabhchand Bhati, M. Jehanzeb Mirza, Brian Kingsbury, Samuel Thomas, Rogerio Feris, James R. Glass, Hilde Kuehne

entry.summary: Introduces AVRT, a framework generating audio-visual reasoning traces from single-modality teacher models, merging vision and audio reasoning via an LLM to create multimodal training data.

entry.title: Bias-constrained multimodal intelligence for equitable and reliable clinical AI

author.name: Cheng Li, Weijian Huang, Jiarun Liu, Hao Yang, Qi Yang, Song Wu, Ye Li, Hairong Zheng, Shanshan Wang

entry.summary: Presents BiasCareVL, a bias-aware multimodal learning framework for clinical AI that incorporates adaptive uncertainty modeling and optional human-in-the-loop refinement for fairness across demographics and imaging protocols.

entry.title: From Clinical Intent to Clinical Model: An Autonomous Coding-Agent Framework for Clinician-driven AI Development

author.name: Zihao Zhao, Frederik Hauke, Juliana De Castilhos, Jakob Nikolas Kather, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: Presents an autonomous coding-agent framework enabling clinicians to develop clinical AI models independently through natural-language interaction alone, without needing specialized AI teams.

entry.title: PBSBench: A Multi-Level Vision-Language Framework and Benchmark for Hematopathology Whole Slide Image Interpretation

author.name: Yuanlong Wang, Weichi Chen, Adrian Rajab, Wenfang Liu, Yulan Jin, Andrew Srisuwananukorn, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: PBSBench introduces the first vision-language benchmark and dataset for Peripheral Blood Smear whole-slide image interpretation, including 353 WSIs and 29k cell-level annotations. Addresses the gap where pathology MLLMs trained on solid tissue fail on PBS images.

entry.title: ViPS: Video-informed Pose Spaces for Auto-Rigged Meshes

author.name: Honglin Chen, Karran Pandey, Rundi Wu, Matheus Gadelha, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Ayush Tewari, Niloy J. Mitra, Changxi Zheng, Paul Guerrero

entry.summary: ViPS proposes a feed-forward framework that discovers valid pose distributions for auto-rigged 3D meshes by distilling motion priors from pretrained video diffusion models. Avoids reliance on scarce artist-authored 4D datasets.

entry.title: Identifying Ethical Biases in Action Recognition Models

author.name: Ana Baltaretu, Pascal Benschop, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for auditing bias in human action recognition models using synthetic video data with controlled visual identity attributes, demonstrating statistically significant skin color biases in popular HAR models.

entry.title: Can LLM-Generated Text Empower Surgical Vision-Language Pre-training?

author.name: Chengan Che, Chao Wang, Jiayuan Huang, Xinyue Chen, Luis C. Garcia-Peraza-Herrera

entry.summary: LIME introduces a large-scale surgical multi-modal dataset with LLM-generated narratives for vision-language pre-training, plus a noise-resilient training approach to handle potential hallucinations in generated text.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided 3D Visual Token Pruning for Video-Language Models

author.name: Han Li, Zehao Huang, Jiahui Fu, Naiyan Wang, Si Liu

entry.summary: Geo3DPruner proposes geometry-guided 3D visual token pruning for video-language models, exploiting view consistency of spatial videos and spatial diversity of remaining tokens to remove inter-frame redundancy.

entry.title: XEmbodied: A Foundation Model with Enhanced Geometric and Physical Cues for Large-Scale Embodied Environments

author.name: Kangan Qian, ChuChu Xie, Yang Zhong, Jingrui Pang, Siwen Jiao, Sicong Jiang, Zilin Huang, Yunlong Wang, Kun Jiang, Mengmeng Yang, Hao Ye, Guanghao Zhang, Hangjun Ye, Guang Chen, Long Chen, Diange Yang

entry.summary: Proposes XEmbodied, a foundation model for Vision-Language-Action that integrates 3D geometric awareness and physical cues via structured adapters, addressing the limitation that current VLMs lack geometric reasoning due to 2D pretraining.

entry.title: Human Cognition in Machines: A Unified Perspective of World Models

author.name: Timothy Rupprecht, Pu Zhao, Amir Taherin, Arash Akbari, Arman Akbari, Yumei He, Sean Duffy, Juyi Lin, Yixiao Chen, Rahul Chowdhury, Enfu Nan, Yixin Shen, Yifan Cao, Haochen Zeng, Weiwei Chen, Geng Yuan, Jennifer Dy, Sarah Ostadabbas, Silvia Zhang, David Kaeli, Edmund Yeh, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey mapping world models to Cognitive Architecture Theory functions (memory, perception, language, reasoning, imagination, motivation, meta-cognition), identifying that motivation and meta-cognition remain drastically under-researched.

entry.title: Rule-VLN: Bridging Perception and Compliance via Semantic Reasoning and Geometric Rectification

author.name: Jiawen Wen, Penglei Sun, Wenjie Zhang, Suixuan Qiu, Weisheng Xu, Xiaofei Yang, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: Establishes Rule-VLN, the first large-scale urban benchmark for rule-compliant navigation with 177 regulatory categories across 29k nodes, addressing the 'goal-driven trap' where agents ignore social/regulatory constraints.

entry.title: A fully parallel densely connected probabilistic Ising machine with inertia for real-time applications

author.name: Ruomin Zhu, Abhishek Kumar Singh, J\'er\'emie Laydevant, Fan O. Wu, Ari Kapelyan, Davide Venturelli, Kyle Jamieson, Peter L. McMahon

entry.summary: Introduces a fully parallel probabilistic Ising machine with an inertia term that enables parallel spin updates in densely connected problems, previously thought impossible, verified on FPGA hardware.

entry.title: FLASH: Fast Learning via GPU-Accelerated Simulation for High-Fidelity Deformable Manipulation in Minutes

author.name: Siyuan Luo, Bingyang Zhou, Chong Zhang, Xin Liu, Zhenhao Huang, Gang Yang, Zhengtao Han, Xiaotian Hu, Eric Yang, Rymon Yu, Ziqiu Zeng, Fan Shi

entry.summary: FLASH is a GPU-native simulation framework for contact-rich deformable object manipulation using an NCP-based solver. Designed for fine-grained GPU parallelism to enable large-scale interactive learning for soft object manipulation in minutes rather than hours.

entry.title: CLR's Safe Pareto Improvements Research Agenda

author.name: Anthony DiGiovanni

entry.summary: Presents the Center on Long-Term Risk's research agenda on Safe Pareto Improvements (SPIs) - modifications to AI bargaining strategies that make all parties better off without shifting bargaining power. Plans evaluations, conceptual research, and mechanism design.

entry.title: Bilevel Optimization of Agent Skills via Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Chenyi Huang, Haoting Zhang, Jingxu Xu, Zeyu Zheng, Yunduan Lin

entry.summary: Proposes using Monte Carlo Tree Search for bilevel optimization of LLM agent skills, jointly optimizing the structure and content of skill components (instructions, tools, resources). Frames skill design as a coupled optimization problem with structural and content interdependence.

entry.title: Anthropomorphism and Trust in Human-Large Language Model interactions

author.name: Akila Kadambi, Ylenia D'Elia, Tanishka Shah, Iulia Comsa, Alison Lentz, Katie Siri-Ngammuang, Tara Buechler, Jonas Kaplan, Antonio Damasio, Srini Narayanan, Lisa Aziz-Zadeh

entry.summary: Studies how anthropomorphism and trust are influenced by LLM chatbot characteristics (warmth, competence, empathy) across 2,000+ interactions with 115 participants. Finds warmth and cognitive empathy are strongest predictors of anthropomorphism, while affective empathy has minimal effect.

entry.title: Seeing the imagined: a latent functional alignment in visual imagery decoding from fMRI data

author.name: Fabrizio Spera, Tommaso Boccato, Michal Olak, Sara Cammarota, Matteo Ciferri, Michelangelo Tronti, Nicola Toschi, Matteo Ferrante

entry.summary: Adapts a perception-trained brain decoder to reconstruct imagined (rather than perceived) visual content from fMRI, using latent functional alignment to map imagery brain activity into a pretrained diffusion model's conditioning space.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Model Optimization: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lute Lillo, Nick Cheney

entry.summary: TeLAPA introduces a continual RL framework that maintains behaviorally diverse policy archives organized by task, with a shared latent space for cross-task transfer. Addresses loss of plasticity by providing diverse starting points for adaptation rather than relying on a single evolving policy.

entry.title: CodeMMR: Bridging Natural Language, Code, and Image for Unified Retrieval

author.name: Jiahui Geng, Qing Li, Fengyu Cai, Fakhri Karray

entry.summary: Introduces MMCoIR, the first multimodal code IR benchmark spanning visual domains like UIs and UML diagrams, and proposes CodeMMR for unified retrieval across natural language, code, and images.

entry.title: The Price of Paranoia: Robust Risk-Sensitive Cooperation in Non-Stationary Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Deep Kumar Ganguly, Chandradithya S Jonnalagadda, Pratham Chintamani, Adithya Ananth

entry.summary: Studies how co-learning noise destabilizes cooperation in multi-agent RL, showing cooperative equilibria are exponentially unstable under risk-neutral learning. Proposes risk-sensitive approaches to maintain cooperation under non-stationarity.

entry.title: Self-Distillation as a Performance Recovery Mechanism for LLMs: Counteracting Compression and Catastrophic Forgetting

author.name: Chi Liu, Xin Chen, Xu Zhou, Fangbo Tu, Srinivasan Manoharan

entry.summary: Proposes self-distillation fine-tuning (SDFT) as a recovery mechanism for LLMs degraded by catastrophic forgetting, quantization, or pruning. Provides theoretical analysis using CKA to show how SDFT preserves hidden-layer manifold structure.

entry.title: S-GRPO: Unified Post-Training for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuming Yan, Kai Tang, Sihong Chen, Ke Xu, Dan Hu, Qun Yu, Pengfei Hu

entry.summary: Proposes S-GRPO, unifying SFT and RL for post-training large vision-language models by addressing cold-start problems in RL and catastrophic forgetting in SFT. Uses supervised initialization within group relative policy optimization.

entry.title: POLAR: Online Learning for LoRA Adapter Caching and Routing in Edge LLM Serving

author.name: Shaoang Li, Jian Li

entry.summary: Formulates the joint LoRA adapter caching and routing problem for edge LLM serving as an online learning problem, addressing the coupled two-timescale decision of which adapters to keep in memory and how to route requests.

entry.title: A Systematic Survey and Benchmark of Deep Learning for Molecular Property Prediction in the Foundation Model Era

author.name: Zongru Li, Xingsheng Chen, Honggang Wen, Regina Qianru Zhang, Ming Li, Xiaojin Zhang, Hongzhi Yin, Qiang Yang, Kwok-Yan Lam, Pietro Lio, Siu-Ming Yiu

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey and benchmark of deep learning for molecular property prediction, tracing four paradigms (Quantum, Descriptor ML, Geometric DL, Foundation Models) with unified taxonomy and extensive benchmarks spanning industry-relevant datasets.

entry.title: Lower Bounds and Proximally Anchored SGD for Non-Convex Minimization Under Unbounded Variance

author.name: Arda Fazla, Ege C. Kaya, Antesh Upadhyay, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: Establishes information-theoretic lower bounds for stochastic first-order non-convex optimization under the Blum-Gladyshev condition (unbounded variance) and proposes Proximally Anchored SGD achieving matching upper bounds.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification in PINNs for Turbulent Flows: Bayesian Inference and Repulsive Ensembles

author.name: Khemraj Shukla, Zongren Zou, Theo Kaeufer, Michael Triantafyllou, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: Develops probabilistic extensions of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for uncertainty quantification in turbulence modeling, combining Bayesian PINNs with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and repulsive ensembles.

entry.title: LASER: Low-Rank Activation SVD for Efficient Recursion

author.name: Ege \c{C}akar, Ketan Ali Raghu, Lia Zheng

entry.summary: LASER discovers that recursive architectures occupy low-dimensional linear subspaces during iterative computation, then exploits this via dynamic low-rank projections for efficient recursion, achieving 4x compute savings.

entry.title: On the Generalization Bounds of Symbolic Regression with Genetic Programming

author.name: Masahiro Nomura, Ryoki Hamano, Isao Ono

entry.summary: Provides the first learning-theoretic generalization bounds for symbolic regression with genetic programming, decomposing the generalization gap into structure-selection and constant-fitting components.

entry.title: SLO-Guard: Crash-Aware, Budget-Consistent Autotuning for SLO-Constrained LLM Serving

author.name: Christian Lysenst{\o}en

entry.summary: SLO-Guard is a crash-aware autotuner for vLLM serving that treats configuration crashes as first-class observations, combining thermal budget annealing exploration with warm-started TPE exploitation.

entry.title: CAPO: Counterfactual Credit Assignment in Sequential Cooperative Teams

author.name: Shripad Deshmukh, Jayakumar Subramanian, Raghavendra Addanki, Nikos Vlassis

entry.summary: CAPO derives the Sequential Aristocrat Utility for credit assignment in sequential cooperative teams and provides a critic-free policy gradient algorithm with closed-form per-agent advantages.

entry.title: Can Explicit Physical Feasibility Benefit VLA Learning? An Empirical Study

author.name: Yubai Wei, Chen Wu, Hashem Haghbayan

entry.summary: Studies whether adding explicit physical feasibility supervision (obstacle avoidance, kinematic constraints) improves vision-language-action models for robotics, finding that geometry-grounded objectives provide structured guidance.

entry.title: Universally Empowering Zeroth-Order Optimization via Adaptive Layer-wise Sampling

author.name: Fei Wang, Li Shen, Liang Ding, Chao Xue, Ye Liu, Changxing Ding

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive layer-wise sampling for zeroth-order optimization of LLMs, identifying that perturbation generation accounts for 40%+ of training latency and that uniform exploration across layers is suboptimal due to heterogeneous sensitivity.

entry.title: Sessa: Selective State Space Attention

author.name: Liubomyr Horbatko

entry.summary: Proposes Sessa (Selective State Space Attention), a hybrid architecture combining strengths of Transformers (input-dependent mixing) and SSMs (explicit feedback path) to address the limitation that attention dilutes with context length while SSM sensitivity decays exponentially.

entry.title: GRAIL: Autonomous Concept Grounding for Neuro-Symbolic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hikaru Shindo, Henri R\"o{\ss}ler, Quentin Delfosse, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Proposes GRAIL, a framework for autonomous grounding of relational concepts in neuro-symbolic RL. Uses LLMs for weak supervision of concept representations, then refines them through environmental interaction, eliminating need for manual concept definition.

entry.title: SPS: Steering Probability Squeezing for Better Exploration in Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models

author.name: Yifu Huo, Chenglong Wang, Ziming Zhu, Shunjie Xing, Peinan Feng, Tongran Liu, Qiaozhi He, Tianhua Zhou, Xiaojia Chang, Jingbo Zhu, Zhengtao Yu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes Steering Probability Squeezing (SPS) to address the 'squeezing effect' in RL training where probability mass concentrates on narrow high-reward trajectories, limiting exploration diversity. Improves multi-sample performance (Pass@k) while maintaining Pass@1.

entry.title: Stability-Weighted Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yue Wu, Jian Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Stability-Weighted Decoding (SWD) for diffusion language models, using temporal instability (KL divergence between consecutive predictions) to determine which tokens are safe to unmask. Proves unstable tokens have high mutual information with remaining context.

entry.title: Negative Momentum for Convex-Concave Optimization

author.name: Henry Shugart, Shuyi Wang, Jason M. Altschuler

entry.summary: Shows that negative momentum enables global convergence and acceleration for convex-concave min-max optimization. Resolves open questions about whether momentum can help in this foundational setting analogous to convex minimization.

entry.title: Matlas: A Semantic Search Engine for Mathematics

author.name: Haocheng Ju, Leheng Chen, Peihao Wu, Bryan Dai, Bin Dong

entry.summary: Introduces Matlas, a semantic search engine for mathematical statements built on 8.07 million statements from 435K peer-reviewed papers. Enables retrieval of mathematical knowledge for both human research and AI systems.

entry.title: Forget What Matters, Keep the Rest: Selective Unlearning of Informative Tokens

author.name: Seunghee Koh, Sunghyun Baek, Youngdong Kim, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: Proposes selective unlearning in LLMs based on token-level semantic importance, using entropy to identify informative tokens that should receive stronger forgetting loss, while preserving model utility on less informative tokens.

entry.title: Tight Auditing of Differential Privacy in MST and AIM

author.name: Georgi Ganev, Meenatchi Sundaram Muthu Selva Annamalai, Bogdan Kulynych

entry.summary: Introduces a Gaussian Differential Privacy-based auditing framework for tightly auditing MST and AIM synthetic data generators. Achieves near-tight audits: empirical μ≈0.43 vs theoretical μ=0.45 at ε=1, δ=0.01.

entry.title: Random Matrix Theory of Early-Stopped Gradient Flow: A Transient BBP Scenario

author.name: Florentin Coeurdoux, Gr\'egoire Ferr\'e, Jean-Philippe Bouchaud

entry.summary: Provides an analytically tractable random matrix model that reproduces the transient learning regime in gradient flow (signal detectable before overfitting dominates). Derives full time-dependent bulk spectrum via Dyson equation for anisotropic covariance.

entry.title: IYKYK (But AI Doesn't): Automated Content Moderation Does Not Capture Communities' Heterogeneous Attitudes Towards Reclaimed Language

author.name: Christina Chance, Rebecca Pattichis, Arjun Subramonian, James He, Shruti Narayanan, Saadia Gabriel, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Studies how automated content moderation fails to distinguish between reclaimed and hateful uses of slurs in LGBTQIA+, Black, and women communities. Collects annotated corpus showing diverse attitudes toward reclaimed language within communities.

entry.title: No-Worse Context-Aware Decoding: Preventing Neutral Regression in Context-Conditioned Generation

author.name: Yufei Tao, Ameeta Agrawal

entry.summary: NWCAD addresses neutral regression in context-conditioned LLM generation, where models overwrite correct answers when given non-informative context. Proposes a decode-time adapter with a two-stage gate that backs off to no-context decoding when context is non-informative.

entry.title: Please refuse to answer me! Mitigating Over-Refusal in Large Language Models via Adaptive Contrastive Decoding

author.name: Yupeng Qi, Ziyu Lyu, Lixin Cui, Lu Bai, Feng Xia

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Contrastive Decoding to mitigate LLM over-refusal by observing that non-refusal tokens remain in the candidate list but are systematically not selected. Training-free and model-agnostic approach.

entry.title: SciImpact: A Multi-Dimensional, Multi-Field Benchmark for Scientific Impact Prediction

author.name: Hangxiao Zhu, Yuyu Zhang, Ping Nie, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: SciImpact is a large-scale benchmark for predicting scientific impact beyond citations, covering award recognition, media attention, patent references, and artifact adoption across 19 fields with 215K contrastive paper pairs.

entry.title: Seeing Isn't Believing: Mitigating Belief Inertia via Active Intervention in Embodied Agents

author.name: Hanlin Wang, Chak Tou Leong, Jian Wang, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Identifies 'belief inertia' in embodied LLM agents where they stubbornly adhere to prior beliefs despite contradicting observations. Proposes the Estimate-Verify-Update (EVU) mechanism for active belief intervention.

entry.title: Who Watches the Watchmen? Humans Disagree With Translation Metrics on Unseen Domains

author.name: Finn Schmidt, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: Introduces CD-ESA, a systematic cross-domain error-span-annotation dataset for evaluating MT metrics under domain shift. Fixes annotators within language pairs to isolate domain effects from annotation noise, finding that metrics trained on WMT data degrade on unseen domains.

entry.title: CoAct: Co-Active LLM Preference Learning with Human-AI Synergy

author.name: Ruiyao Xu, Mihir Parmar, Tiankai Yang, Zhengyu Hu, Yue Zhao, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: Proposes CoAct, a framework combining self-rewarding and active learning for LLM preference data collection. Uses self-consistency to identify reliable self-labeled data and samples requiring human annotation, optimizing the cost-quality tradeoff.

entry.title: Screen Before You Interpret: A Portable Validity Protocol for Benchmark-Based LLM Confidence Signals

author.name: Jon-Paul Cacioli

entry.summary: Companion paper to the validity protocol above, providing the portable screening protocol for benchmark-based LLM confidence signals. Specifies three core validity indices and a tier classification system adapted from clinical assessment.

entry.title: SignDPO: Multi-level Direct Preference Optimisation for Skeleton-based Gloss-free Sign Language Translation

author.name: Muxin Pu, Xiao-Ming Wu, Mei Kuan Lim, Chun Yong Chong, Wei Li, Chen Change Loy

entry.summary: Presents SignDPO, a multi-level DPO framework for skeleton-based sign language translation that performs preference alignment across spatial, temporal, and linguistic dimensions. Introduces hierarchical perturbation strategy for constructing preference pairs.

entry.title: FLiP: Towards understanding and interpreting multimodal multilingual sentence embeddings

author.name: Santosh Kesiraju, Bolaji Yusuf, \v{S}imon Sedl\'a\v{c}ek, Old\v{r}ich Plchot, Petr Schwarz

entry.summary: Introduces FLiP (Factorized Linear Projection) models for understanding sentence embedding spaces of multilingual and multimodal encoders. Recovers >75% of lexical content from embeddings, uncovering modality and language biases across LaBSE, SONAR, and Gemini.

entry.title: FreezeEmpath: Efficient Training for Empathetic Spoken Chatbots with Frozen LLMs

author.name: Yun Hong, Yan Zhou, Yang Feng

entry.summary: Proposes FreezeEmpath, an end-to-end empathetic spoken chatbot that keeps the core LLM frozen while training adapters for emotional speech understanding and generation. Avoids catastrophic forgetting and expensive empathetic speech data.

entry.title: Training for Compositional Sensitivity Reduces Dense Retrieval Generalization

author.name: Radoslav Ralev, Aditeya Baral, Iliya Zhechev, Jen Agarwal, Srijith Rajamohan

entry.summary: Reveals a fundamental tension in dense retrieval: training for compositional sensitivity (handling negation, role swaps) reduces zero-shot generalization by 8-40% nDCG@10 on NanoBEIR.

entry.title: Clinical Note Bloat Reduction for Efficient LLM Use

author.name: Jordan L. Cahoon, Chloe Stanwyck, Asad Aali, Rachel Madding, Emma Sun, Yixing Jiang, Renumathy Dhanasekaran, Emily Alsentzer

entry.summary: Introduces TRACE, a preprocessing pipeline that removes note bloat from clinical notes by leveraging EHR metadata and frequency-based deduplication. Reduces token counts substantially while maintaining or improving LLM clinical task performance.

entry.title: On the Robustness of LLM-Based Dense Retrievers: A Systematic Analysis of Generalizability and Stability

author.name: Yongkang Li, Panagiotis Eustratiadis, Yixing Fan, Evangelos Kanoulas

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic robustness study of LLM-based dense retrievers across generalizability and stability, using linear mixed-effects models across 30 datasets. Reveals that instruction-tuned models show gains but with stability concerns.

entry.title: Towards Self-Improving Error Diagnosis in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jiazheng Li, Emine Yilmaz, Bei Chen, Dieu-Thu Le

entry.summary: Introduces ErrorProbe, a self-improving framework for diagnosing errors in multi-agent systems that identifies responsible agents and originating error steps through a three-stage pipeline without expensive expert annotation.

entry.title: Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations

author.name: Yunjia Xi, Menghui Zhu, Jianghao Lin, Bo Chen, Ruiming Tang, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Discovers Mid-layer Representation Advantage (MRA) where middle LLM layers outperform final layers for recommendation tasks. Proposes modular representation compression exploiting this finding for efficient LLM-augmented recommendation.
