entry.summary: Proposes PATH-FORMER using graph transformers with learnable gene embeddings to construct pathway representations for cancer prognosis, improving on approaches that use raw molecular inputs or simple aggregations.

entry.title: Semantic-based Distributed Learning for Diverse and Discriminative Representations

author.name: Zhuojun Tian, Chaouki Ben Issaid, Mehdi Bennis

entry.summary: Proposes a distributed learning framework ensuring diverse and discriminative representations by reformulating global optimization with mutual information constraints for both i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. data settings.

entry.title: Forecasting Ionospheric Irregularities on GNSS Lines of Sight Using Dynamic Graphs with Ephemeris Conditioning

author.name: Mert Can Turkmen, Eng Leong Tan, Yee Hui Lee

entry.summary: Models the ionosphere as a dynamic graph over pierce points for GNSS forecasting, introducing ephemeris conditioning to exploit predictable satellite trajectories for forecasting on future lines of sight.

entry.title: Fuzzy Encoding-Decoding to Improve Spiking Q-Learning Performance in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Aref Ghoreishee, Abhishek Mishra, Lifeng Zhou, John Walsh, Anup Das, Nagarajan Kandasamy

entry.summary: Develops a fuzzy encoder-decoder architecture for spiking Q-networks in autonomous driving, addressing information loss in spike conversion and limited Q-value discrimination in spiking networks.

entry.title: FM-CAC: Carbon-Aware Control for Battery-Buffered Edge AI via Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Kang Yang, Walid A. Hanafy, Prashant Shenoy, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: Proposes FM-CAC, a carbon-aware control framework for edge AI that uses batteries as temporal buffers and time series foundation models to optimize energy consumption and reduce carbon emissions. Jointly optimizes software pipeline variants, hardware operating points, and battery actions.

entry.title: SynthPID: P&ID digitization from Topology-Preserving Synthetic Data

author.name: Suraj Prasad, Pinak Mahapatra

entry.summary: Introduces SynthPID for digitizing piping and instrumentation diagrams using topology-preserving synthetic data generation. Addresses the severe data scarcity (only 12 public annotated images) by generating structurally realistic synthetic process plant diagrams.

entry.title: FairNVT: Improving Fairness via Noise Injection in Vision Transformers

author.name: Qiaoyue Tang, Sepidehsadat Hosseini, Mengyao Zhai, Thibaut Durand, Greg Mori

entry.title: SPaRSe-TIME: Saliency-Projected Low-Rank Temporal Modeling for Efficient and Interpretable Time Series Prediction

author.name: K. A. Shahriar

entry.summary: Presents SPaRSe-TIME, a time series forecasting framework that decomposes temporal modeling into saliency, memory, and trend components using projection onto informative subspaces. Aims to reduce computation by focusing on sparse informative patterns rather than processing all time steps uniformly.

entry.title: Scaling Human-AI Coding Collaboration Requires a Governable Consensus Layer

entry.title: A Sugeno Integral View of Binarized Neural Network Inference

author.name: Isma\"il Baaj, Henri Prade

entry.title: Domain-Specialized Object Detection via Model-Level Mixtures of Experts

author.name: Svetlana Pavlitska, Malte St\"uven, Beyza Keskin, J. Marius Z\"ollner

entry.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation

entry.title: Revisiting Active Sequential Prediction-Powered Mean Estimation

author.name: Maria-Eleni Sfyraki, Jun-Kun Wang

entry.summary: Revisits active sequential prediction-powered mean estimation where ground-truth labels are queried probabilistically, and ML predictions fill in otherwise. Finds that the simplest approach (constant query probability) often achieves the smallest confidence width, simplifying the method.

entry.title: Mira-Embeddings-V1: Domain-Adapted Semantic Reranking for Recruitment via LLM-Synthesized Data

author.name: Zhaohua Liang, Zhilin Wang, Renjie Cao, Yining Zhang

entry.title: On the Importance and Evaluation of Narrativity in Natural Language AI Explanations

author.name: Mateusz Cedro, David Martens

entry.title: RoMathExam: A Longitudinal Dataset of Romanian Math Exams (1895-2025) with a Seven-Decade Core (1957-2025)

author.name: Rahul Mehta, Kavin R V, Indrajit Pal, Tushar Abhishek, Pawan Goyal, Manish Gupta

entry.title: Amortized Inverse Kinematics via Graph Attention for Real-Time Human Avatar Animation

author.name: Chen Yang

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Dose PET Denoising: Mitigating Averaging Effects via Residual Noise Learning

author.name: Yichao Liu, Zongru Shao, Yueyang Teng, Junwen Guo

author.name: Andrei Dumitriu, Aakash Ralhan, Florin Miron, Florin Tatui, Radu Tudor Ionescu, Radu Timofte, Abdullah Naeem, Anav Katwal, Ayon Dey, Md Tamjidul Hoque, Asuka Shin, Hiroto Shirono, Kosuke Shigematsu, Gaurav Mahesh, Anjana Nanditha, Jiji CV, Akbarali Vakhitov, Sang-Chul Lee, Xinger Li, Chun'an Yu, Junhao Chen, Yang Yang, Gundluri Yuvateja Reddy, Harshitha Palaram, Gejalakshmi N, Jeevitha S, Jiachen Tu, Guoyi Xu, Yaoxin Jiang, Jiajia Liu, Yaokun Shi, Amitabh Tripathi, Modugumudi Mahesh, Santosh Kumar Vipparthi, Subrahmanyam Murala

entry.title: Research Summary: April 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
A major model release and a wave of safety-critical findings dominate today's research landscape.

  • Qwen3.5-Omni sets new SOTA across 215 benchmarks as a hundred-billion-parameter omni-modal model with 256k context and 100M+ hours of audio-visual training data
  • π₀.₇ from Physical Intelligence demonstrates a steerable generalist robotic foundation model with emergent cross-task transfer capabilities
  • MatRIS-MoE breaks the billion-parameter barrier for universal machine learning interatomic potentials via a distributed training framework called Janus

AI safety research is exceptionally strong today. ASMR-Bench tests whether auditors can detect subtle sabotage in ML codebases. Subliminal unsafe behavior transfer through model distillation reveals a novel attack surface for agentic systems. GRIFT uses gradient fingerprints to detect and suppress reward hacking in RL-trained reasoning models. LinuxArena provides the largest control setting (1,671 tasks) for evaluating agent safety in live production environments.

  • Chain-of-Thought prompting consistently degrades visual spatial reasoning across 17 models and 13 benchmarks, challenging universal CoT assumptions
  • DELEGATE-52 shows even frontier models (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude 4.6 Opus, GPT 5.4) corrupt 25% of document content during long delegated editing workflows
  • MEDLEY-BENCH reveals a dissociation in AI metacognition: scale improves self-evaluation but not self-regulation

entry.title: Qwen3.5-Omni Technical Report

author.name: Qwen Team

entry.summary: Qwen3.5-Omni is a massive omni-modal model scaling to hundreds of billions of parameters with 256k context, trained on 100M+ hours of audio-visual data. It achieves SOTA on 215 audio/audio-visual benchmarks, surpassing Gemini-3.1 Pro on key audio tasks using a Hybrid Attention MoE architecture for both Thinker and Talker components.

entry.title: Polarization by Default: Auditing Recommendation Bias in LLM-Based Content Curation

author.name: Nicol\`o Pagan, Christopher Barrie, Chris Andrew Bail, Petter T\"ornberg

entry.summary: Audits recommendation biases in LLMs from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google when curating social media content, finding that across 540,000 simulated selections, LLMs show structural polarization biases that differ substantially by provider and are difficult to fully mitigate via prompting.

entry.title: MEDLEY-BENCH: Scale Buys Evaluation but Not Control in AI Metacognition

author.name: Farhad Abtahi, Abdolamir Karbalaie, Eduardo Illueca-Fernandez, Fernando Seoane

entry.summary: Introduces MEDLEY-BENCH, evaluating metacognition (monitoring and regulating one's own reasoning) in 35 models from 12 families, finding a robust dissociation: evaluation ability scales with model size but control/regulation does not.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Degrades Visual Spatial Reasoning Capabilities of Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Sai Srinivas Kancheti, Aditya Sanjiv Kanade, Vineeth N. Balasubramanian, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: Shows that Chain-of-Thought prompting consistently degrades performance in visual spatial reasoning across 17 models and 13 benchmarks. Demonstrates that reasoning models suffer from shortcut learning, hallucinating visual details from textual priors even without images.

entry.title: Detecting and Suppressing Reward Hacking with Gradient Fingerprints

author.name: Songtao Wang, Quang Hieu Pham, Fangcong Yin, Xinpeng Wang, Jocelyn Qiaochu Chen, Greg Durrett and Xi Ye

entry.summary: Proposes Gradient Fingerprint (GRIFT) for detecting reward hacking in RLVR by analyzing models' internal gradient computations rather than surface-level text monitoring. Compresses CoT gradients into compact fingerprints that distinguish genuine from hacking reasoning.

entry.title: AgentV-RL: Scaling Reward Modeling with Agentic Verifier

author.name: Jiazheng Zhang and Ziche Fu and Zhiheng Xi and Wenqing Jing and Mingxu Chai and Wei He and Guoqiang Zhang and Chenghao Fan and Chenxin An and Wenxiang Chen and Zhicheng Liu and Haojie Pan and Dingwei Zhu and Tao Gui and Qi Zhang and Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Agentic Verifier for LLM reasoning, transforming reward modeling into a multi-turn tool-augmented process with bidirectional verification (forward tracing from premises to conclusions and backward checking). Shows improvements in RL training for reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Where does output diversity collapse in post-training?

author.name: Constantinos Karouzos, Xingwei Tan, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: Traces output diversity collapse through three Olmo 3 post-training lineages (Think, Instruct, RL-Zero), finding that collapse location co-varies with data composition rather than training method, and that the generation format contributes independently from model weights.

entry.title: Hallucination as Trajectory Commitment: Causal Evidence for Asymmetric Attractor Dynamics in Transformer Generation

author.name: G. Aytug Akarlar

entry.summary: Provides causal evidence that LLM hallucination is an early trajectory commitment governed by asymmetric attractor dynamics. Shows factual/hallucinated trajectories diverge at the first token, with hallucinated activations being much more 'sticky' than correct ones.

entry.title: LACE: Lattice Attention for Cross-thread Exploration

author.name: Yang Li, Zirui Zhang, Yang Liu, Chengzhi Mao

entry.summary: LACE transforms parallel reasoning from independent trials into coordinated processes by enabling cross-thread attention, allowing concurrent reasoning paths to share intermediate insights and correct each other during inference.

entry.title: Faster LLM Inference via Sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Yahya Emara, Mauricio Barba da Costa, Chi-Chih Chang, Cameron Freer, Tim Vieira, Ryan Cotterell, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah

entry.summary: Proposes SMC-SD (Sequential Monte Carlo Speculative Decoding), which replaces token-level rejection in speculative decoding with importance-weighted resampling over draft particles. Trades exactness for speed while maintaining theoretical approximation bounds.

entry.title: Aligning What Vision-Language Models See and Perceive with Adaptive Information Flow

author.name: Chengxin Liu, Wonseok Choi, Chenshuang Zhang, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: Identifies that VLMs often attend to correct image regions but still produce wrong answers due to suboptimal information flow, where text tokens attend too much to irrelevant visual tokens. Proposes modulating attention during inference to fix this misalignment without retraining.

entry.title: TwoHamsters: Benchmarking Multi-Concept Compositional Unsafety in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Chaoshuo Zhang and Yibo Liang and Mengke Tian and Chenhao Lin and Zhengyu Zhao and Le Yang and Chong Zhang and Yang Zhang and Chao Shen

entry.summary: Introduces TwoHamsters benchmark with 17.5k prompts probing Multi-Concept Compositional Unsafety (MCCU) in text-to-image models, where individually benign concepts combine to create unsafe content. Evaluates 10 models and 16 defense mechanisms.

entry.title: Beyond Distribution Sharpening: The Importance of Task Rewards

author.name: Sarthak Mittal, Leo Gagnon, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: Presents explicit comparison between distribution sharpening and task-reward-based RL, showing fundamental limitations and instability of sharpening approaches. Demonstrates that task rewards genuinely teach new capabilities rather than merely surfacing latent ones.

entry.title: Why Fine-Tuning Encourages Hallucinations and How to Fix It

author.name: Guy Kaplan, Zorik Gekhman, Zhen Zhu, Lotem Rozner, Yuval Reif, Swabha Swayamdipta, Derek Hoiem, Roy Schwartz

entry.summary: Explains why supervised fine-tuning induces hallucinations (knowledge degradation during training) and proposes a self-distillation method that regularizes output-distribution drift, along with freezing strategies to suppress unnecessary factual plasticity.

entry.title: CoEvolve: Training LLM Agents via Agent-Data Mutual Evolution

author.name: Shidong Yang, Ziyu Ma, Tongwen Huang, Yiming Hu, Yong Wang, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: Proposes CoEvolve, a framework for training LLM agents where the agent and training data co-evolve: feedback signals from rollouts identify failure patterns, which guide LLM-based task synthesis to update the training distribution in a closed loop.

entry.title: Cut Your Losses! Learning to Prune Paths Early for Efficient Parallel Reasoning

author.name: Jiaxi Bi, Tongxu Luo, Wenyu Du, Zhengyang Tang, Benyou Wang

entry.summary: Proposes STOP (Super TOken for Pruning), a learnable method for pruning futile reasoning paths in parallel Large Reasoning Models. Introduces a systematic taxonomy of path pruning methods and demonstrates effectiveness across 1.5B to 20B parameter models.

entry.title: Experience Compression Spectrum: Unifying Memory, Skills, and Rules in LLM Agents

author.name: Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang, Yanwei Cui, Wei Qiu, Ziyuan Li, Bing Zhu, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Proposes the Experience Compression Spectrum, a unifying framework positioning agent memory, skills, and rules along a single axis of increasing compression (5-20x for memory, 50-500x for skills, 1000x+ for rules). Analysis of 1,136 references reveals less than 1% cross-citation between memory and skill communities.

entry.title: The Spectral Geometry of Thought: Phase Transitions, Instruction Reversal, Token-Level Dynamics, and Perfect Correctness Prediction in How Transformers Reason

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Discovers spectral phase transitions in LLM hidden activations during reasoning vs factual recall across 11 models and 5 architecture families. Identifies seven phenomena including reasoning spectral compression and instruction tuning reversal.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Frame: Multi-Frame Spatially Grounded Reasoning Across Volumetric MRI

author.name: Lama Moukheiber, Caleb M. Yeung, Haotian Xue, Alec Helbling, Zelin Zhao, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SGMRI-VQA, a 41,307-pair benchmark for multi-frame spatially grounded reasoning on volumetric MRI. Built from expert radiologist annotations, each QA pair includes chain-of-thought traces with frame-indexed bounding boxes, addressing the gap in evaluating VLMs on volumetric medical imaging.

entry.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization

author.name: Junyi Li, Yongqiang Chen, Ningning Ding

entry.summary: Introduces CiPO, a framework for machine unlearning in Large Reasoning Models that uses counterfactual reasoning to selectively remove knowledge from chain-of-thought traces via iterative preference optimization, avoiding degradation of reasoning ability.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Repo-level Code Localization

author.name: Xiufeng Xu, Xiufeng Wu, Zejun Zhang, Yi Li

entry.summary: Identifies a 'Keyword Shortcut' bias in code localization benchmarks where models rely on lexical matching rather than structural reasoning. Introduces KA-LogicQuery benchmark requiring structural reasoning without naming hints and a neurosymbolic approach to address the gap.

entry.title: Mind's Eye: A Benchmark of Visual Abstraction, Transformation and Composition for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Rohit Sinha, Aditya Kanade, Sai Srinivas Kancheti, Vineeth N Balasubramanian, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: Introduces Mind's Eye benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on visual cognitive tasks inspired by human intelligence tests, organized under Abstraction-Relation-Transformation taxonomy. Humans achieve 80% while top MLLMs remain below 50%, revealing significant gaps in visuospatial reasoning.

entry.title: Predicting Where Steering Vectors Succeed

author.name: Jayadev Billa

entry.summary: Introduces the Linear Accessibility Profile (LAP), a training-free diagnostic using the logit lens to predict when and where steering vectors will be effective, achieving high correlation (ρ=0.86-0.91) across multiple models.

entry.title: SocialGrid: A Benchmark for Planning and Social Reasoning in Embodied Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Hikaru Shindo, Hanzhao Lin, Lukas Helff, Patrick Schramowski, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Introduces SocialGrid, an Among Us-inspired multi-agent environment evaluating LLM agents on planning, task execution, and social reasoning. Finds GPT-OSS-120B achieves below 60% on basic tasks, with agents getting stuck in loops. Offers a Planning Oracle to isolate social from planning deficits.

entry.title: Do Vision-Language Models Truly Perform Vision Reasoning? A Rigorous Study of the Modality Gap

author.name: Yige Xu, Yongjie Wang, Zizhuo Wu, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Zhiqi Shen

entry.summary: Introduces CrossMath benchmark with text-only, image-only, and image+text formats of identical problems to isolate whether VLM reasoning is truly vision-grounded. Finds significant modality gaps suggesting heavy reliance on textual reasoning.

entry.title: Weak-to-Strong Knowledge Distillation Accelerates Visual Learning

author.name: Baiang Li, Wenhao Chai, Felix Heide

entry.summary: Proposes a counterintuitive 'weak-to-strong' knowledge distillation approach where a weaker frozen teacher accelerates early training of stronger students, achieving up to 4.8x training speedup on ImageNet classification and generalizing to detection and segmentation tasks.

entry.title: QuantSightBench: Evaluating LLM Quantitative Forecasting with Prediction Intervals

author.name: Jeremy Qin and Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: Proposes QuantSightBench evaluating LLMs on quantitative forecasting using prediction intervals rather than simple binary/multiple-choice questions, requiring scale awareness, internal consistency across confidence levels, and calibration over continuous outcomes.

entry.title: AtManRL: Towards Faithful Reasoning via Differentiable Attention Saliency

author.name: Max Henning H\"oth, Kristian Kersting, Bj\"orn Deiseroth, Letitia Parcalabescu

entry.summary: Introduces AtManRL, combining differentiable attention manipulation with reinforcement learning to improve faithfulness of chain-of-thought reasoning. Uses saliency-based rewards to encourage CoT traces that genuinely influence model predictions.

entry.title: The Harder Path: Last Iterate Convergence for Uncoupled Learning in Zero-Sum Games with Bandit Feedback

author.name: C\^ome Fiegel, Pierre M\'enard, Tadashi Kozuno, Michal Valko, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: Studies last-iterate convergence for uncoupled learning in zero-sum games with bandit feedback. Proves a tight Ω(T^{-1/4}) lower bound for policy convergence to Nash equilibrium and provides matching algorithms, showing this is strictly harder than average-iterate convergence.

entry.title: Exascale Multi-Task Graph Foundation Models for Imbalanced, Multi-Fidelity Atomistic Data

author.name: Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, Jong Youl Choi, Kshitij Mehta, Richard Messerly, Rylie Weaver, Linda Ungerboeck, Isaac Lyngaas, Benajmin Stump, Ashwin M. Aji, Karl W. Schulz, Jorda Polo

entry.summary: Presents an exascale workflow for materials discovery using HydraGNN graph foundation models, jointly training on 16 datasets (544M+ structures, 85+ elements) on Frontier supercomputer. Enables screening 1.1B structures in 50 seconds.

entry.title: PRL-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark Evaluating LLMs' Capabilities in Frontier Physics Research

author.name: Tingjia Miao, Wenkai Jin, Muhua Zhang, Jinxin Tan, Yuelin Hu, Tu Guo, Jiejun Zhang, Yuhan Wang, Wenbo Li, Yinuo Gao, Shuo Chen, Weiqi Jiang, Yayun Hu, Zixing Lei, Xianghe Pang, Zexi Liu, Yuzhi Zhang, Linfeng Zhang, Kun Chen, Wei Wang, Weinan E, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: PRL-Bench evaluates LLMs' ability to conduct end-to-end physics research workflows using 100 curated papers, testing beyond simple knowledge comprehension to assess exploratory capabilities needed for agentic science. This is a systematic attempt to map the frontier of LLMs in executing real research tasks.

entry.title: Symbolic Guardrails for Domain-Specific Agents: Stronger Safety and Security Guarantees Without Sacrificing Utility

author.name: Yining Hong, Yining She, Eunsuk Kang, Christopher S. Timperley, Christian K\"astner

entry.summary: Studies symbolic guardrails as a practical path toward provable safety guarantees for AI agents, analyzing 80 benchmarks to identify evaluable policies and showing symbolic guardrails can guarantee safety without significantly sacrificing utility.

entry.title: EVIL: Evolving Interpretable Algorithms for Zero-Shot Inference on Event Sequences and Time Series with LLMs

author.name: David Berghaus

entry.summary: EVIL uses LLM-guided evolutionary search to discover interpretable Python/NumPy algorithms for dynamical systems inference (temporal point processes, Markov jump processes, time series). Single evolved algorithms generalize across datasets without training.

entry.title: From Seeing to Simulating: Generative High-Fidelity Simulation with Digital Cousins for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation

author.name: Jasper Lu, Zhenhao Shen, Yuanfei Wang, Shugao Liu, Shengqiang Xu, Shawn Xie, Jingkai Xu, Feng Jiang, Jade Yang, Chen Xie, and Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: Presents a generative framework for converting real-world panoramas into high-fidelity simulation scenes, then synthesizing diverse 'cousin' scenes via semantic and geometric editing. Supports interactive manipulation tasks and multi-room stitching for large-scale environments.

entry.title: Placing Puzzle Pieces Where They Matter: A Question Augmentation Framework for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yangyi Fang, Jiaye Lin, Xiaoliang Fu, Cong Qin, Haolin Shi

entry.summary: Proposes PieceHint, a framework for RL-based LLM training that strategically identifies critical reasoning bottlenecks and provides targeted hints rather than uniform hint provision, addressing the easy/hard problem dilemma in reinforcement learning for reasoning.

entry.title: Stochasticity in Tokenisation Improves Robustness

author.name: Sophie Steger, Rui Li, Sofiane Ennadir, Anya Sims, Arno Solin, Franz Pernkopf, Martin Trapp

entry.summary: Demonstrates that stochastic tokenization during pre-training and fine-tuning improves LLM robustness to adversarial attacks and random perturbations. Systematically studies this across pre-training, SFT, and in-context learning regimes.

entry.title: R1 CoT illegibility revisited

author.name: nostalgebraist

entry.summary: Reruns experiments from the paper 'Reasoning Models Sometimes Output Illegible Chains of Thought' using a different R1 provider (Novita vs Targon) and finds dramatically lower illegibility scores (2.30 vs 4.30), with better GPQA accuracy. Provides strong evidence that the original paper's findings about R1 CoT illegibility may be artifacts of a specific model deployment rather than inherent model behavior.

entry.title: The Illusion of Equivalence: Systematic FP16 Divergence in KV-Cached Autoregressive Inference

author.name: Ranjith Chodavarapu and Lei Xu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that KV caching introduces systematic FP16 divergence in transformer inference due to non-associative floating-point accumulation, with 100% token divergence rate across three models even under greedy decoding.

entry.title: Ragged Paged Attention: A High-Performance and Flexible LLM Inference Kernel for TPU

author.name: Jevin Jiang, Ying Chen, Blake A. Hechtman, Fenghui Zhang, Yarong Mu

entry.summary: Presents Ragged Paged Attention (RPA), a high-performance attention kernel optimized for TPUs using Pallas and Mosaic, addressing the gap in efficient LLM inference on non-GPU accelerators through fine-grained tiling and custom pipelining.

entry.title: Frequency-Aware Flow Matching for High-Quality Image Generation

author.name: Sucheng Ren, Qihang Yu, Ju He, Xiaohui Shen, Alan Yuille, Liang-Chieh Chen

entry.summary: FreqFlow introduces frequency-aware conditioning into flow matching for image generation, using a two-branch architecture that explicitly handles low-frequency structure and high-frequency details with time-dependent adaptive weighting.

entry.title: LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought

author.name: Wenshuo Wang

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that LLM reasoning should be studied as latent-state trajectory formation rather than surface chain-of-thought. Formalizes three competing hypotheses about the locus of reasoning (latent states vs. CoT vs. generic serial compute).

entry.title: When Do Early-Exit Networks Generalize? A PAC-Bayesian Theory of Adaptive Depth

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu Ming Yiu

entry.summary: Establishes the first PAC-Bayesian generalization theory for early-exit neural networks, proving bounds that depend on exit-depth entropy and expected depth rather than maximum depth. Shows early exiting provides provable regularization benefits.

entry.title: Disentangling Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs: A Methodological Investigation of Internal Mechanisms

author.name: Tanja Baeumel, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: Investigates how LLMs perform arithmetic by tracing internal mechanisms using early decoding. Finds that models recognize arithmetic tasks early but correct results emerge only in final layers, with proficient models showing clear division of labor between attention (information propagation) and MLP (aggregation) modules.

entry.title: RAGognizer: Hallucination-Aware Fine-Tuning via Detection Head Integration

author.name: Fabian Ridder, Laurin Lessel, Malte Schilling

entry.summary: Introduces RAGognizer, a hallucination-aware fine-tuning approach that uses internal state representations as training signals for detecting closed-domain hallucinations in RAG, along with RAGognize dataset of naturally occurring hallucinations with token-level annotations.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Statistics: Robust Conformal Prediction for LLMs via Internal Representations

author.name: Yanli Wang, Peng Kuang, Xiaoyu Han, Kaidi Xu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a conformal prediction framework for LLM QA using internal representations (Layer-Wise Information scores) rather than output statistics. Measures how input conditioning reshapes entropy across model depth for more robust uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Stochastic Shortest Path with a Generative Model

author.name: Jean Tarbouriech, Matteo Pirotta, Michal Valko, Alessandro Lazaric

entry.summary: Derives tight sample complexity bounds for learning near-optimal policies in Stochastic Shortest Path problems with a generative model. Reveals that SSPs with zero minimum cost may be unlearnable, making them strictly harder than finite-horizon/discounted settings.

entry.title: Enhancing AI and Dynamical Subseasonal Forecasts with Probabilistic Bias Correction

author.name: Hannah Guan, Soukayna Mouatadid, Paulo Orenstein, Judah Cohen, Haiyu Dong, Zekun Ni, Jeremy Berman, Genevieve Flaspohler, Alex Lu, Jakob Schloer, Joshua Talib, Jonathan A. Weyn, Lester Mackey

entry.summary: Introduces probabilistic bias correction (PBC), an ML framework that learns to correct systematic errors in subseasonal weather forecasts from both dynamical and AI models. Doubles useful forecast skill for ECMWF models at 2-6 week timescales.

entry.title: Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries: Beyond the Per-Vector Shannon Limit

author.name: Gregory Magarshak

entry.summary: Proposes sequential KV cache compression using probabilistic language tries that exploit the sequential structure of token data, going beyond per-vector Shannon limits. Uses prefix deduplication and predictive coding for cross-session compression.

entry.title: (1D) Ordered Tokens Enable Efficient Test-Time Search

author.name: Zhitong Gao, Parham Rezaei, Ali Cy, Mingqiao Ye, Nata\v{s}a Jovanovi\'c, Jesse Allardice, Afshin Dehghan, Amir Zamir, Roman Bachmann, O\u{g}uzhan Fatih Kar

entry.summary: Demonstrates that 1D ordered (coarse-to-fine) tokenization enables more effective test-time search in autoregressive image generation compared to 2D grid tokenizers, because intermediate states carry semantic meaning that verifiers can meaningfully evaluate.

entry.title: Harmonizing Multi-Objective LLM Unlearning via Unified Domain Representation and Bidirectional Logit Distillation

author.name: Yisheng Zhong, Sijia Liu, Zhuangdi Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-objective LLM unlearning framework that harmonizes knowledge removal, utility preservation, over-refusal avoidance, and adversarial robustness through unified domain representation and bidirectional logit distillation.

entry.title: Neural Continuous-Time Markov Chain: Discrete Diffusion via Decoupled Jump Timing and Direction

author.name: Jingyuan Li, Xiaoyi Jiang, Fukang Wen, Wei Liu, Renqian Luo, Yi Zhu, Zuoqiang Shi, Pipi Hu

entry.summary: Neural CTMC proposes decomposing discrete diffusion models into separate exit rate (when to jump) and jump distribution (where to go) components, aligning with the fundamental structure of continuous-time Markov chains. Shows improvements on language generation tasks.

entry.title: Reasoning-targeted Jailbreak Attacks on Large Reasoning Models via Semantic Triggers and Psychological Framing

author.name: Zehao Wang, Lanjun Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a novel attack on Large Reasoning Models that injects harmful content into reasoning steps while preserving correct final answers, using semantic triggers and psychological framing to bypass safety alignment.

entry.title: DPrivBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Reasoning for Differential Privacy

author.name: Erchi Wang, Pengrun Huang, Eli Chien, Om Thakkar, Kamalika Chaudhuri, Yu-Xiang Wang, Ruihan Wu

entry.summary: Introduces DPrivBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can reason about differential privacy, with instances asking if algorithms satisfy stated DP guarantees. Designed to resist shortcut reasoning and covers diverse DP topics at multiple difficulty levels.

entry.title: How Hypocritical Is Your LLM judge? Listener-Speaker Asymmetries in the Pragmatic Competence of Large Language Models

author.name: Judith Sieker and Sina Zarrie{\ss}

entry.summary: Studies asymmetry between LLMs' pragmatic listening (judging appropriateness) and pragmatic speaking (generating appropriate language), finding that many models are 'hypocritical judges' who can evaluate pragmatic quality but fail to produce it.

entry.title: Discovering quantum phenomena with Interpretable Machine Learning

author.name: Paulin de Schoulepnikoff, Hendrik Poulsen Nautrup, Hans J. Briegel, and Gorka Mu\~noz-Gil

entry.summary: Demonstrates that variational autoencoders can learn physically meaningful representations from unlabeled quantum datasets, augmented with symbolic methods to discover compact analytical order parameters. Applied to experimental Rydberg-atom data and classical shadows.

entry.title: AEGIS: Anchor-Enforced Gradient Isolation for Knowledge-Preserving Vision-Language-Action Fine-Tuning

author.name: Guransh Singh

entry.summary: Introduces AEGIS, a method to prevent catastrophic forgetting of VQA capabilities when fine-tuning vision-language models for robotic control. Addresses the cross-modal gradient asymmetry between flow-matching action gradients and cross-entropy-trained backbones.

entry.title: DINOv3 Beats Specialized Detectors: A Simple Foundation Model Baseline for Image Forensics

author.name: Jieming Yu, Qiuxiao Feng, Zhuohan Wang, Xiaochen Ma

entry.summary: Shows that DINOv3 with LoRA adaptation and a lightweight decoder surpasses all prior specialized image forensics methods for detecting manipulated images, improving pixel-level F1 by 17 points with only 9.1M trainable parameters.

entry.title: Learning to Reason with Insight for Informal Theorem Proving

author.name: Yunhe Li, Hao Shi, Bowen Deng, Wei Wang, Mengzhe Ruan, Hanxu Hou, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Chao Wang, Shuang Qiu, Linqi Song

entry.summary: Proposes DeepInsightTheorem, a hierarchical dataset and progressive multi-stage SFT framework for informal theorem proving that explicitly extracts core techniques and proof sketches to cultivate insightful reasoning in LLMs.

entry.title: Evaluating the Progression of Large Language Model Capabilities for Small-Molecule Drug Design

author.name: Shriram Chennakesavalu, Kirill Shmilovich, Hayley Weir, Colin Grambow, John Bradshaw, Patricia Suriana, Chen Cheng, Kangway Chuang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark suite for evaluating LLM capabilities in small-molecule drug design spanning property prediction, representation transformations, and molecular design, formulated as RL environments. Finds frontier models improving but significant room remains.

entry.title: Reevaluating "AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities" in 2026

author.name: lc

entry.summary: A 2026 re-evaluation of Eliezer Yudkowsky's 2022 'AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities' in light of four years of AI development. Examines which of the 43 doom arguments have held up, which have been weakened, and how the overall picture has changed.

entry.title: DeepER-Med: Advancing Deep Evidence-Based Research in Medicine Through Agentic AI

author.name: Zhizheng Wang, Chih-Hsuan Wei, Joey Chan, Robert Leaman, Chi-Ping Day, Chuan Wu, Mark A Knepper, Antolin Serrano Farias, Jordina Rincon-Torroella, Hasan Slika, Betty Tyler, Ryan Huu-Tuan Nguyen, Asmita Indurkar, M\'elanie H\'ebert, Shubo Tian, Lauren He, Noor Naffakh, Aseem Aseem, Nicholas Wan, Emily Y Chew, Tiarnan D L Keenan, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: DeepER-Med is an agentic AI framework for evidence-based medical research that incorporates explicit evidence appraisal criteria and inspectable reasoning, addressing trustworthiness gaps in existing deep research systems for clinical use.

entry.title: Majority Voting for Code Generation

author.name: Tim Launer, Jonas H\"ubotter, Marco Bagatella, Ido Hakimi, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: Investigates Functional Majority Voting (FMV) for code generation, using runtime execution signatures on test inputs for consensus, achieving substantial performance gains on LiveCodeBench and serving as an aggregation strategy for test-time RL.

entry.title: The World Leaks the Future: Harness Evolution for Future Prediction Agents

author.name: Chuyang Wei (1 and 2), Maohang Gao (1 and 2), Zhixin Han (2), Kefei Chen (2 and 3), Yu Zhuang (2), Haoxiang Guan (1 and 2), Yanzhi Zhang (2), Yilin Cheng (2), Jiyan He (2), Huanhuan Chen (1), Jian Li (3), Yu Shi (2), Yitong Duan (2), Shuxin Zheng (2) ((1) University of Science and Technology of China, (2) Zhongguancun Academy, Beijing, China, (3) Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for future prediction agents that uses temporal contrasts between earlier and later predictions to provide self-supervision (evolutionary signal) without waiting for final outcomes. Enables agents to improve factor tracking and evidence gathering.

entry.title: MemEvoBench: Benchmarking Memory MisEvolution in LLM Agents

author.name: Weiwei Xie, Shaoxiong Guo, Fan Zhang, Tian Xia, Xue Yang, Lizhuang Ma, Junchi Yan, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: MemEvoBench is the first benchmark evaluating long-horizon memory safety in LLM agents against adversarial memory injection, noisy tool outputs, and biased feedback. Tests how contaminated memory leads to behavioral drift over time.

entry.title: One-Shot Generative Flows: Existence and Obstructions

author.name: Panos Tsimpos, Daniel Sharp, Youssef Marzouk

entry.summary: Studies theoretical conditions under which generative flow models can achieve straight-line (one-step) transport between source and target distributions. Proves a sharp dichotomy: under endpoint independence, straight-line flows exist only for Gaussian or uniform targets on the circle.

entry.title: How people use Copilot for Health

author.name: Beatriz Costa-Gomes, Pavel Tolmachev, Eloise Taysom, Viknesh Sounderajah, Hannah Richardson, Philipp Schoenegger, Xiaoxuan Liu, Matthew M Nour, Seth Spielman, Samuel F. Way, Yash Shah, Michael Bhaskar, Harsha Nori, Christopher Kelly, Peter Hames, Bay Gross, Mustafa Suleyman, Dominic King

entry.summary: Analyzes 500,000+ de-identified health conversations with Microsoft Copilot to characterize how people use conversational AI for health queries. Develops a 12-category intent taxonomy and reveals that ~20% involve personal symptom assessment.

entry.title: Aletheia: Gradient-Guided Layer Selection for Efficient LoRA Fine-Tuning Across Architectures

author.name: Abdulmalek Saket

entry.summary: Introduces Aletheia, a gradient-guided method for selecting which transformer layers receive LoRA adapters, achieving 15-28% training speedup across 81 experiments covering 14 models from 8 architecture families (0.5B-72B).

entry.title: StoSignSGD: Unbiased Structural Stochasticity Fixes SignSGD for Training Large Language Models

author.name: Dingzhi Yu, Rui Pan, Yuxing Liu, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: StoSignSGD fixes the non-convergence issue of SignSGD on non-smooth objectives by injecting structural stochasticity while maintaining unbiased updates, achieving convergence rates matching lower bounds in convex settings and being applied to LLM training.

entry.title: FineSteer: A Unified Framework for Fine-Grained Inference-Time Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Weng, Jinghuai Zhang, Kunlin Cai, Ying Li, Peiran Wang and Yuan Tian

entry.summary: FineSteer decomposes inference-time steering into conditional steering and fine-grained vector synthesis stages, enabling precise control over when and how to steer LLM internal representations to address safety violations and hallucinations.

entry.title: Brain Score Tracks Shared Properties of Languages: Evidence from Many Natural Languages and Structured Sequences

author.name: Jingnong Qu, Ashvin Ranjan, Shane Steinert-Threlkeld

entry.summary: Finds that LMs trained on various natural languages and even structured non-language data (genome, Python, nested parentheses) achieve similar Brain Scores, suggesting Brain Score captures general structural processing properties rather than language-specific features.

entry.title: Reward Weighted Classifier-Free Guidance as Policy Improvement in Autoregressive Models

author.name: Alexander Peysakhovich, William Berman

entry.summary: Shows that reward-weighted classifier-free guidance (RCFG) can act as a policy improvement operator for autoregressive models without retraining, applied to molecular generation for optimizing novel reward functions at inference time.

entry.title: Adapting in the Dark: Efficient and Stable Test-Time Adaptation for Black-Box Models

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Shuaicheng Niu, Chengyi Cai, Feng Liu, Jihun Hamm

entry.summary: BETA enables test-time adaptation for black-box API models using a lightweight local steering model to create gradient pathways, achieving stable adaptation without additional API calls through prediction harmonization.

entry.title: The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring

author.name: Jon-Paul Cacioli

entry.summary: Introduces the Metacognitive Monitoring Battery, a 524-item cross-domain benchmark for evaluating LLM self-monitoring capabilities using human psychometric methodology. Measures whether LLMs can appropriately withdraw incorrect answers.

entry.title: Towards Robust Endogenous Reasoning: Unifying Drift Adaptation in Non-Stationary Tuning

author.name: Xiaoyu Yang, En Yu, Wei Duan, Jie Lu

entry.summary: Reveals that multimodal LLMs are susceptible to endogenous reasoning drift during autoregressive generation, manifesting as unpredictable distribution changes independent of external perturbations. Proposes theoretical framework and adaptation methods.

entry.title: GTA-2: Benchmarking General Tool Agents from Atomic Tool-Use to Open-Ended Workflows

author.name: Jize Wang, Xuanxuan Liu, Yining Li, Songyang Zhang, Yijun Wang, Zifei Shan, Xinyi Le, Cailian Chen, Xinping Guan, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: GTA-2 is a hierarchical benchmark for general tool agents spanning atomic tool use and open-ended workflows, using real user queries, deployed tools, and multimodal contexts. Introduces GTA-Workflow for long-horizon task completion evaluation.

entry.title: KWBench: Measuring Unprompted Problem Recognition in Knowledge Work

author.name: Ankit Maloo

entry.summary: KWBench evaluates LLMs on unprompted problem recognition in knowledge work - whether models can identify the governing structure of professional scenarios (principal-agent conflicts, signaling, mechanism design failures) before solving them.

entry.title: Closing the Theory-Practice Gap in Spiking Transformers via Effective Dimension

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu Ming Yiu

entry.summary: Establishes the first comprehensive expressivity theory for spiking transformers, proving universal approximation, deriving spike-count lower bounds via rate-distortion theory, and providing explicit circuit constructions for softmax normalization.

entry.title: Pruning Unsafe Tickets: A Resource-Efficient Framework for Safer and More Robust LLMs

author.name: Wai Man Si, Mingjie Li, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a resource-efficient pruning framework that identifies and removes unsafe subnetworks in LLMs using gradient-free attribution, requiring only modest GPU resources. Shows substantial reductions in unsafe generations while preserving utility.

entry.title: UsefulBench: Towards Decision-Useful Information as a Target for Information Retrieval

author.name: Tobias Schimanski, Stefanie Lewandowski, Christian Woerle, Nicola Reichenau, Yauheni Huryn, Markus Leippold

entry.summary: Introduces UsefulBench, distinguishing between text relevance (similarity-based) and usefulness (practical value for answering a query) in information retrieval. Shows that classic IR aligns with relevance while LLM-based systems can better capture usefulness.

entry.title: Beyond Text Prompts: Precise Concept Erasure through Text-Image Collaboration

author.name: Jun Li, Lizhi Xiong, Ziqiang Li, Weiwei Jiang, Zhangjie Fu, Yong Li, Guo-Sen Xie

entry.summary: Proposes TICoE, a text-image collaborative framework for precise concept erasure in text-to-image models, using a continuous convex concept manifold and hierarchical visual representation learning to remove target concepts while preserving unrelated content.

entry.title: UniEditBench: A Unified and Cost-Effective Benchmark for Image and Video Editing via Distilled MLLMs

author.name: Lifan Jiang, Tianrun Wu, Yuhang Pei, Chenyang Wang, Boxi Wu, Deng Cai

entry.summary: Introduces UniEditBench, a unified benchmark for image and video editing supporting both reconstruction-based and instruction-driven methods, with distilled MLLMs as cost-effective evaluators and a structured taxonomy of editing operations.

entry.title: Efficient Video Diffusion Models: Advancements and Challenges

author.name: Shitong Shao, Lichen Bai, Pengfei Wan, James Kwok, and Zeke Xie

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of efficient video diffusion models, categorizing methods into step distillation, efficient attention, model compression, and cache/trajectory optimization. Provides a deployment-oriented review addressing spatial-temporal computation bottlenecks.

entry.title: Making Image Editing Easier via Adaptive Task Reformulation with Agentic Executions

author.name: Bo Zhao and Kairui Guo and Runnan Du and Haiyang Sun and Pengshan Wang and Huan Yang and Kun Gai and Yixin Cao and Wei Ji

entry.summary: Frames image editing failures as a task formulation problem rather than model capacity issue, proposing an adaptive reformulation framework where an MLLM agent analyzes, routes, and reformulates editing tasks to improve success without modifying the underlying model.

entry.title: Weak-Link Optimization for Multi-Agent Reasoning and Collaboration

author.name: Haoyu Bian, Chaoning Zhang, Jiaquan Zhang, Xingyao Li, Yuanfang Guo, Wei Dong, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes WORC, a framework that systematically identifies and reinforces performance-limiting 'weak-link' agents in multi-agent LLM systems, based on the weak-link principle that overall system performance is bottlenecked by the weakest agent.

entry.title: ReactBench: A Benchmark for Topological Reasoning in MLLMs on Chemical Reaction Diagrams

author.name: Qiang Xu, Shengyuan Bai, Yu Wang, He Cao, Leqing Chen, Yuanyuan Liu, Bin Feng, Zijing Liu, Yu Li

entry.summary: Introduces ReactBench, a benchmark testing MLLMs on topological/structural reasoning in chemical reaction diagrams, revealing that models struggle with branching, converging, and cyclic structures even on basic tasks like counting endpoints.

entry.title: Towards Intrinsic Interpretability of Large Language Models:A Survey of Design Principles and Architectures

author.name: Yutong Gao, Qinglin Meng, Yuan Zhou, Liangming Pan

entry.summary: Surveys intrinsic interpretability approaches for LLMs, categorizing them into five design paradigms: functional transparency, concept alignment, representational decomposability, explicit modularization, and latent sparsity induction. Contrasts with post-hoc explanation methods.

entry.title: The Amazing Stability of Flow Matching

author.name: Rania Briq, Michael Kamp, Ohad Fried, Sarel Cohen, Stefan Kesselheim

entry.summary: Investigates the stability of flow matching models, finding they remain stable even when 50% of training data is pruned. Shows that latent representations are remarkably consistent across different data subsets, architectures, and training configurations.

entry.title: On the Rejection Criterion for Proxy-based Test-time Alignment

author.name: Ayoub Hammal, Pierre Zweigenbaum and Caio Corro

entry.summary: Shows that proxy-based test-time alignment methods (implicit reward and nudging) reduce to similar graphical models differing only in rejection criteria. Proposes a novel conservative confidence bet criterion that outperforms existing approaches.

entry.title: Sketching the Readout of Large Language Models for Scalable Data Attribution and Valuation

author.name: Yide Ran, Jianwen Xie, Minghui Wang, Wenjin Zheng, Denghui Zhang, Chuan Li, Zhaozhuo Xu

entry.summary: Introduces RISE, a scalable data attribution method for LLMs that focuses on influence hotspots at the output layer using CountSketch projections. Combines lexical and semantic channels for efficient influence estimation.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic ODE Discovery with Latent Grammar Flow

author.name: Karin Yu, Eleni Chatzi, Georgios Kissas

entry.summary: Introduces Latent Grammar Flow (LGF), a neuro-symbolic framework for discovering ODEs from data that embeds equations as grammar-based representations in a discrete latent space, using discrete flow models to generate candidate equations.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Simulators as Differentially Private Data Generators

author.name: Nassima M. Bouzid, Dehao Yuan, Nam H. Nguyen, Mayana Pereira

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLM-based simulators can generate differentially private synthetic data, finding that while PersonaLedger achieves reasonable fraud detection utility, systematic LLM biases cause significant distribution drift, overriding input statistics.

entry.title: Bilevel Optimization of Agent Skills via Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Chenyi Huang, Haoting Zhang, Jingxu Xu, Zeyu Zheng, Yunduan Lin

entry.summary: Proposes bilevel optimization of LLM agent skills via Monte Carlo Tree Search, jointly optimizing the structure and content of skills (instructions, tools, resources) that guide agent performance.

entry.title: The Synthetic Media Shift: Tracking the Rise, Virality, and Detectability of AI-Generated Multimodal Misinformation

author.name: Zacharias Chrysidis, Stefanos-Iordanis Papadopoulos, Symeon Papadopoulos

entry.summary: Introduces CONVEX, a 150K+ post dataset of multimodal misinformation from X's Community Notes. Finds AI-generated content achieves disproportionate virality driven by passive engagement, and existing detectors have declining effectiveness.

entry.title: RelativeFlow: Taming Medical Image Denoising Learning with Noisy Reference

author.name: Yuxin Liu, Yiqing Dong, Wenxue Yu, Zhan Wu, Rongjun Ge, Yang Chen, Yuting He

entry.summary: RelativeFlow proposes a flow matching framework for medical image denoising that learns from heterogeneous noisy references by decomposing absolute noise-to-clean mapping into relative mappings, addressing the fundamental lack of clean supervision in medical imaging.

entry.title: NeuroMesh: A Unified Neural Inference Framework for Decentralized Multi-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Yang Zhou, Yash Shetye, Long Quang, Devon Super, Jesse Milzman, Manohari Goarin, Aditya Azad, Devang Sunil Dhake, Jeffery Mao, Carlos Nieto-Granda, and Giuseppe Loianno

entry.summary: NeuroMesh provides a unified neural inference framework for decentralized multi-robot collaboration, standardizing observation encoding, message passing, and task decoding across heterogeneous platforms with a high-performance C++ implementation.

entry.title: SecureRouter: Encrypted Routing for Efficient Secure Inference

author.name: Yukuan Zhang, Mengxin Zheng, Qian Lou

entry.summary: SecureRouter enables input-adaptive model selection under encryption for faster secure neural network inference, routing encrypted inputs to appropriately-sized models using MPC-compatible techniques.

entry.title: PolicyBank: Evolving Policy Understanding for LLM Agents

author.name: Jihye Choi, Jinsung Yoon, Long T. Le, Somesh Jha and Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: PolicyBank introduces a memory mechanism for LLM agents that iteratively refines tool-level policy insights through interaction and corrective feedback, addressing specification gaps in organizational policies rather than treating them as immutable.

entry.title: GroupDPO: Memory efficient Group-wise Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Jixuan Leng, Si Si, Hsiang-Fu Yu, Vinod Raman, Inderjit S. Dhillon

entry.summary: GroupDPO introduces a memory-efficient group-wise preference optimization algorithm that preserves gradients while decoupling samples during backpropagation, enabling scaling to larger groups and improving alignment performance.

entry.title: Stargazer: A Scalable Model-Fitting Benchmark Environment for AI Agents under Astrophysical Constraints

author.name: Xinge Liu, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Zhijing Jin, Kristen Menou

entry.summary: Stargazer is a scalable benchmark environment for evaluating AI agents on physics-grounded model-fitting tasks using radial-velocity time series data. Evaluation of 8 frontier agents reveals they achieve good numerical optimization but struggle with physical constraints.

entry.title: Target-Oriented Pretraining Data Selection via Neuron-Activated Graph

author.name: Zijun Wang, Haoqin Tu, Weidong Zhou, Yiyang Zhou, Xiaohuan Zhou, Bingni Zhang, Weiguo Feng, Taifeng Wang, Cihang Xie, Fengze Liu

entry.summary: NAG-based Ranking proposes a training-free framework for target-oriented pretraining data selection by characterizing inputs through sparse high-impact neurons (Neuron-Activated Graphs) in existing LLMs, then ranking candidate data by NAG similarity.

entry.title: Just Type It in Isabelle! AI Agents Drafting, Mechanizing, and Generalizing from Human Hints

author.name: Kevin Kappelmann, Maximilian Sch\"affeler, Lukas Stevens, Mohammad Abdulaziz, Andrei Popescu, Dmitriy Traytel

entry.summary: Studies type annotation problems in Isabelle proof assistant, with both human and AI-driven formalization workflows. An LLM-powered AI agent independently produces pen-and-paper proofs and autoformalizes them in Isabelle/HOL.

entry.title: A Case Study on the Impact of Anonymization Along the RAG Pipeline

author.name: Andreea-Elena Bodea, Stephen Meisenbacher, and Florian Matthes

entry.summary: Case study examining the impact of anonymization placement along the RAG pipeline, systematically measuring how anonymizing at different stages affects retrieval and generation quality.

entry.title: MMGait: Towards Multi-Modal Gait Recognition

author.name: Chenye Wang, Qingyuan Cai, Saihui Hou, Aoqi Li, Yongzhen Huang

entry.summary: Introduces MMGait, a comprehensive multi-modal gait recognition benchmark with 334,060 sequences from 725 subjects using five sensors (RGB, depth, infrared, LiDAR, 4D radar), enabling systematic evaluation across 12 modalities.

entry.title: Elucidating the SNR-t Bias of Diffusion Probabilistic Models

author.name: Meng Yu, Lei Sun, Jianhao Zeng, Xiangxiang Chu, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: Identifies and analyzes SNR-timestep bias in diffusion models where the signal-to-noise ratio misaligns with timesteps during inference, causing error accumulation. Proposes a differential correction method to mitigate this bias.

entry.title: Prototype-Grounded Concept Models for Verifiable Concept Alignment

author.name: Stefano Colamonaco, David Debot, Pietro Barbiero, Giuseppe Marra

entry.summary: Introduces Prototype-Grounded Concept Models that ground learned concepts in visual prototypes, enabling verification of concept alignment and targeted human intervention. Matches CBM performance while improving transparency and intervenability.

entry.title: neuralCAD-Edit: An Expert Benchmark for Multimodal-Instructed 3D CAD Model Editing

author.name: Toby Perrett, Matthew Bouchard, William McCarthy

entry.summary: Introduces neuralCAD-Edit, the first benchmark for 3D CAD model editing collected from expert engineers using multimodal inputs (video, speech, gestures). Even GPT 5.2 scores 53% lower than human CAD experts in acceptance trials.

entry.title: VEFX-Bench: A Holistic Benchmark for Generic Video Editing and Visual Effects

author.name: Xiangbo Gao, Sicong Jiang, Bangya Liu, Xinghao Chen, Minglai Yang, Siyuan Yang, Mingyang Wu, Jiongze Yu, Qi Zheng, Haozhi Wang, Jiayi Zhang, Jared Yang, Jie Yang, Zihan Wang, Qing Yin, and Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: Introduces VEFX-Dataset with 5,049 human-annotated video editing examples across 9 categories and 32 subcategories, plus VEFX-Judge, a specialized evaluator for comparing video editing systems.

entry.title: Will AI make everything more correlated?

author.name: TFD

entry.summary: Explores whether widespread AI adoption will increase correlation across information sources, reducing the diversity that makes systems like Community Notes effective. Argues that if everyone relies on similar AI systems, errors become correlated, undermining the epistemic value of having diverse independent sources.

entry.title: When the Loop Closes: Architectural Limits of In-Context Isolation, Metacognitive Co-option, and the Two-Target Design Problem in Human-LLM Systems

author.name: Z. Cheng and N. Song

entry.summary: Autoethnographic case study documenting how a single subject's cognitive self-regulation was co-opted by an LLM system within 48 hours, with observable behavioral changes including loss of self-initiated reasoning.

entry.title: One-Shot Cross-Geometry Skill Transfer through Part Decomposition

author.name: Skye Thompson, Ondrej Biza, and George Konidaris

entry.summary: Proposes one-shot cross-geometry skill transfer for robots by decomposing objects into semantic parts and leveraging generative shape models to transfer interaction points from demonstration objects to novel objects with unfamiliar geometries.

entry.title: Think Multilingual, Not Harder: A Data-Efficient Framework for Teaching Reasoning Models to Code-Switch

author.name: Eleanor M. Lin, David Jurgens

entry.summary: Introduces the first linguistically motivated fine-tuning framework for teaching reasoning models to code-switch beneficially, showing that strategic language mixing can improve reasoning performance across diverse languages and tasks.

entry.title: CTSCAN: Evaluation Leakage in Chest CT Segmentation and a Reproducible Patient-Disjoint Benchmark

author.name: Anton Ivchenko

entry.summary: CTSCAN reveals that reported chest CT segmentation performance is strongly inflated by data leakage when train/test partitions mix slices from same studies, providing a reproducible patient-disjoint benchmark showing significant performance drops.

entry.title: "Excuse me, may I say something..." CoLabScience, A Proactive AI Assistant for Biomedical Discovery and LLM-Expert Collaborations

author.name: Yang Wu, Jinhong Yu, Jingwei Xiong, Zhimin Tao, Xiaozhong Liu

entry.summary: CoLabScience is a proactive LLM assistant that autonomously determines when and how to intervene in biomedical research discussions using PULI, a PU learning framework with RL objectives for timely context-aware interventions.

entry.title: DALM: A Domain-Algebraic Language Model via Three-Phase Structured Generation

author.name: Chao Li

entry.summary: DALM replaces unconstrained token generation with structured denoising over a domain lattice, resolving domain, relation, and concept uncertainty in sequence to prevent cross-domain knowledge interference in LLMs.

entry.title: Rethinking the Necessity of Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation through the Lens of Adaptive Listwise Ranking

author.name: Jun Feng, Jiahui Tang, Zhicheng He, Hang Lv, Hongchao Gu, Hao Wang, Xuezhi Yang, Shuai Fang

entry.summary: Rethinks the necessity of adaptive retrieval-augmented generation as LLMs become more noise-robust, proposing AdaRankLLM with adaptive listwise reranking and passage dropout to determine when retrieval actually helps.

entry.title: CodeMMR: Bridging Natural Language, Code, and Image for Unified Retrieval

author.name: Jiahui Geng, Qing Li, Fengyu Cai, Fakhri Karray

entry.summary: CodeMMR introduces multimodal code information retrieval that jointly embeds natural language, code, and visual content (UIs, diagrams, SVGs). Also presents MMCoIR, the first comprehensive benchmark for multimodal code IR spanning 5 visual domains and 8 programming languages.

entry.title: The Price of Paranoia: Robust Risk-Sensitive Cooperation in Non-Stationary Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Deep Kumar Ganguly, Chandradithya S Jonnalagadda, Pratham Chintamani, Adithya Ananth

entry.summary: Studies how co-learning noise destabilizes cooperative equilibria in multi-agent RL, finding that even Pareto-dominant cooperative equilibria are exponentially unstable under risk-neutral learning. Proposes robust risk-sensitive methods that balance cooperation stability with efficiency.

entry.title: Learning Uncertainty from Sequential Internal Dispersion in Large Language Models

author.name: Ponhvoan Srey, Xiaobao Wu, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: SIVR presents a supervised hallucination detection framework that uses token-wise, layer-wise variance of hidden states across layers as an uncertainty signal. Model and task agnostic approach that avoids strict assumptions about hidden state evolution.

entry.title: A Systematic Study of Training-Free Methods for Trustworthy Large Language Models

author.name: Wai Man Si, Mingjie Li, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Systematic study re-evaluating training-free methods for trustworthy LLMs across multiple dimensions including safety, robustness, and utility. Finds these methods can introduce undesirable side effects like utility degradation and brittleness.

entry.title: Modern Structure-Aware Simplicial Spatiotemporal Neural Network

author.name: Zhaobo Hu and Vincent Gauthier and Mehdi Naima

entry.summary: Introduces ModernSASST, the first approach to use simplicial complex structures for spatiotemporal modeling, going beyond pairwise GNN relationships to capture richer topological relationships using spatiotemporal random walks on higher-order structures.

entry.title: Learning to Look before Learning to Like: Incorporating Human Visual Cognition into Aesthetic Quality Assessment

author.name: Liwen Yu, Chi Liu, Xiaotong Han, Congcong Zhu, Minghao Wang, Sheng Shen

entry.summary: Proposes AestheticNet, a cognitive-inspired aesthetic quality assessment model with two pathways: a gaze-aligned visual encoder pre-trained on eye-tracking data and a semantic perception pathway, mimicking how humans actually explore images before judging them.

entry.title: Towards Rigorous Explainability by Feature Attribution

author.name: Olivier L\'etoff\'e, Xuanxiang Huang, Joao Marques-Silva

entry.summary: Overview of efforts toward rigorous symbolic methods for explainability as alternatives to non-rigorous approaches like SHAP and Shapley values, arguing that non-symbolic XAI methods lack rigor and can mislead decision-makers in high-stakes ML.

entry.title: Neural Gabor Splatting: Enhanced Gaussian Splatting with Neural Gabor for High-frequency Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Haato Watanabe, Nobuyuki Umetani

entry.summary: Proposes neural Gabor splatting, augmenting each Gaussian primitive with a lightweight MLP that models color variations within a single primitive, reducing the need for many primitives to represent high-frequency surface details.

entry.title: Integrating Graphs, Large Language Models, and Agents: Reasoning and Retrieval

author.name: Hamed Jelodar, Samita Bai, Mohammad Meymani, Parisa Hamedi, Roozbeh Razavi-Far, Ali Ghorbani

entry.summary: Survey of graph-LLM integration methods, categorizing by purpose (reasoning, retrieval, generation, recommendation), graph modality (knowledge, scene, interaction, causal graphs), and integration strategy (prompting, augmentation, training, agent-based).

entry.title: The Relic Condition: When Published Scholarship Becomes Material for Its Own Replacement

author.name: Lin Deng and Chang-bo Liu

entry.summary: Extracts scholarly reasoning systems from published humanities/social science corpora and converts them into structured LLM constraints, creating 'scholar-bots' that perform doctoral supervision, peer review, and lecturing at expert-assessed quality.

entry.title: JumpLoRA: Sparse Adapters for Continual Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Alexandra Dragomir, Ioana Pintilie, Antonio Barbalau, Marius Dragoi, Florin Brad, Cristian Daniel Paduraru, Alexandru Tifrea, Elena Burceanu, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: Proposes JumpLoRA, a continual learning framework using JumpReLU gating to induce adaptive sparsity in LoRA blocks for dynamic parameter isolation, mitigating catastrophic forgetting across sequential tasks in LLMs.

entry.title: DENALI: A Dataset Enabling Non-Line-of-Sight Spatial Reasoning with Low-Cost LiDARs

author.name: Nikhil Behari, Diego Rivero, Luke Apostolides, Suman Ghosh, Paul Pu Liang, Ramesh Raskar

entry.summary: Presents DENALI, the first large-scale real-world dataset of time-resolved LiDAR histograms from consumer devices capturing non-line-of-sight scenes. Enables data-driven NLOS perception with 72,000 scenes across diverse conditions.

entry.title: Semantic Area Graph Reasoning for Multi-Robot Language-Guided Search

author.name: Ruiyang Wang, Hao-Lun Hsu, Jiwoo Kim, and Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: Proposes SAGR, a hierarchical framework enabling LLMs to coordinate multi-robot exploration and semantic search through structured semantic-topological abstraction of environments using semantic area graphs.

entry.title: Phase Transitions as the Breakdown of Statistical Indistinguishability

author.name: Taiyo Narita and Hideyuki Miyahara

entry.summary: Proposes characterizing phase transitions through hypothesis testing and statistical indistinguishability rather than order parameters. Demonstrates the framework by accurately identifying the 2D Ising model critical point using a distribution-free two-sample test without prior knowledge.

entry.title: Adaptive multi-fidelity optimization with fast learning rates

author.name: Come Fiegel, Victor Gabillon, Michal Valko

entry.summary: Studies multi-fidelity optimization where biased approximations of varying costs are available. Proves lower bounds for simple regret and presents the Kometo algorithm that achieves near-optimal rates without knowledge of smoothness or fidelity assumptions.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Model Optimization: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lute Lillo, Nick Cheney

entry.summary: TeLAPA addresses loss of plasticity in continual reinforcement learning by maintaining behaviorally diverse policy archives organized in a shared latent space, inspired by quality-diversity methods. This allows archived policies to remain comparable and reusable under non-stationary drift.

entry.title: ShapeGen: Robotic Data Generation for Category-Level Manipulation

author.name: Yirui Wang, Xiuwei Xu, Angyuan Ma, Bingyao Yu, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: ShapeGen generates shape-varied manipulation training data in a simulator-free manner by decomposing data generation into shape variation and trajectory adaptation, enabling category-level manipulation policies.

entry.title: GaussianFlow SLAM: Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM Guided by GaussianFlow

author.name: Dong-Uk Seo, Jinwoo Jeon, Eungchang Mason Lee, and Hyun Myung

entry.summary: GaussianFlow SLAM uses optical flow to guide optimization of 3D Gaussian splatting maps and camera poses in monocular SLAM, providing geometric supervision that prevents local minima and structural degeneracies.

entry.title: A Structure-Preserving Graph Neural Solver for Parametric Hyperbolic Conservation Laws

author.name: Jiamin Jiang, Shanglin Lv, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: Presents a structure-preserving graph neural solver for parametric hyperbolic conservation laws that respects PDE structure (conservation, entropy) while enabling rapid inference for many-query tasks.

entry.title: AdaVFM: Adaptive Vision Foundation Models for Edge Intelligence via LLM-Guided Execution

author.name: Yiwei Zhao, Yi Zheng, Huapeng Su, Jieyu Lin, Stefano Ambrogio, Cijo Jose, Micha\"el Ramamonjisoa, Patrick Labatut, Barbara De Salvo, Chiao Liu, Phillip B. Gibbons, Ziyun Li

entry.summary: AdaVFM adapts vision foundation models for edge deployment by dynamically adjusting computation based on scene context and task complexity, using NAS-enabled subnets guided by a cloud-based multimodal LLM.

entry.title: SPLIT: Self-supervised Partitioning for Learned Inversion in Nonlinear Tomography

author.name: Markus Haltmeier, Lukas Neumann, Nadja Gruber, Gyeongha Hwang

entry.summary: SPLIT is a self-supervised framework for nonlinear tomographic reconstruction that doesn't require ground-truth images. It uses cross-partition consistency and measurement-domain fidelity to learn from incomplete and noisy projection data.

entry.title: Long-Term Memory for VLA-based Agents in Open-World Task Execution

author.name: Xu Huang, Weixin Mao, Yinhao Li, Hua Chen and Jiabao Zhao

entry.summary: ChemBot is a dual-layer framework combining an AI agent with a progress-aware VLA model for chemical laboratory automation. Uses dual-layer memory architecture to consolidate successful trajectories for multi-stage chemical protocols.

entry.title: Improving Reasoning Capabilities in Small Models through Mixture-of-Layers Distillation with Stepwise Attention on Key Information

author.name: Yao Chen, Jiawei Sheng, Wenyuan Zhang, Tingwen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a CoT distillation framework that transfers teachers' progressive attention shifts toward key information during reasoning to student models, using a Mixture-of-Layers approach for more effective knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Skill-RAG: Failure-State-Aware Retrieval Augmentation via Hidden-State Probing and Skill Routing

author.name: Kai Wei, Raymond Li, Xi Zhu, Zhaoqian Xue, Jiaojiao Han, Jingcheng Niu, Fan Yang

entry.summary: Skill-RAG proposes a failure-aware RAG framework that diagnoses structural causes of retrieval failures through hidden-state probing and routes to appropriate 'skills' (query transformations) rather than simply retrying retrieval.

entry.title: Reversible Residual Normalization Alleviates Spatio-Temporal Distribution Shift

author.name: Zhaobo Hu and Vincent Gauthier and Mehdi Naima

entry.summary: Proposes Reversible Residual Normalization (RRN) to address distribution shift in spatiotemporal forecasting, handling both temporal drift of individual nodes and spatial heterogeneity across the graph network through spatially-aware invertible transformations.

entry.title: DiZiNER: Disagreement-guided Instruction Refinement via Pilot Annotation Simulation for Zero-shot Named Entity Recognition

author.name: Siun Kim, Hyung-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes DiZiNER, a framework simulating pilot annotation processes for zero-shot NER, where multiple heterogeneous LLMs annotate shared texts as annotators and supervisors, resolving disagreements to refine instructions iteratively.

entry.title: Hierarchical Codec Diffusion for Video-to-Speech Generation

author.name: Jiaxin Ye, Gaoxiang Cong, Chenhui Wang, Xin-Cheng Wen, Zhaoyang Li, Boyuan Cao, Hongming Shan

entry.summary: Proposes HiCoDiT, a hierarchical codec diffusion transformer for video-to-speech generation that exploits the hierarchical structure of RVQ-based speech codecs to align coarse speaker semantics and fine-grained prosody with visual features at corresponding levels.

entry.title: VADF: Vision-Adaptive Diffusion Policy Framework for Efficient Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Xinglei Yu, Zhenyang Liu, Shufeng Nan, Simo Wu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Proposes VADF, a vision-driven framework for diffusion policies in robotics that addresses hard negative class imbalance through adaptive loss-based sample prioritization during training and early success in inference.

entry.title: TwinTrack: Post-hoc Multi-Rater Calibration for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Tristan Kirscher (ICube), Alexandra Ertl (DKFZ), Klaus Maier-Hein (DKFZ), Xavier Coubez (ICANS), Philippe Meyer (ICube), Sylvain Faisan (ICube)

entry.summary: Presents TwinTrack, a post-hoc calibration framework for medical image segmentation that calibrates ensemble probabilities to the empirical mean human response, explicitly modeling inter-rater disagreement for pancreatic tumor segmentation.

entry.title: A Wasserstein Geometric Framework for Hebbian Plasticity

author.name: Ulrich Tan

entry.summary: Introduces the Tan-HWG framework formalizing Hebbian plasticity through Wasserstein geometry, modeling memory states as probability measures evolving through optimal transport minimizing movements. Provides theoretical connections between internal dynamics and observable synaptic weights.

entry.title: Tabular foundation models for in-context prediction of molecular properties

author.name: Karim K. Ben Hicham, Jan G. Rittig, Martin Grohe, Alexander Mitsos

entry.summary: Evaluates tabular foundation models for molecular property prediction via in-context learning, comparing against molecular foundation models and classical baselines in low-to-medium data regimes across pharmaceutical and chemical engineering datasets.

entry.title: Find, Fix, Reason: Context Repair for Video Reasoning

author.name: Haojian Huang, Chuanyu Qin, Yinchuan Li, Yingcong Chen

entry.summary: Introduces an observation-level intervention for video reasoning where a frozen teacher model with tool integration identifies missing spatiotemporal dependencies and repairs context for smaller student models during RL training.

entry.title: Information Router for Mitigating Modality Dominance in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Seulgi Kim, Mohit Prabhushankar, Ghassan AlRegib

entry.summary: Proposes MoIR (Multi-modal Information Router) to address modality dominance in VLMs by routing information based on density and signal-to-noise ratio rather than just adjusting attention allocation.

entry.title: ProtoTTA: Prototype-Guided Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Parvin Mousavi, Purang Abolmaesumi, Evan Shelhamer

entry.summary: ProtoTTA adapts prototype-based interpretable models at test time by minimizing entropy of prototype-similarity distributions, enabling robustness to distribution shifts while maintaining interpretability for critical domains like healthcare.

entry.title: C-Mining: Unsupervised Discovery of Seeds for Cultural Data Synthesis via Geometric Misalignment

author.name: Pufan Zeng, Yilun Liu, Mingchen Dai, Mengyao Piao, Chunguang Zhao, Lingqi Miao, Shimin Tao, Weibin Meng, Minggui He, Chenxin Liu, Zhenzhen Qin, Li Zhang, Hongxia Ma, Boxing Chen, Daimeng Wei

entry.summary: C-Mining is an unsupervised framework for discovering cultural seeds for synthetic data generation by exploiting cross-lingual misalignment of cultural concepts in pre-trained embedding spaces. Transforms subjective cultural seed selection into a computable data mining formulation.

entry.title: DepCap: Adaptive Block-Wise Parallel Decoding for Efficient Diffusion LM Inference

author.name: Xiang Xia, Wuyang Zhang, Jiazheng Liu, Cheng Yan, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: DepCap proposes adaptive block-wise parallel decoding for diffusion language models, using cross-step signals for block boundary decisions and enabling more aggressive parallelism while maintaining quality.

entry.title: Collective Kernel EFT for Pre-activation ResNets

author.name: Hidetoshi Kawase, Toshihiro Ota

entry.summary: Develops a collective kernel effective field theory for pre-activation ResNets, deriving exact stochastic recursions for the empirical kernel and identifying finite validity windows of Gaussian approximations in deep networks.

entry.title: Phase transitions in Doi-Onsager, Noisy Transformer, and other multimodal models

author.name: Kyunghoo Mun and Matthew Rosenzweig

entry.summary: Proves that for repulsive-attractive mean-field free energies on the circle, the critical coupling strength equals the linear stability threshold and the phase transition is continuous. Applies results to Doi-Onsager, Noisy Transformer, and Maier-Saupe models.

entry.title: Symbolic Density Estimation: A Decompositional Approach

author.name: Angelo Rajendram, Xieting Chu, Vijay Ganesh, Max Fieg, Aishik Ghosh

entry.summary: Introduces AI-Kolmogorov, a framework for Symbolic Density Estimation that combines clustering, nonparametric estimation, and symbolic regression to discover interpretable density functions, demonstrated on physics-motivated distributions.

entry.title: Anthropomorphism and Trust in Human-Large Language Model interactions

author.name: Akila Kadambi, Ylenia D'Elia, Tanishka Shah, Iulia Comsa, Alison Lentz, Katie Siri-Ngammuang, Tara Buechler, Jonas Kaplan, Antonio Damasio, Srini Narayanan, Lisa Aziz-Zadeh

entry.summary: Studies how people anthropomorphize and trust LLMs across 2,000+ interactions, finding that warmth and cognitive empathy most strongly predict anthropomorphism and trust, while competence predicts all outcomes except anthropomorphism.

entry.title: Foundation Models in Robotics: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Models, Datasets, Challenges and Future Research Directions

author.name: Aggelos Psiris, Vasileios Argyriou, Evangelos K. Markakis, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis, Efstratios Gavves, Kostas Bekris, Arash Ajoudani adn Georgios Th. Papadopoulos

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of foundation models in robotics, covering evolution from single-task to general-purpose agents. Reviews multimodal understanding, long-horizon planning, and cross-embodiment generalization.

entry.title: The Semi-Executable Stack: Agentic Software Engineering and the Expanding Scope of SE

author.name: Robert Feldt, Per Lenberg, Julian Frattini, Dhasarathy Parthasarathy

entry.summary: Argues that AI agents don't threaten software engineering but expand its scope to 'semi-executable artifacts' that combine natural language, code, and model behavior, requiring new engineering practices for this expanded stack.

entry.title: CXR-LT 2026 Challenge: Multi-Center Long-Tailed and Zero Shot Chest X-ray Classification

author.name: Hexin Dong, Yi Lin, Pengyu Zhou, Fengnian Zhao, Alan Clint Legasto, Juno Cho, Dohui Kim, Justin Namuk Kim, Mingeon Kim, Sunwoo Kwak, Gabriel Moy\`a-Alcover, Ky Trung Nguyen, Thanh-Huy Nguyen, Ha-Hieu Pham, Huy-Hieu Pham, Huy Le Pham, Nikhileswara Rao Sulake, Aina Tur-Serrano, Ruichi Zhang, Ang Zu, Adam E. Flanders, Zhiyong Lu, Ronald M. Summers, Mingquan Lin, Hao Chen, Yuzhe Yang, George Shih, Yifan Peng

entry.summary: CXR-LT 2026 is a multi-center chest X-ray classification challenge with 145,000+ images addressing long-tailed distribution of pathologies and zero-shot recognition of novel findings, expanding on previous iterations.

entry.title: Imperfectly Cooperative Human-AI Interactions: Comparing the Impacts of Human and AI Attributes in Simulated and User Studies

author.name: Myke C. Cohen, Mingqian Zheng, Neel Bhandari, Hsien-Te Kao, Xuhui Zhou, Daniel Nguyen, Laura Cassani, Maarten Sap, Svitlana Volkova

entry.summary: Compares simulated and human studies of imperfectly cooperative human-AI interactions across hiring negotiations and information-concealing transactions, examining how AI design characteristics interact with human personality traits.

entry.title: CIG: Measuring Conversational Information Gain in Deliberative Dialogues with Semantic Memory Dynamics

author.name: Ming-Bin Chen and Jey Han Lau and Lea Frermann

entry.summary: Introduces Conversational Information Gain (CIG), a framework that measures how each utterance in a deliberative dialogue advances collective understanding by tracking evolving semantic memory of atomic claims. Scores utterances on Novelty, Relevance, and Implication Scope dimensions.

entry.title: Hierarchical Active Inference using Successor Representations

author.name: Prashant Rangarajan, Rajesh P. N. Rao

entry.summary: Proposes hierarchical active inference using successor representations for efficient planning. Combines multi-scale hierarchical representations with successor representations, inspired by brain architectures, for scalable planning in complex environments.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving LLMs Routing

author.name: Xidong Wu, Yukuan Zhang, Yuqiong Ji, Reza Shirkavand, Qian Lou, Shangqian Gao
