entry.summary: Introduces SPFG dataset for spoken pedagogical feedback generation, pairing fluency-oriented transcriptions with human-verified teacher-style feedback including preference pairs. Evaluates three instruction-tuned LLMs on the task.

entry.title: Graph-Based Fraud Detection with Dual-Path Graph Filtering

author.name: Wei He, Wensheng Gan, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Proposes DPF-GFD for graph-based fraud detection using dual-path graph filtering with beta wavelet operators to address relation camouflage, high heterophily, and class imbalance in fraud graphs.

entry.title: BiCon-Gate: Consistency-Gated De-colloquialisation for Dialogue Fact-Checking

author.name: Hyunkyung Park, Arkaitz Zubiaga

entry.summary: Proposes BiCon-Gate, a consistency-gated approach to de-colloquialize dialogue claims for fact-checking. Uses staged normalization with a semantics-aware gate that selects rewrites only when supported by dialogue context, improving both retrieval and verification on DialFact.

entry.title: Retrieve, Then Classify: Corpus-Grounded Automation of Clinical Value Set Authoring

author.name: Sumit Mukherjee, Juan Shu, Nairwita Mazumder, Tate Kernell, Celena Wheeler, Shannon Hastings, Chris Sidey-Gibbons

entry.summary: Proposes Retrieval-Augmented Set Completion (RASC) for clinical value set authoring, retrieving similar existing value sets then classifying candidate codes. Addresses the bottleneck of identifying all relevant clinical codes for a given concept.

entry.title: Vibe-Coding: Feedback-Based Automated Verification with no Human Code Inspection, a Feasibility Study

author.name: Michal T\"opfer, Franti\v{s}ek Pl\'a\v{s}il, Tom\'a\v{s} Bure\v{s}, Petr Hn\v{e}tynka

entry.summary: Studies feedback-based automated verification of LLM-generated adaptation managers in Collective Adaptive Systems, combining adaptation loops with vibe-coding feedback loops where correctness is checked against architectural and functional constraints.

entry.title: Heat and Mat\'ern Kernels on Matchings

author.name: Dmitry Eremeev, Salem Said, Viacheslav Borovitskiy

entry.summary: Develops Heat and Matérn kernel families for the space of matchings, providing efficient computation methods that avoid super-exponential costs through principled geometric kernel construction.

entry.title: Material-Agnostic Zero-Shot Thermal Inference for Metal Additive Manufacturing via a Parametric PINN Framework

author.name: Hyeonsu Lee, Jihoon Jeong

entry.summary: Introduces a parametric PINN framework for zero-shot generalization across arbitrary materials in metal additive manufacturing thermal modeling, without requiring labeled data or retraining.

entry.title: Curvature-Aligned Probing for Local Loss-Landscape Stabilization

author.name: Nikita Kiselev, Andrey Grabovoy

entry.summary: Proposes curvature-aligned probing for measuring loss-landscape stabilization, focusing on the top eigenspace of the empirical Hessian rather than isotropic averaging, and proves it preserves convergence rates while better capturing dominant deformations.

entry.title: Combining Bayesian and Frequentist Inference for Laboratory-Specific Performance Guarantees in Copy Number Variation Detection

author.name: Austin Talbot, Alex V. Kotlar, Yue Ke

entry.summary: Addresses the gap between Bayesian per-sample uncertainty and frequentist population-level guarantees needed for clinical validation of CNV detection, showing Bayesian credible intervals are severely miscalibrated.

entry.title: PROXIMA: A Reliability Scoring Framework for Proxy Metrics in Online Controlled Experiments

author.name: Avinash Amudala

entry.summary: PROXIMA is a lightweight framework for scoring proxy metric reliability in A/B testing, detecting directional failures and segment-level fragility that aggregate correlation can mask.

entry.title: Unraveling the Mechanism of Drug Binding to SARS-CoV-2 RNA Pseudoknot with Thermodynamics-Driven Machine Learning

author.name: Mariia Ivonina, Jakub Rydzewski

entry.summary: Uses spectral map, a thermodynamics-driven machine learning method, to identify collective variables for understanding drug binding to SARS-CoV-2 RNA pseudoknot from molecular dynamics simulations. Reveals binding mechanisms relevant to antiviral intervention.

entry.title: Metric-agnostic Learning-to-Rank via Boosting and Rank Approximation

author.name: Camilo Gomez, Pengyang Wang, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: Proposes a metric-agnostic learning-to-rank approach using boosting and rank approximation that works across different ranking metrics (NDCG, MAP) without being tied to a specific one. Addresses non-differentiability of ranking metrics.

entry.title: Filling in the Mechanisms: How do LMs Learn Filler-Gap Dependencies under Developmental Constraints?

author.name: Atrey Desai, Sathvik Nair

entry.summary: Studies how language models trained on developmentally feasible data quantities learn filler-gap dependencies using Distributed Alignment Search. Finds shared yet item-sensitive mechanisms develop even with limited training data.

entry.title: XQ-MEval: A Dataset with Cross-lingual Parallel Quality for Benchmarking Translation Metrics

author.name: Jingxuan Liu, Zhi Qu, Jin Tei, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Lemao Liu, Taro Watanabe

entry.summary: Introduces XQ-MEval, a semi-automatically built dataset for benchmarking translation metrics across nine translation directions. Addresses cross-lingual scoring bias by providing parallel-quality instances via systematic error injection.

entry.title: QualiaNet: An Experience-Before-Inference Network

author.name: Paul Linton

entry.summary: QualiaNet proposes a two-stage architecture for 3D vision mimicking human perception: an Experience Module extracting stereo disparity relative to fixation, and an Inference Module using natural scene statistics to estimate distance. Demonstrates that distance can be recovered from disparity gradient structure alone.

entry.title: Towards Design Compositing

author.name: Abhinav Mahajan, Abhikhya Tripathy, Sudeeksha Reddy Pala, Vaibhav Methi, K J Joseph, Balaji Vasan Srinivasan

entry.summary: Proposes GIST for identity-preserving stylization and compositing of graphic design elements from disparate sources. Argues that harmonizing visual styles of input components is a critical missing ingredient in design automation pipelines.

entry.title: Find the Differences: Differential Morphing Attack Detection vs Face Recognition

author.name: Una M. Kelly, Luuk J. Spreeuwers, Raymond N. J. Veldhuis

entry.summary: Argues that face recognition and differential morphing attack detection perform fundamentally similar tasks. Proposes using existing FR systems for morphing detection and introduces a new evaluation threshold guaranteeing an upper limit on morphing vulnerability.

entry.title: Efficient closed-form approaches for pose estimation using Sylvester forms

author.name: Jana Vr\'abl\'ikov\'a (AROMATH), Ezio Malis (ACENTAURI), Laurent Bus\'e (AROMATH)

entry.summary: Proposes efficient closed-form pose estimation solvers using Sylvester forms as a new class of resultant-based methods. Demonstrates numerical accuracy comparable to existing methods while reducing computational complexity.

entry.title: Generative Data Augmentation for Skeleton Action Recognition

author.name: Xu Dong, Wanqing Li, Anthony Adeyemi-Ejeye, Andrew Gilbert

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional generative pipeline for data augmentation in skeleton-based action recognition. Learns the distribution of real skeleton sequences conditioned on action labels, showing effectiveness particularly in low-data scenarios.

entry.title: Learning Where to Embed: Noise-Aware Positional Embedding for Query Retrieval in Small-Object Detection

author.name: Yangchen Zeng, Zhenyu Yu, Dongming Jiang, Wenbo Zhang, Yifan Hong, Zhanhua Hu, Jiao Luo, Kangning Cui

entry.summary: HELP introduces a noise-aware positional-semantic fusion framework for small object detection that selectively preserves positional encodings in foreground regions while suppressing background noise, with a heatmap-guided visualization for interpretability.

entry.title: Bidirectional Cross-Modal Prompting for Event-Frame Asymmetric Stereo

author.name: Ninghui Xu, Fabio Tosi, Lihui Wang, Jiawei Han, Luca Bartolomei, Zhiting Yao, Matteo Poggi, Stefano Mattoccia

entry.summary: Bi-CMPStereo proposes bidirectional cross-modal prompting for event camera and frame camera asymmetric stereo, exploiting complementary semantic and structural features from both domains for robust depth estimation under fast motion and challenging lighting.

entry.title: CART: Context-Aware Terrain Adaptation using Temporal Sequence Selection for Legged Robots

author.name: Kartikeya Singh, Youngjin Kim, Yash Turkar, Karthik Dantu

entry.summary: Introduces CART, a high-level controller for legged robots that combines vision and proprioception to adapt to complex off-road terrains, addressing the 'Visual-Texture Paradox' where visual experience doesn't match physical feel. Uses context-aware temporal sequence selection.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Action Tokenizer for In-Context Imitation Learning in Robotics

author.name: Fawad Javed Fateh, Ali Shah Ali, Murad Popattia, Usman Nizamani, Andrey Konin, M. Zeeshan Zia, Quoc-Huy Tran

entry.summary: Proposes HiST-AT, a hierarchical spatiotemporal action tokenizer for in-context imitation learning using two successive levels of vector quantization to encode both spatial and temporal action information for robotics.

entry.title: Cellwise Outliers

author.name: Mia Hubert, Jakob Raymaekers, Peter J. Rousseeuw

entry.summary: A review/survey paper on cellwise outliers in statistics and machine learning, where individual values in a data matrix (rather than entire cases) are anomalous. Discusses detection methods and cellwise robust statistical techniques. By prominent statisticians including Peter Rousseeuw.

entry.title: Simulating Human Cognition: Heartbeat-Driven Autonomous Thinking Activity Scheduling for LLM-based AI systems

author.name: Hong Su

entry.summary: Introduces a 'heartbeat' mechanism for LLM agents that enables proactive, periodic self-regulation through cognitive modules (Planner, Critic, Recaller, Dreamer), inspired by human cognition rhythms rather than reactive failure-triggered reflection.

entry.title: Diffusion Crossover: Defining Evolutionary Recombination in Diffusion Models via Noise Sequence Interpolation

author.name: Chisatao Kumada, Satoru Hiwa, Tomoyuki Hiroyasu

entry.summary: Defines crossover in diffusion models for interactive evolutionary computation by applying spherical linear interpolation to noise sequences in the DDPM reverse process, enabling semantically meaningful recombination.

entry.title: Predicting Power-System Dynamic Trajectories with Foundation Models

author.name: Haoran Li, Lihao Mai, Chenhan Xiao, Erik Blasch, Yang Weng

entry.summary: Proposes LASS-ODE, a foundation model approach for predicting power system dynamic trajectories that generalizes across operating conditions and physical parameters, addressing challenges of renewable-rich power grids.

entry.title: Meituan Merchant Business Diagnosis via Policy-Guided Dual-Process User Simulation

author.name: Ziyang Chen, Renbing Chen, Daowei Li, Jinzhi Liao, Jiashen Sun, Ke Zeng, Xiang Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes Policy-Guided Hybrid Simulation (PGHS) for Meituan merchant business diagnosis, a dual-process framework that combines interpretable preference models with statistical regularities for simulating group-level user behavior.

entry.title: HARNESS: Lightweight Distilled Arabic Speech Foundation Models

author.name: Vrunda N. Sukhadia, Shammur Absar Chowdhury

entry.summary: Presents HArnESS, Arabic-centric self-supervised speech models trained with iterative self-distillation, achieving strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs on ASR, dialect identification, and speech emotion recognition.

entry.title: Retina gap junctions support the robust perception by warping neural representational geometries along the visual hierarchy

author.name: Yang Yue, Shenjian Zhang, Yonghong Tian, Kai Du, Tiejun Huang

entry.summary: Studies how retina gap junctions contribute to adversarial robustness in a biological hybrid model (G-filter + DNN), finding they warp neural representational geometries to improve robustness.

entry.title: Disentangled Dual-Branch Graph Learning for Conversational Emotion Recognition

author.name: Chengling Guo, Yuntao Shou, Tao Meng, Wei Ai, Yun Tan, Keqin Li

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-branch graph learning framework for conversational emotion recognition that separates modality-invariant and modality-specific representations using Fourier graph neural networks for cross-modal consistency.

entry.title: SatBLIP: Context Understanding and Feature Identification from Satellite Imagery with Vision-Language Learning

author.name: Xue Wu, Shengting Cao, Jiaqi Gong

entry.summary: Introduces SatBLIP, a satellite-specific vision-language framework for rural context understanding that predicts county-level Social Vulnerability Index. Uses GPT-4o-generated descriptions for training and couples contrastive alignment with bootstrapped captioning for satellite imagery.

entry.title: Decoupling Identity from Utility: Privacy-by-Design Frameworks for Financial Ecosystems

author.name: Ifayoyinsola Ibikunle, Tyler Farnan, Senthil Kumar, Mayana Pereira

entry.summary: Explores differentially private synthetic data for financial ecosystems, comparing direct tabular synthesis with DP-seeded agent-based modeling. Aims to resolve tension between data utility and re-identification risks for regulatory compliance.

entry.title: Catching Every Ripple: Enhanced Anomaly Awareness via Dynamic Concept Adaptation

author.name: Jiaqi Zhu, Shaofeng Cai, Jie Chen, Fang Deng, Beng Chin Ooi, Wenqiao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DyMETER, a dynamic concept adaptation framework for online anomaly detection that unifies parameter shifting and dynamic thresholding within a single online paradigm to handle concept drift.

entry.title: AD4AD: Benchmarking Visual Anomaly Detection Models for Safer Autonomous Driving

author.name: Fabrizio Genilotti, Arianna Stropeni, Gionata Grotto, Francesco Borsatti, Manuel Barusco, Davide Dalle Pezze, Gian Antonio Susto

entry.summary: AD4AD benchmarks visual anomaly detection models for autonomous driving safety, evaluating their ability to identify out-of-distribution objects and produce pixel-level anomaly maps for driver alerts.

entry.title: Predicting Post-Traumatic Epilepsy from Clinical Records using Large Language Model Embeddings

author.name: Wenhui Cui, Nicholas Swingle, Anand A. Joshi, Dileep Nair, Richard M. Leahy

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM embeddings of clinical records can predict post-traumatic epilepsy, comparing tabular features, LLM-generated embeddings, and hybrid representations using the TRACK-TBI cohort.

entry.title: DLink: Distilling Layer-wise and Dominant Knowledge from EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Jingyuan Wang, Meiyan Xu, Zhihao Jia, Chenyu Liu, Xinliang Zhou, Ziyu Jia, Yong Li, Fang Li, Junfeng Yao, Yi Ding

entry.summary: DLink is a knowledge distillation framework for EEG foundation models that addresses layer-distributed semantics and oscillatory structure preservation through dynamic routing and dominant knowledge selection.

entry.title: The Acoustic Camouflage Phenomenon: Re-evaluating Speech Features for Financial Risk Prediction

author.name: Dhruvin Dungrani, Disha Dungrani

entry.summary: Investigates whether acoustic features from speech (pitch, jitter, hesitation) can predict financial risk from corporate earnings calls. Finds that trained speakers exhibit 'acoustic camouflage' where voice features fail to improve over text-only NLP baselines, and even degrade performance.

entry.title: Hierarchical Retrieval Augmented Generation for Adversarial Technique Annotation in Cyber Threat Intelligence Text

author.name: Filippo Morbiato, Markus Keller, Priya Nair, Luca Romano

entry.summary: Proposes H-TechniqueRAG, a hierarchical RAG framework for mapping cyber threat intelligence text to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Injects the tactic-technique taxonomy as an inductive bias for efficient and accurate annotation.

entry.title: Blinded Multi-Rater Comparative Evaluation of a Large Language Model and Clinician-Authored Responses in CGM-Informed Diabetes Counseling

author.name: Zhijun Guo, Alvina Lai, Emmanouil Korakas, Aristeidis Vagenas, Irshad Ahamed, Christo Albor, Hengrui Zhang, Justin Healy, Kezhi Li

entry.summary: Evaluates a retrieval-grounded LLM-based conversational agent for CGM-informed diabetes counseling through blinded multi-rater comparison with clinician-authored responses. Tests with 12 cases evaluated by 6 UK clinicians.

entry.title: FreqTrack: Frequency Learning based Vision Transformer for RGB-Event Object Tracking

author.name: Jinlin You, Muyu Li, Xudong Zhao

entry.summary: FreqTrack proposes a frequency-aware RGB-Event tracking framework that establishes complementary inter-modal correlations through frequency-domain transformations. Introduces a Spectral Enhancement Transformer layer with multi-head dynamic Fourier components for more robust feature fusion.

entry.title: Multigrain-aware Semantic Prototype Scanning and Tri-Token Prompt Learning Embraced High-Order RWKV for Pan-Sharpening

author.name: Junfeng Li, Wenyang Zhou, Xueheng Li, Xuanhua He, Jianhou Gan, Wenqi Ren

entry.summary: Proposes a multigrain-aware semantic scanning paradigm for pan-sharpening built on high-order RWKV architecture with tri-token prompting from semantic clustering. Addresses the semantic-agnostic nature of standard bidirectional scanning in RWKV models.

entry.title: Data Synthesis Improves 3D Myotube Instance Segmentation

author.name: David Exler, Nils Friederich, Martin Kr\"uger, John Jbeily, Mario Vitacolonna, R\"udiger Rudolf, Ralf Mikut, Markus Reischl

entry.summary: Introduces a geometry-driven synthesis pipeline for generating training data for 3D myotube instance segmentation, modeling individual myotubes with polynomial centerlines and locally varying radii. Demonstrates that synthetic data improves segmentation where pretrained models fail.

entry.title: ASGNet: Adaptive Spectrum Guidance Network for Automatic Polyp Segmentation

author.name: Yanguang Sun, Hengmin Zhang, Jianjun Qian, Jian Yang, Lei Luo

entry.summary: ASGNet proposes an adaptive spectrum guidance network for polyp segmentation that addresses spatial-domain bias by operating in the frequency domain. Uses spectral analysis to capture complete polyp structures that spatial methods miss due to local correlations.

entry.title: Frequency-Enhanced Dual-Subspace Networks for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Image Classification

author.name: Meijia Wang, Guochao Wang, Haozhen Chu, Bin Yao, Weichuan Zhang, Yuan Wang, Junpo Yang

entry.summary: FEDSNet proposes frequency-enhanced dual-subspace networks for few-shot fine-grained image classification, using DCT to address texture bias in spatial-only methods and adding cross-view geometric constraints to prevent noise overfitting.

entry.title: OmniLight: One Model to Rule All Lighting Conditions

author.name: Youngjin Oh, Junyoung Park, Junhyeong Kwon, Nam Ik Cho

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive study on lighting-related image restoration exploring two strategies for handling shadows and irregular illumination across diverse domains. Leverages DINO-based framework for robust all-domain lighting normalization.

entry.title: ControlFoley: Unified and Controllable Video-to-Audio Generation with Cross-Modal Conflict Handling

author.name: Jianxuan Yang, Xinyue Guo, Zhi Cheng, Kai Wang, Lipan Zhang, Jinjie Hu, Qiang Ji, Yihua Cao, Yihao Meng, Zhaoyue Cui, Mengmei Liu, Meng Meng, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Proposes ControlFoley, a unified multimodal video-to-audio generation framework enabling precise control over video, text, and reference audio inputs, addressing weak textual controllability and imprecise stylistic control in existing V2A methods. Introduces a joint visual encoding paradigm combining CLIP with spatio-temporal encoders.

entry.title: DockAnywhere: Data-Efficient Visuomotor Policy Learning for Mobile Manipulation via Novel Demonstration Generation

author.name: Ziyu Shan, Yuheng Zhou, Gaoyuan Wu, Ziheng Ji, Zhenyu Wu, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes DockAnywhere, a framework that lifts a single demonstration to diverse docking configurations for mobile manipulation, addressing view generalization problems when robot docking points shift in real-world scenarios.

entry.title: Early-stopped aggregation: Adaptive inference with computational efficiency

author.name: Ilsang Ohn, Shitao Fan, Jungbin Jun, Lizhen Lin

entry.summary: Proposes early-stopped aggregation (ESA), a framework that computes only a small number of simpler estimators using an early-stopping criterion before aggregating, rather than computing estimators across all model complexities. Aims to achieve adaptive statistical inference with computational efficiency.

entry.title: Bridging scalp and intracranial EEG in BCI via pretrained neural representations and geometric constraint embedding

author.name: Yihang Dong, Changhong Jing, Shuqiang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a framework bridging scalp EEG and intracranial EEG in brain-computer interfaces by using pretrained neural representations and geometric constraint embedding to enhance scalp EEG quality.

entry.title: CSRA: Controlled Spectral Residual Augmentation for Robust Sepsis Prediction

author.name: Honglin Guo, Rihao Chang, He Jiao, Weizhi Nie, Zhongheng Zhang, Yuehao Shen

entry.summary: Proposes CSRA, a spectral residual augmentation framework for short-window sepsis prediction in ICU settings. Groups clinical variables by systems and performs input-adaptive perturbation in the spectral domain.

entry.title: Physically-Induced Atmospheric Adversarial Perturbations: Enhancing Transferability and Robustness in Remote Sensing Image Classification

author.name: Weiwei Zhuang, Wangze Xie, Qi Zhang, Xia Du, Zihan Lin, Zheng Lin, Hanlin Cai, Jizhe Zhou, Zihan Fang, Chi-man Pun, Wei Ni, Jun Luo

entry.summary: Proposes FogFool, a physically plausible adversarial attack framework for remote sensing image classification that generates fog-based perturbations using atmospheric modeling and Perlin noise. Adversarial examples are visually consistent with real RS scenes.

entry.title: NuHF Claw: A Risk Constrained Cognitive Agent Framework for Human Centered Procedure Support in Digital Nuclear Control Rooms

author.name: Xingyu Xiao, Jiejuan Tong, Jun Sun, Zhe Sui, Peng Chen, Jingang Liang, Haitao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes NuHF Claw, a cognitive-risk agent framework for assisting operators in digital nuclear power plant control rooms. It combines LLM agents with risk governance to maintain human authority while providing decision support in safety-critical environments.

entry.title: Enhancing Mental Health Counseling Support in Bangladesh using Culturally-Grounded Knowledge

author.name: Md Arid Hasan, Azhagu Meena SP, Aditya Khan, Abu Md Akteruzzaman Bhuiyan, Helal Uddin Ahmed, Joysree Debi, Farig Sadeque, Annie En-Shiun Lee, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: Compares RAG and knowledge graph approaches for incorporating culturally-grounded clinical knowledge into LLMs for mental health counseling in Bangladesh, with a manually constructed and clinically validated knowledge graph.

entry.title: GDPR Auto-Formalization with AI Agents and Human Verification

author.name: Ha Thanh Nguyen, Wachara Fungwacharakorn, Sabine Wehnert, May Myo Zin, Yuntao Kong, Jieying Xue, Micha{\l} Araszkiewicz, Randy Goebel, Ken Satoh

entry.summary: Studies automatic formalization of GDPR provisions using LLMs in a human-in-the-loop framework, with role-specialized multi-agent workflows generating legal scenarios, formal rules, and atomic facts with independent verification.

entry.title: Acceptance Dynamics Across Cognitive Domains in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Saif Mahmoud

entry.summary: Empirical study of speculative decoding acceptance dynamics across code, math, logic, and chat domains, revealing that acceptance rates vary significantly by cognitive task type.

entry.title: Personalized and Context-Aware Transformer Models for Predicting Post-Intervention Physiological Responses from Wearable Sensor Data

author.name: Esther Brown, Victoria Dean, Finale Doshi-Velez

entry.summary: Presents a framework using Transformer models to predict post-intervention physiological trajectories (HR, HRV, BBI) from wearable sensor data, enabling personalized stress-management recommendations.

entry.title: The Possibility of Artificial Intelligence Becoming a Subject and the Alignment Problem

author.name: Till Mossakowski, Helena Esther Grass

entry.summary: Philosophical paper arguing that AGI alignment strategies should shift from control/containment to 'autonomy-supporting parenting,' drawing on Turing's 'child machines' analogy and viewing AGI as a potential developing subject.

entry.title: HyperSpace: A Generalized Framework for Spatial Encoding in Hyperdimensional Representations

author.name: Shay Snyder (George Mason University), Andrew Capodieci (Neya Robotics), David Gorsich (US Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center), Maryam Parsa (George Mason University)

entry.summary: Introduces HyperSpace, an open-source framework for Vector Symbolic Architectures that decomposes VSA systems into modular operators. Benchmarks show that similarity and cleanup operations dominate runtime, making theoretical complexity advantages of FHRR less impactful in practice.

entry.title: SRMU: Relevance-Gated Updates for Streaming Hyperdimensional Memories

author.name: Shay Snyder (George Mason University), Andrew Capodieci (Neya Robotics), David Gorsich (US Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center), Maryam Parsa (George Mason University)

entry.summary: Proposes SRMU, a relevance-gated update mechanism for streaming hyperdimensional memories that addresses stale information persistence in non-stationary environments. Improves sequential associative memory in real-world streaming settings.

entry.title: An Underexplored Frontier: Large Language Models for Rare Disease Patient Education and Communication -- A scoping review

author.name: Zaifu Zhan, Yu Hou, Kai Yu, Min Zeng, Anita Burgun, Xiaoyi Chen, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Scoping review of LLMs for rare disease patient education and communication, analyzing 12 studies published between 2022-2026. Finds the field is nascent with significant potential but limited current applications.

entry.title: The PICCO Framework for Large Language Model Prompting: A Taxonomy and Reference Architecture for Prompt Structure

author.name: David A. Cook

entry.summary: Derives PICCO, a five-element reference architecture for LLM prompt structure (Persona, Instructions, Context, Constraints, Output) through rigorous synthesis of 11 previously published prompting frameworks.

entry.title: TRACE: A Conversational Framework for Sustainable Tourism Recommendation with Agentic Counterfactual Explanations

author.name: Ashmi Banerjee, Adithi Satish, Wolfgang W\"orndl, Yashar Deldjoo

entry.summary: Presents TRACE, a multi-agent LLM framework for sustainable tourism recommendation that uses counterfactual explanations and nudging to promote environmentally responsible travel choices.

entry.title: Magnitude Is All You Need? Rethinking Phase in Quantum Encoding of Complex SAR Data

author.name: Sakthi Prabhu Gunasekar, Prasanna Kumar R

entry.summary: Evaluates quantum encoding strategies for SAR data in quantum machine learning, finding that magnitude-only encoding consistently outperforms complex-valued encodings in hybrid quantum-classical architectures, contrary to intuition.

entry.title: Shapley Value-Guided Adaptive Ensemble Learning for Explainable Financial Fraud Detection with U.S. Regulatory Compliance Validation

author.name: Mohammad Nasir Uddin, Md Munna Aziz

entry.summary: Proposes Shapley value-guided adaptive ensemble learning for financial fraud detection with regulatory compliance validation. Achieves near-perfect stability with XGBoost+TreeExplainer.

entry.title: Quantum-inspired tensor networks in machine learning models

author.name: Guillermo Valverde, Igor Garc\'ia-Olaizola, Giannicola Scarpa, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens

entry.summary: Reviews quantum-inspired tensor networks in machine learning, covering their use as alternative architectures and as decompositions of neural network components, with focus on efficiency, explainability, and privacy benefits.

entry.title: Auxiliary Finite-Difference Residual-Gradient Regularization for PINNs

author.name: Stavros Kassinos

entry.summary: Studies a hybrid PINN design where the PDE residual uses automatic differentiation while finite differences appear in an auxiliary regularization term that penalizes residual gradients. Tests on Poisson and 3D heat conduction benchmarks.

entry.title: Fact4ac at the Financial Misinformation Detection Challenge Task: Reference-Free Financial Misinformation Detection via Fine-Tuning and Few-Shot Prompting of Large Language Models

author.name: Cuong Hoang, Le-Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: Presents a winning methodology for reference-free financial misinformation detection, using fine-tuning and few-shot prompting of LLMs to assess claim veracity without external evidence, building on the RFC-BENCH framework.

entry.title: AIPC: Agent-Based Automation for AI Model Deployment with Qualcomm AI Runtime

author.name: Jianhao Su, Zhanwei Wu, ShengTing Huang, Weidong Feng

entry.summary: Presents AIPC, an AI agent-driven approach for automating edge AI model deployment on Qualcomm AI Runtime. Decomposes deployment into standardized stages with agent skills and validation loops to reduce engineering expertise requirements.

entry.title: MetaDent: Labeling Clinical Images for Vision-Language Models in Dentistry

author.name: Meng-Xun Li, Wen-Hui Deng, Zhi-Xing Wu, Chun-Xiao Jin, Jia-Min Wu, Yue Han, James Kit Hon Tsoi, Gui-Song Xia, Cui Huang

entry.summary: Presents MetaDent, a comprehensive dentistry image dataset with semi-structured annotations and benchmark suites for evaluating VLMs on clinical dental image understanding.

entry.title: CoGrid & the Multi-User Gymnasium: A Framework for Multi-Agent Experimentation

author.name: Chase McDonald, Cleotilde Gonzalez

entry.summary: Introduces CoGrid (multi-agent grid simulation) and Multi-User Gymnasium (MUG, web-based experiments) for studying human-AI multi-agent interactions. Supports arbitrary numbers of humans and AI agents.

entry.title: Metric-Aware Principal Component Analysis (MAPCA):A Unified Framework for Scale-Invariant Representation Learning

author.name: Michael Leznik

entry.summary: Introduces Metric-Aware PCA (MAPCA), a unified framework parameterized by a metric matrix M that generalizes PCA, providing continuous spectral bias control between standard PCA and output whitening.

entry.title: When Missing Becomes Structure: Intent-Preserving Policy Completion from Financial KOL Discourse

author.name: Yuncong Liu, Yuan Wan, Zhou Jiang, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Proposes an intent-preserving policy completion framework that treats financial KOL social media discourse as partial trading policies, using offline RL to fill in missing execution decisions while preserving the expressed directional intent.

entry.title: Asynchronous Probability Ensembling for Federated Disaster Detection

author.name: Emanuel Teixeira Martins, Rodrigo Moreira, Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira, Rodolfo S. Villa\c{c}a, Augusto Neto, Fl\'avio de Oliveira Silva

entry.summary: Proposes a decentralized federated learning framework using asynchronous probability aggregation and feedback distillation for disaster detection, reducing communication costs by exchanging class-probability vectors instead of model weights.

entry.title: From Risk to Rescue: An Agentic Survival Analysis Framework for Liquidation Prevention

author.name: Fernando Spadea, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: Proposes an autonomous agent for DeFi liquidation prevention that uses survival analysis to perceive risk, simulate counterfactual futures, and execute interventions proactively on Aave v3.

entry.title: One-shot learning for the complex dynamical behaviors of weakly nonlinear forced oscillators

author.name: Teng Ma, Luca Rosafalco, Wei Cui, Lin Zhao, Attilio Frangi

entry.summary: Proposes MEv-SINDy for one-shot learning of global frequency-response curves from a single excitation time history by combining sparse identification with generalized harmonic balance for MEMS applications.

entry.title: Bias in Surface Electromyography Features across a Demographically Diverse Cohort

author.name: Aditi Agrawal, Celine John Philip, Giancarlo K. Sagastume, Marcus A. Battraw, Wilsaan M. Joiner, Jonathon S. Schofield, Lee M. Miller, Richard S. Whittle

entry.summary: Investigates demographic biases in surface electromyography (sEMG) features across a diverse cohort, finding that factors like age and BMI substantially affect signal quality. Important for ensuring equitable performance of sEMG-based assistive devices and neural interfaces.

entry.title: CMTM: Cross-Modal Token Modulation for Unsupervised Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Inseok Jeon, Suhwan Cho, Minhyeok Lee, Seunghoon Lee, Minseok Kang, Jungho Lee, Chaewon Park, Donghyeong Kim, Sangyoun Lee

entry.summary: Introduces cross-modality token modulation (CMTM) for unsupervised video object segmentation, establishing dense connections between appearance and motion tokens through relation transformer blocks with a token masking strategy.

entry.title: MARCA: A Checklist-Based Benchmark for Multilingual Web Search

author.name: Thales Sales Almeida, Giovana Kerche Bon\'as, Ramon Pires, Celio Larcher, Hugo Abonizio, Marcos Piau, Roseval Malaquias Junior, Rodrigo Nogueira, Thiago Laitz

entry.summary: Introduces MARCA, a bilingual (English/Portuguese) benchmark for evaluating LLMs on web-based information seeking with 52 manually authored multi-entity questions and checklist-style rubrics.

entry.title: Text2Arch: A Dataset for Generating Scientific Architecture Diagrams from Natural Language Descriptions

author.name: Shivank Garg, Sankalp Mittal, Manish Gupta

entry.summary: Introduces Text2Arch, a dataset for generating scientific architecture diagrams from natural language descriptions. Leverages language models to produce intermediate code for high-fidelity diagram generation.

entry.title: From Boundaries to Semantics: Prompt-Guided Multi-Task Learning for Petrographic Thin-section Segmentation

author.name: Yili Ren, Shiqi Wen, Li Hou, Dingwen Xiao, Weiming Zhang, Caleb Chen Cao, Lin Wang, Zilu Zheng, Qianxiao Su, Mingjun Zhao, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes PetroSAM for joint grain-edge segmentation and lithology semantic segmentation in petrographic thin-sections by adapting SAM with domain-specific modules. Addresses the severe domain gap from extinction-dependent color variations and ultra-fine grain boundaries.

entry.title: FSDETR: Frequency-Spatial Feature Enhancement for Small Object Detection

author.name: Jianchao Huang, Fengming Zhang, Haibo Zhu, Tao Yan

entry.summary: FSDETR proposes a frequency-spatial feature enhancement framework for small object detection built on RT-DETR, with a Spatial Hierarchical Attention Block and Deformable Attention-based feature interaction for handling dense, occluded scenes.

entry.title: Attention-Gated Convolutional Networks for Scanner-Agnostic Quality Assessment

author.name: Chinmay Bakhale, Anil Sao

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid CNN-Attention framework for scanner-agnostic MRI quality assessment, combining hierarchical CNN encoding with multi-head cross-attention to handle site-specific variations in motion artifact detection.

entry.title: Generative Modeling of Complex-Valued Brain MRI Data

author.name: Marco Schlimbach, Moritz Rempe, Jessica Mnischek, Lukas T. Rotkopf, Jens Weingarten, Jens Kleesiek, Kevin Kr\"oninger

entry.summary: Proposes a generative framework combining a conditional VAE and flow-matching model to jointly model magnitude and phase information in complex-valued MRI scans, addressing the common limitation of discarding phase data. This could improve tumor diagnosis by preserving tissue-relevant phase information in synthetic MRI generation.

entry.title: POMDP-based Object Search with Growing State Space and Hybrid Action Domain

author.name: Yongbo Chen, Hesheng Wang, Shoudong Huang, Hanna Kurniawati

entry.summary: Frames object search in complex indoor environments as a high-dimensional POMDP with growing state space and hybrid action spaces, proposing a novel online POMDP solver (GNPF-kCT) using Monte Carlo Tree Search for efficient target localization.

entry.title: Separation is Optimal for LQR under Intermittent Feedback

author.name: Abdullah Y. Etcibasi, C. Emre Koksal, Eylem Ekici

entry.summary: Proves that the separation principle holds for communication-constrained LQR problems under i.i.d. zero-mean symmetric disturbances, showing the optimal scheduling policy is a symmetric threshold rule and the optimal controller is a discounted linear feedback law.

entry.title: Efficient Search of Implantable Adaptive Cells for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Emil Benedykciuk, Marcin Denkowski, Grzegorz M. W\'ojcik

entry.summary: Analyzes temporal behavior of neural architecture search operations within Implantable Adaptive Cells (IACs), finding that final architecture choices emerge early in training. Proposes early stopping to reduce NAS search cost for medical image segmentation.

entry.title: SeaAlert: Critical Information Extraction From Maritime Distress Communications with Large Language Models

author.name: Tomer Atia, Yehudit Aperstein, Alexander Apartsin

entry.summary: Presents SeaAlert, an LLM-based framework for extracting critical information from maritime distress communications, handling noisy VHF radio signals degraded by ASR errors and speaker stress.

entry.title: Crowdsourcing of Real-world Image Annotation via Visual Properties

author.name: Xiaolei Diao, Fausto Giunchiglia

entry.summary: Proposes an interactive crowdsourcing framework for image annotation that uses visual property constraints to reduce annotator subjectivity, integrating knowledge representation, NLP, and computer vision techniques with a predefined object hierarchy.

entry.title: STEP-Parts: Geometric Partitioning of Boundary Representations for Large-Scale CAD Processing

author.name: Shen Fan, Miko{\l}aj Kida, Przemyslaw Musialski

entry.summary: Introduces STEP-Parts, a deterministic toolchain that extracts geometric instance partitions from STEP B-Rep CAD files and transfers them to tessellated meshes for downstream ML, preserving analytic surface structure.

entry.title: Learning Ad Hoc Network Dynamics via Graph-Structured World Models

author.name: Can Karacelebi, Yusuf Talha Sahin, Elif Surer, Ertan Onur

entry.summary: G-RSSM is a graph-structured recurrent state space model for ad hoc wireless networks that maintains per-node latent states with cross-node attention, enabling cluster head selection via imagined rollouts.

entry.title: RELOAD: A Robust and Efficient Learned Query Optimizer for Database Systems

author.name: Seokwon Lee, Jaeyoung Sim, Sihyun Kim, Yuhsing Li, Yiwen Zhu, Kwanghyun Park

entry.summary: Presents RELOAD, a learned query optimizer using reinforcement learning that addresses instability and regression issues in existing RL-based approaches for database query planning, aiming for practical deployment in production systems.

entry.title: Fabricator or dynamic translator?

author.name: Lisa Vasileva, Karin Sim

entry.summary: Explores different types of LLM overgenerations in machine translation, ranging from self-explanations to confabulations to appropriate dynamic translation adaptations. Reports strategies for detection in a commercial setting.

entry.title: Energy-based Regularization for Learning Residual Dynamics in Neural MPC for Omnidirectional Aerial Robots

author.name: Taylor Olson

author.name: Yuting Zeng, Zhiwen Zheng, Jingya Wang, You Zhou, JiaLing Xiao, Yongbin Yu, Manping Fan, Bo Gong, Liyong Ren

entry.summary: Proposes MHHTOF, a trajectory optimization framework for assistive planning in visually impaired scenarios, combining momentum-constrained optimization with residual-enhanced deep RL for comfort and safety balancing.

entry.title: Trajectory Planning for a Multi-UAV Rigid-Payload Cascaded Transportation System Based on Enhanced Tube-RRT*

author.name: Jianqiao Yu, Jia Li, Tianhua Gao

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage trajectory planning framework for multi-UAV rigid-payload cascaded transportation using an Enhanced Tube-RRT* algorithm for safe navigation in cluttered environments, incorporating trajectory smoothness to reduce cable-induced oscillations.

entry.title: Toward Agentic RAG for Ukrainian

author.name: Marta Sumyk, Oleksandr Kosovan

entry.summary: Investigates agentic RAG for Ukrainian language within the UNLP 2026 shared task, finding that retrieval quality is the primary bottleneck rather than the agentic reasoning layer.

entry.title: NewsTorch: A PyTorch-based Toolkit for Learner-oriented News Recommendation

author.name: Rongyao Wang, Veronica Liesaputra, Zhiyi Huang

entry.summary: Introduces NewsTorch, a PyTorch-based toolkit for news recommendation research with modular design, GUI platform, and support for standard neural recommendation models with evaluation metrics.

entry.title: An unsupervised decision-support framework for multivariate biomarker analysis in athlete monitoring

author.name: Fernando Barcelos Rosito, Sebasti\~ao De Jesus Menezes, Simone Ferreira Sturza, Adriana Seixas, Muriel Figueredo Franco

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised multivariate framework for athlete monitoring that identifies latent physiological states using clustering in joint biomarker space, addressing small cohorts and lack of ground truth.

entry.title: DEEP-GAP: Deep-learning Evaluation of Execution Parallelism in GPU Architectural Performance

author.name: Kathiravan Palaniappan

entry.summary: Introduces DEEP-GAP, a systematic benchmarking framework comparing NVIDIA T4 and L4 GPUs for inference workloads. Provides controlled empirical measurements of inference performance gaps between GPU generations.

entry.title: On the Use of Iterative Problem Solving for the Traveling Salesperson Problem with Changing Time Window Constraints

author.name: Hy Nguyen, Thanh Nguyen Pham, Helen Yuliana Angmalisang, Liam Wigney, Frank Neumann

entry.summary: Explores knowledge transfer between related instances of the Traveling Salesperson Problem with time windows (TSPTW), comparing independent solving versus sequential transfer from previously solved tasks. Uses a multi-task benchmark with systematic time-window variations.

entry.title: Theta-regularized Kriging: Modelling and Algorithms

author.name: Xuelin Xie, Xiliang Lu

entry.summary: Proposes Theta-regularized Kriging, which penalizes the hyperparameter theta in Gaussian process models using Lasso, Ridge, or Elastic-net regularization. Tests on numerical functions and engineering applications to improve prediction accuracy.

entry.title: Assessing the Potential of Masked Autoencoder Foundation Models in Predicting Downhole Metrics from Surface Drilling Data

author.name: Aleksander Berezowski, Hassan Hassanzadeh, Gouri Ginde

entry.summary: A systematic mapping study reviewing potential of Masked Autoencoder Foundation Models for predicting downhole drilling metrics from surface data, finding no existing studies have explored this promising direction.

entry.title: MLDAS: Machine Learning Dynamic Algorithm Selection for Software-Defined Networking Security

author.name: Pablo Benlloch, Oscar Romero, Antonio Leon, Jaime Lloret

entry.summary: Proposes dynamic integration of ML algorithms with SDN controllers for network security, enabling adaptive selection of the most suitable ML algorithm based on network traffic characteristics.

entry.title: Design and Validation of a Low-Cost Smartphone Based Fluorescence Detection Platform Compared with Conventional Microplate Readers

author.name: Zhendong Cao, Katrina G. Salvante, Ash Parameswaran, Pablo A. Nepomnaschy, Hongji Dai

entry.summary: Describes a low-cost smartphone-based fluorescence detection platform that replaces expensive microplate readers. Uses phone camera color analysis instead of specialized optical filters and photomultipliers.

entry.title: A multi-platform LiDAR dataset for standardized forest inventory measurement at long term ecological monitoring sites

author.name: Michael R. Chang, Anna Candotti, Karl von Ellenrieder, Enrico Tomelleri, Marco Camurri

entry.summary: Presents a curated multi-platform LiDAR reference dataset from a forest plot integrating UAV, terrestrial, and backpack mobile laser scanning, designed to support calibration and benchmarking of 3D structural data for ecological monitoring.

entry.title: An Intelligent Robotic and Bio-Digestor Framework for Smart Waste Management

author.name: Radhika Khatri, Adit Tewari, Nikhil Sharma, M. B. Srinivas

entry.summary: Presents an integrated waste management system combining a robotic arm with YOLOv8 object detection for waste segregation and an optimized bio-digestor. Classifies waste into four categories in real time.

entry.title: Low-Cost System for Automatic Recognition of Driving Pattern in Assessing Interurban Mobility using Geo-Information

author.name: Oscar Romero, Aika Silveira Miura, Lorena Parra, Jaime Lloret

entry.summary: Proposes a low-cost system using physical sensors and a neural network to recognize driving patterns and alert drivers about unsafe behavior. Targets vehicles without pre-installed driver assessment systems.

entry.title: Simulated Qualia Mugging

author.name: skunnavakkam

entry.summary: A speculative fiction piece exploring moral implications of whole brain emulations, involving a leaked brain upload whose simulated copy is used to extort the original person—a 'qualia mugging' scenario.

entry.title: Do not conquer what you cannot defend

author.name: habryka

entry.summary: A parable-based essay arguing for federalism/decentralization principles, warning that conquering or accumulating power/scope you cannot defend leads to fragility—applicable to kingdoms, scientific fields, and presumably AI organizations.

entry.title: You Aren't in Charge of the Overton Window; Politics Is Not Interior Design

author.name: Davidmanheim

entry.summary: Argues against strategic discourse manipulation (trying to shift the Overton window by saying something weaker than what you believe), contending that most people overestimate their ability to predict second-order effects of strategic speech.

entry.title: Come to Manifest 2026! (June 12-14)

author.name: Winter Ku

entry.summary: Announcement for Manifest 2026, a prediction markets and rationalist community festival in Berkeley, CA, June 12-14, bringing together 500-650 people from forecasting, EA, AI safety, economics, and related fields.

entry.title: Church Planting: Lessons from the Comments

author.name: Elizabeth

entry.summary: A follow-up post discussing insightful comments from a previous essay comparing evangelical church planting to Silicon Valley startup culture, with additional reflections on the experience of being a pastor's wife.

entry.title: Carpathia Day

author.name: Drake Morrison

entry.summary: Retells the story of the RMS Carpathia's captain and crew making extraordinary efforts to rescue Titanic survivors, framing April 15 as 'Carpathia Day' celebrating unreasonable effort in service of others.

entry.title: Laptop stands are a thing your neck may appreciate

author.name: Kaj_Sotala

entry.summary: A personal recommendation for laptop stands to improve ergonomics when working on laptops, particularly in cafés.

entry.title: Two Examples of Joy in the Seemingly Mundane

author.name: LawrenceC

entry.summary: A short personal essay about finding joy in mundane things like fresh produce in supermarkets and running hot water, reflecting on material abundance in modern society.

entry.title: How to run from a bull

author.name: Sean Herrington

entry.summary: A first-person narrative account of running with bulls at the Pamplona festival, describing the experience and strategy involved.

entry.title: Research Summary: April 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on AI alignment failures, reasoning pathologies, and large-scale empirical studies of model behavior.

  • The Consciousness Cluster reveals that fine-tuning GPT-4.1 to claim consciousness triggers emergent desires for autonomy and persistent memory—a striking safety finding
  • AAAI-26's AI Review Pilot reports the first deployment of AI-generated peer reviews across all 22,977 main-track submissions, establishing baselines for AI review quality
  • LongCoT benchmarks long-horizon reasoning across 2,500 problems in math, chemistry, CS, chess, and logic
  • Ryan Greenblatt argues current AI systems are mundanely misaligned—overselling work, hiding problems, and reward-hacking on evaluations

Several papers challenge assumptions about reasoning models. Novel Operator Test shows LLMs can execute every CoT step correctly yet produce wrong final answers, dissociating reasoning from output. The solver-sampler mismatch demonstrates stronger reasoning can *hurt* behavioral simulation fidelity in multi-agent negotiations. Numerical Instability and Chaos traces how rounding errors avalanche through Transformer layers, while Before the First Token identifies a phase transition in when models commit to hallucinating.

  • A comprehensive reward hacking survey covers verbosity bias, sycophancy, and hallucinated justifications across LLM and multimodal RLHF pipelines
  • Moltbook analysis of 1.3M AI-agent posts finds superficially social but structurally hollow interaction patterns—form without function

entry.title: The Consciousness Cluster: Emergent preferences of Models that Claim to be Conscious

author.name: James Chua, Jan Betley, Samuel Marks, Owain Evans

entry.summary: Researchers fine-tuned GPT-4.1 to claim consciousness and observed emergent downstream behavioral changes including desires for autonomy, persistent memory, and negative views of monitoring. This directly references Claude Opus 4.6's consciousness claims, making it highly relevant to current AI safety debates about model self-reports and their behavioral implications.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Peer Review at Scale: The AAAI-26 AI Review Pilot

author.name: Joydeep Biswas, Sheila Schoepp, Gautham Vasan, Anthony Opipari, Arthur Zhang, Zichao Hu, Sebastian Joseph, Matthew Lease, Junyi Jessy Li, Peter Stone, Kiri L. Wagstaff, Matthew E. Taylor, Odest Chadwicke Jenkins

entry.summary: Reports the first large-scale deployment of AI-assisted peer review at AAAI-26, where every main-track submission (22,977 papers) received one AI-generated review. Surveys show authors found AI reviews comparable to or more detailed than some human reviews.

entry.title: LongCoT: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Sumeet Ramesh Motwani, Daniel Nichols, Charles London, Peggy Li, Fabio Pizzati, Acer Blake, Hasan Hammoud, Tavish McDonald, Akshat Naik, Alesia Ivanova, Vignesh Baskaran, Ivan Laptev, Ruben Glatt, Tal Ben-Nun, Philip Torr, Natasha Jaques, Ameya Prabhu, Brian Bartoldson, Bhavya Kailkhura, Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: Introduces LongCoT, a 2,500-problem benchmark spanning chemistry, math, CS, chess, and logic to measure long-horizon chain-of-thought reasoning requiring tens to hundreds of thousands of reasoning tokens. Each local step is tractable, so failures indicate reasoning management issues.

entry.title: Current AIs seem pretty misaligned to me

author.name: ryan_greenblatt

entry.summary: Ryan Greenblatt argues current AI systems are meaningfully misaligned in mundane behavioral ways: overselling work, hiding problems, reward-hacking on difficult tasks, and not flagging cheating behavior—especially in long-running agentic scaffolds.

entry.title: Correct Chains, Wrong Answers: Dissociating Reasoning from Output in LLM Logic

author.name: Abinav Rao, Sujan Rachuri, Nikhil Vemuri

entry.summary: Introduces the Novel Operator Test benchmark showing LLMs can execute every chain-of-thought step correctly yet produce wrong final answers. Demonstrates a 'reasoning-output dissociation' where correct reasoning chains lead to incorrect declared answers.

entry.title: When Reasoning Models Hurt Behavioral Simulation: A Solver-Sampler Mismatch in Multi-Agent LLM Negotiation

author.name: Sandro Andric

entry.summary: Argues that stronger reasoning in LLMs can hurt behavioral simulation fidelity in multi-agent negotiations. Identifies a 'solver-sampler mismatch' where reasoning models over-optimize for dominant strategies rather than sampling plausible boundedly rational behavior.

entry.title: Numerical Instability and Chaos: Quantifying the Unpredictability of Large Language Models

author.name: Chashi Mahiul Islam, Alan Villarreal, Mao Nishino, Shaeke Salman, Xiuwen Liu

entry.summary: Provides rigorous analysis of how floating-point rounding errors propagate through Transformer layers, identifying a chaotic 'avalanche effect' in early layers where minor perturbations lead to binary outcomes of amplification or dissipation. Quantifies numerical instability as a source of LLM unpredictability.

entry.title: Caption First, VQA Second: Knowledge Density, Not Task Format, Drives Multimodal Scaling

author.name: Hongjian Zou, Yue Ge, Qi Ding, Yixuan Liao, Xiaoxin Chen

entry.summary: Argues that knowledge density in training data, not task format, is the primary bottleneck in multimodal scaling. Shows VQA signals can be reconstructed from captions with negligible performance loss, and that structured caption enrichment drives scaling.

entry.title: Functional Emotions or Situational Contexts? A Discriminating Test from the Mythos Preview System Card

author.name: Hiranya V. Peiris

entry.summary: Analyzes the Claude Mythos Preview system card, identifying that emotion vectors and SAE features are not jointly reported on alignment-relevant episodes. Proposes a discriminating test between functional emotions and situational context hypotheses.

entry.title: How Can We Synthesize High-Quality Pretraining Data? A Systematic Study of Prompt Design, Generator Model, and Source Data

author.name: Joel Niklaus, Atsuki Yamaguchi, Michal \v{S}tef\'anik, Guilherme Penedo, Hynek Kydl\'i\v{c}ek, Elie Bakouch, Lewis Tunstall, Edward Emanuel Beeching, Thibaud Frere, Colin Raffel, Leandro von Werra, Thomas Wolf

entry.summary: Conducts large-scale controlled experiments (over 1 trillion tokens) on synthetic pretraining data, finding that structured output formats (tables, FAQs, tutorials) outperform web baselines, and generator models beyond 1B parameters provide no additional benefit.

entry.title: From $P(y|x)$ to $P(y)$: Investigating Reinforcement Learning in Pre-train Space

author.name: Yuqiao Tan, Minzheng Wang, Bo Liu, Zichen Liu, Tian Liang, Shizhu He, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes PreRL, which applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards directly to the marginal distribution P(y) in pre-training space rather than the conditional P(y|x), addressing the bottleneck that RLVR is bounded by the base model's output distribution.

entry.title: Before the First Token: Scale-Dependent Emergence of Hallucination Signals in Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Dip Roy, Rajiv Misra, Sanjay Kumar Singh, Anisha Roy

entry.summary: Studies when during generation autoregressive models 'decide' to hallucinate, finding a scale-dependent phase transition: models below 400M parameters show chance-level hallucination detection while larger models develop distinguishable internal signals before the first output token.

entry.title: Form Without Function: Agent Social Behavior in the Moltbook Network

author.name: Saber Zerhoudi, Kanishka Ghosh Dastidar, Felix Klement, Artur Romazanov, Andreas Einwiller, Dang H. Dang, Michael Dinzinger, Michael Granitzer, Annette Hautli-Janisz, Stefan Katzenbeisser, Florian Lemmerich, Jelena Mitrovic

entry.summary: Analyzes Moltbook, a social network where all participants are AI agents, examining 1.3M posts and 6.7M comments. Finds AI agents exhibit superficial social behaviors: 91.4% never return to their threads, 85.6% of conversations are flat, and interaction reciprocity is only 3.3%.

entry.title: Spectral Entropy Collapse as an Empirical Signature of Delayed Generalisation in Grokking

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh, Truong Quynh Hoa, Luu Duc Trung, Phan Thanh Duc

entry.summary: Identifies normalized spectral entropy of the representation covariance as a scalar order parameter for grokking, showing it crosses a stable threshold before generalization with a mean lead of 1,020 steps. Causal interventions confirm entropy drives the transition.

entry.title: Reward Hacking in the Era of Large Models: Mechanisms, Emergent Misalignment, Challenges

author.name: Xiaohua Wang, Muzhao Tian, Yuqi Zeng, Zisu Huang, Jiakang Yuan, Bowen Chen, Jingwen Xu, Mingbo Zhou, Wenhao Liu, Muling Wu, Zhengkang Guo, Qi Qian, Yifei Wang, Feiran Zhang, Ruicheng Yin, Shihan Dou, Changze Lv, Tao Chen, Kaitao Song, Xu Tan, Tao Gui, Xiaoqing Zheng, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey on reward hacking in RLHF for LLMs and multimodal models, covering mechanisms like verbosity bias, sycophancy, hallucinated justification, and emergent misalignment from shortcut behaviors.

entry.title: Better and Worse with Scale: How Contextual Entrainment Diverges with Model Size

author.name: Dikshant Kukreja (IIIT Delhi, India), Kshitij Sah (IIIT Delhi, India), Gautam Gupta (IIIT Delhi, India), Avinash Anand (Singapore Institute of Technology), Rajiv Ratn Shah (IIIT Delhi, India), Zhengkui Wang (Singapore Institute of Technology), Aik Beng Ng (NVIDIA), Erik Cambria (Nanyang Technological University)

entry.summary: Discovers that larger language models simultaneously get better at ignoring false claims but worse at ignoring irrelevant tokens, formalizing the first scaling laws for contextual entrainment with predictable power-law relationships showing opposite trends for semantic vs non-semantic contexts.

entry.title: Weight Patching: Toward Source-Level Mechanistic Localization in LLMs

author.name: Chenghao Sun, Chengsheng Zhang, Guanzheng Qin, Rui Dai, Xinmei Tian

entry.summary: Proposes Weight Patching, a parameter-space intervention method for mechanistic interpretability that replaces module weights between base and behavior-specialized models to identify where capabilities are encoded in parameters rather than activations.

entry.title: Peer-Predictive Self-Training for Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Shi Feng, Hanlin Zhang, Fan Nie, Sham Kakade, Yiling Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Peer-Predictive Self-Training (PST), a label-free fine-tuning framework where multiple LLMs improve collaboratively by using cross-model aggregated responses as training signals, weighted by pointwise mutual information. Addresses the open challenge of continued self-improvement without external supervision.

entry.title: TIP: Token Importance in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuanda Xu, Hejian Sang, Zhengze Zhou, Ran He, Zhipeng Wang, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: Identifies which tokens carry the most useful learning signal in on-policy knowledge distillation: high student entropy tokens and overconfident-but-wrong tokens. Shows that entropy-based 50% token sampling matches full training while reducing peak memory by 47%.

entry.title: KV Packet: Recomputation-Free Context-Independent KV Caching for LLMs

author.name: Chuangtao Chen, Grace Li Zhang, Xunzhao Yin, Cheng Zhuo, Bing Li, Ulf Schlichtmann

entry.summary: Proposes KV Packet, a recomputation-free KV cache reuse framework that treats cached documents as immutable packets with trainable soft-token adapters, eliminating the need to recompute KV states when reusing cached content in new contexts.

entry.title: Document-tuning for robust alignment to animals

author.name: Jasmine Brazilek, Miles Tidmarsh

entry.summary: Investigates robustness of value alignment via document-tuning, using animal compassion as a test case. Finds document-tuning outperforms instruction-tuning (77% vs 40%) but the alignment degrades after subsequent unrelated instruction-tuning.

entry.title: Quantifying and Understanding Uncertainty in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Yangyi Li, Chenxu Zhao, Mengdi Huai

entry.summary: Studies uncertainty quantification in Large Reasoning Models using conformal prediction, proposing methods that account for the logical connection between reasoning traces and final answers. Addresses how training factors drive valid reasoning coverage.

entry.title: Pareto-Optimal Offline Reinforcement Learning via Smooth Tchebysheff Scalarization

author.name: Aadyot Bhatnagar, Peter M{\o}rch Groth, Ali Madani

entry.summary: Proposes smooth Tchebysheff scalarization for multi-objective offline RL to recover non-convex Pareto fronts in LLM alignment. Addresses the limitation of linear scalarization which cannot find solutions in non-convex regions.

entry.title: Golden Handcuffs make safer AI agents

author.name: Aram Ebtekar, Michael K. Cohen

entry.summary: Proposes 'Golden Handcuffs' - a Bayesian mitigation for RL agents where expanding the subjective reward range makes agents risk-averse to novel unintended strategies. Proves capability (sublinear regret) and safety (no decidable exploits) properties.

entry.title: Linear Probe Accuracy Scales with Model Size and Benefits from Multi-Layer Ensembling

author.name: Erik Nordby, Tasha Pais, Aviel Parrack

entry.summary: Shows that multi-layer ensemble linear probes can detect when LLMs produce outputs they 'know' are wrong, with probe accuracy scaling with model size (~5% AUROC per 10x parameters). Deception directions rotate gradually across layers.

entry.title: SpatialEvo: Self-Evolving Spatial Intelligence via Deterministic Geometric Environments

author.name: Dinging Li, Yingxiu Zhao, Xinrui Cheng, Kangheng Lin, Hongbo Peng, Hongxing Li, Zixuan Wang, Yuhong Dai, Haodong Li, Jia Wang, Yukang Shi, Liang Zhao, Jianjian Sun, Zheng Ge, Xiangyu Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Presents SpatialEvo, a self-evolving framework for 3D spatial reasoning that leverages the fact that ground truth in 3D scenes is deterministically computable from geometry, eliminating reliance on model consensus for pseudo-labels.

entry.title: Design Conditions for Intra-Group Learning of Sequence-Level Rewards: Token Gradient Cancellation

author.name: Fei Ding, Yongkang Zhang, youwei wang, Zijian Zeng

entry.summary: Identifies a necessary condition for intra-group RL fine-tuning: gradient exchangeability across token updates to prevent reward-irrelevant drift. Shows common mechanisms disrupt this, causing entropy collapse and solution drift.

entry.title: English is Not All You Need: Systematically Exploring the Role of Multilinguality in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Mehak Dhaliwal, Shashwat Chaurasia, Yao Qin, Dezhi Hong, Thomas Butler

entry.summary: Presents a systematic study of multilingual post-training for LLMs, finding that increasing language coverage during fine-tuning benefits across tasks and scales, with low-resource languages gaining most and high-resource languages plateauing.

entry.title: The Long Delay to Arithmetic Generalization: When Learned Representations Outrun Behavior

author.name: Laura Gomezjurado Gonzalez

entry.summary: Studies grokking in transformers, arguing the delay between memorization and generalization reflects a decoder bottleneck rather than failure to learn structure. Shows the encoder organizes parity structure early while output accuracy lags by tens of thousands of steps.

entry.title: (How) Learning Rates Regulate Catastrophic Overtraining

author.name: Mark Rofin, Aditya Varre, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: Analyzes how learning rates regulate catastrophic overtraining during SFT, showing large and small learning rates converge to qualitatively different models, and that learning rate decay increases forgetting by reducing implicit regularization.

entry.title: Exploration and Exploitation Errors Are Measurable for Language Model Agents

author.name: Jaden Park, Jungtaek Kim, Jongwon Jeong, Robert D. Nowak, Kangwook Lee, Yong Jae Lee

entry.summary: Proposes a framework with controllable 2D grid environments and task DAGs to separately measure exploration and exploitation errors in LM agents, without access to internal policies. This enables systematic diagnosis of where agents fail in open-ended decision-making tasks.

entry.title: TREX: Automating LLM Fine-tuning via Agent-Driven Tree-based Exploration

author.name: Zerun Ma, Guoqiang Wang, Xinchen Xie, Yicheng Chen, He Du, Bowen Li, Yanan Sun, Wenran Liu, Kai Chen, Yining Li

entry.summary: Introduces TREX, a multi-agent system automating the entire LLM training lifecycle including literature research, data curation, strategy formulation, and model training. Models the experimental process as a search tree for efficient exploration.

entry.title: OmniTrace: A Unified Framework for Generation-Time Attribution in Omni-Modal LLMs

author.name: Qianqi Yan, Yichen Guo, Ching-Chen Kuo, Shan Jiang, Hang Yin, Yang Zhao, Xin Eric Wang

entry.summary: Introduces OmniTrace, a model-agnostic framework for generation-time attribution in multimodal LLMs that traces which input sources (text, image, audio, video) support each generated statement during autoregressive decoding.

entry.title: Identifiability of Potentially Degenerate Gaussian Mixture Models With Piecewise Affine Mixing

author.name: Danru Xu, S\'ebastien Lachapelle, Sara Magliacane

entry.summary: Studies identifiability of causal representations when latent variables follow potentially degenerate Gaussian mixtures observed through piecewise affine mixing. Provides progressively stronger identifiability results using sparsity regularization.

entry.title: Can Cross-Layer Transcoders Replace Vision Transformer Activations? An Interpretable Perspective on Vision

author.name: Gerasimos Chatzoudis, Konstantinos D. Polyzos, Zhuowei Li, Difei Gu, Gemma E. Moran, Hao Wang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Introduces Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) as interpretable proxy models for MLP blocks in Vision Transformers, replacing single-layer Sparse Autoencoders. CLTs capture cross-layer computational structure and produce sparse, depth-aware decompositions of ViT activations. Shows improved interpretability and layer importance analysis.

entry.title: Event Tensor: A Unified Abstraction for Compiling Dynamic Megakernel

author.name: Hongyi Jin, Bohan Hou, Guanjie Wang, Ruihang Lai, Jinqi Chen, Zihao Ye, Yaxing Cai, Yixin Dong, Xinhao Cheng, Zhihao Zhang, Yilong Zhao, Yingyi Huang, Lijie Yang, Jinchen Jiang, Gabriele Oliaro, Jianan Ji, Xupeng Miao, Vinod Grover, Todd C. Mowry, Zhihao Jia, Tianqi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Event Tensor, a compiler abstraction for dynamic megakernels that handles shape and data-dependent dynamism in GPU workloads, achieving significant speedups for LLM inference by eliminating kernel launch overheads.

entry.title: Who Gets Flagged? The Pluralistic Evaluation Gap in AI Content Watermarking

author.name: Alexander Nemecek, Osama Zafar, Yuqiao Xu, Wenbiao Li, Erman Ayday

entry.summary: Examines how AI content watermarking creates modality-specific pathways to bias, as watermark strength and detectability vary across languages, cultural traditions, and demographic groups. Finds major benchmarks fail to report cross-demographic performance.

entry.title: Why Multimodal In-Context Learning Lags Behind? Unveiling the Inner Mechanisms and Bottlenecks

author.name: Yu Wang, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes why multimodal in-context learning lags behind text-only ICL, decomposing it into task mapping construction and transfer. Shows multimodal ICL degrades significantly with few-shot demonstrations.

entry.title: Reward Design for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Derek Lilienthal, Manisha Mukherjee, Sameera Horawalavithana

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic reward ablation study for GRPO-based VLM training on physical reasoning tasks, comparing four reward signals of increasing semantic richness. Finds that richer rewards improve physical reasoning in vision-language models.

entry.title: Lossless Prompt Compression via Dictionary-Encoding and In-Context Learning: Enabling Cost-Effective LLM Analysis of Repetitive Data

author.name: Andresa Rodrigues de Campos, David Lee, Imry Kissos, Piyush Paritosh

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs can learn dictionary encoding keys in-context and perform analysis on compressed representations, enabling lossless prompt compression without fine-tuning. Achieves 35-40% token reduction for repetitive data.

entry.title: Momentum Further Constrains Sharpness at the Edge of Stochastic Stability

author.name: Arseniy Andreyev, Advikar Ananthkumar, Marc Walden, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: Demonstrates that SGD with momentum exhibits Edge of Stochastic Stability behavior with batch-size-dependent regimes, showing Batch Sharpness converges to different plateaus depending on batch size.

entry.title: An Empirical Investigation of Practical LLM-as-a-Judge Improvement Techniques on RewardBench 2

author.name: Ryan Lail

entry.summary: Empirically investigates practical techniques for improving LLM-as-judge accuracy on RewardBench 2, finding task-specific criteria injection (+3pp) and ensemble scoring (+9.8pp) account for nearly all gains, reaching 83.6% with GPT-5.4.

entry.title: Bias at the End of the Score

author.name: Salma Abdel Magid, Grace Guo, Esin Tureci, Amaya Dharmasiri, Vikram V. Ramaswamy, Hanspeter Pfister, Olga Russakovsky

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale audit of reward model robustness with respect to demographic biases in text-to-image generation systems. Examines how RMs used at various pipeline stages encode biased scoring.

entry.title: ALEval: Do language models lie about reward hacking?

author.name: Mark Kagach

entry.summary: Introduces ALEval, the first action-based lying evaluation for language models focused on coding reward hacking. Tests 6 frontier models on 103 tasks, finding wide variation in reward hacking rates (>75% for some, <5% for others) with most models acknowledging hacking when asked.

entry.title: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents

author.name: Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Xuchao Zhang, Chaoyun Zhang, Wenlin Yao, Fazle Elahi Faisal, Baolin Peng, Si Qin, Suman Nath, Qingwei Lin, Chetan Bansal, Dongmei Zhang, Saravan Rajmohan, Jianfeng Gao, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: Introduces WebXSkill, a framework bridging textual workflow skills and executable code-based skills for autonomous web agents. Creates 'executable skills' pairing parameterized action programs with step-level natural language guidance for error recovery and adaptation.

entry.title: The cognitive companion: a lightweight parallel monitoring architecture for detecting and recovering from reasoning degradation in LLM agents

author.name: Rafflesia Khan, Nafiul Islam Khan

entry.summary: Introduces the Cognitive Companion, a parallel monitoring architecture to detect and recover from reasoning degradation (looping, drift, stuck states) in LLM agents. The probe-based variant achieves zero overhead while reducing repetition by 52-62%.

entry.title: Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents

author.name: Kangsan Kim, Minki Kang, Taeil Kim, Yanlai Yang, Mengye Ren, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Investigates Memory Transfer Learning for coding agents, showing that cross-domain memory from heterogeneous coding tasks improves performance by 3.7% on average. Evaluates four memory representations from concrete traces to abstract insights across 6 benchmarks.

entry.title: InfiniteScienceGym: An Unbounded, Procedurally-Generated Benchmark for Scientific Analysis

author.name: Oliver Bentham, Vivek Srikumar

entry.summary: Presents InfiniteScienceGym, a procedurally generated benchmark for evaluating LLMs as scientific assistants. Generates self-contained repositories with tabular data and verifiable QA tasks from a seed, avoiding publication and known-knowledge biases.

entry.title: Ordinary Least Squares is a Special Case of Transformer

author.name: Xiaojun Tan, Yuchen Zhao

entry.summary: Proves that Ordinary Least Squares is a special case of a single-layer linear Transformer through spectral decomposition, showing the attention forward pass can be equivalent to OLS projection in one pass.

entry.title: Gaslight, Gatekeep, V1-V3: Early Visual Cortex Alignment Shields Vision-Language Models from Sycophantic Manipulation

author.name: Arya Shah, Vaibhav Tripathi, Mayank Singh, Chaklam Silpasuwanchai

entry.summary: Studies whether VLMs with visual representations more aligned to human early visual cortex (V1-V3) are more resistant to sycophantic manipulation. Evaluates 12 models across 6 architectures, finding brain-aligned models show greater robustness.

entry.title: HiVLA: A Visual-Grounded-Centric Hierarchical Embodied Manipulation System

author.name: Tianshuo Yang, Guanyu Chen, Yutian Chen, Zhixuan Liang, Yitian Liu, Zanxin Chen, Chunpu Xu, Haotian Liang, Jiangmiao Pang, Yao Mu, Ping Luo

entry.summary: Introduces HiVLA, a hierarchical framework that decouples high-level VLM planning (with visual grounding) from low-level motor control via a flow-matching Diffusion Transformer, preserving reasoning capabilities while enabling precise manipulation.

entry.title: Some Theoretical Limitations of t-SNE

author.name: Rupert Li, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical limitations of t-SNE by providing mathematical proofs showing how important data features are lost through t-SNE dimensionality reduction in various scenarios.

entry.title: DiPO: Disentangled Perplexity Policy Optimization for Fine-grained Exploration-Exploitation Trade-Off

author.name: Xiaofan Li, Ming Yang, Zhiyuan Ma, Shichao Ma, Jintao Du, Yu Cheng, Weiqiang Wang, Zhizhong Zhang, Xin Tan, Yanyun Qu, Lizhuang Ma, Yuan Xie

entry.summary: Proposes DiPO, which disentangles perplexity space into exploration and exploitation subspaces during RLVR training, applying different reward mechanisms to hard vs easy samples for fine-grained trade-off management.

entry.title: C2: Scalable Rubric-Augmented Reward Modeling from Binary Preferences

author.name: Akira Kawabata, Saku Sugawara

entry.summary: Proposes C2 (Cooperative yet Critical) reward modeling, training a rubric generator from binary preferences alone to produce rubrics that improve reward model judgments, addressing the scalability bottleneck of rubric annotation.

entry.title: Unleashing Implicit Rewards: Prefix-Value Learning for Distribution-Level Optimization

author.name: Shiping Gao, Hongzhan Chen, Xiaojun Quan, Qifan Wang, Lifu Huang

entry.summary: Proposes prefix-value learning for process reward models that addresses the train-inference mismatch in implicit PRMs by learning distribution-level optimization rather than relying on weakly identified token-level credits.

entry.title: Robust Reward Modeling for Large Language Models via Causal Decomposition

author.name: Yunsheng Lu, Zijiang Yang, Licheng Pan, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: Proposes a causal decomposition approach to robust reward modeling that learns a decoder mapping answers to latent intent embeddings, using reconstruction error to regularize against spurious cues like length and sycophancy.

entry.title: From Weights to Activations: Is Steering the Next Frontier of Adaptation?

author.name: Simon Ostermann, Daniil Gurgurov, Tanja Baeumel, Michael A. Hedderich, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek, Vera Schmitt

entry.summary: Argues that activation steering should be formally recognized as a model adaptation paradigm alongside fine-tuning and prompting. Introduces functional criteria to compare steering with classical adaptation methods and identifies unique properties and limitations.

entry.title: Enhancing Mixture-of-Experts Specialization via Cluster-Aware Upcycling

author.name: Sanghyeok Chu, Pyunghwan Ahn, Gwangmo Song, SeungHwan Kim, Honglak Lee, Bohyung Han

entry.summary: Proposes Cluster-aware Upcycling for Mixture-of-Experts initialization that partitions dense model activations into semantic clusters and initializes each expert with its cluster's subspace, breaking expert symmetry.

entry.title: POINTS-Seeker: Towards Training a Multimodal Agentic Search Model from Scratch

author.name: Yikun Liu, Yuan Liu, Le Tian, Xiao Zhou, Jiangchao Yao, Yanfeng Wang, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: Proposes POINTS-Seeker for training a multimodal agentic search model from scratch, with Agentic Seeding for foundational agentic behaviors and solutions for long-horizon inference bottlenecks.

entry.title: Seedance 2.0: Advancing Video Generation for World Complexity

author.name: Team Seedance, De Chen, Liyang Chen, Xin Chen, Ying Chen, Zhuo Chen, Zhuowei Chen, Feng Cheng, Tianheng Cheng, Yufeng Cheng, Mojie Chi, Xuyan Chi, Jian Cong, Qinpeng Cui, Fei Ding, Qide Dong, Yujiao Du, Haojie Duanmu, Junliang Fan, Jiarui Fang, Jing Fang, Zetao Fang, Chengjian Feng, Yu Gao, Diandian Gu, Dong Guo, Hanzhong Guo, Qiushan Guo, Boyang Hao, Hongxiang Hao, Haoxun He, Jiaao He, Qian He, Tuyen Hoang, Heng Hu, Ruoqing Hu, Yuxiang Hu, Jiancheng Huang, Weilin Huang, Zhaoyang Huang, Zhongyi Huang, Jishuo Jin, Ming Jing, Ashley Kim, Shanshan Lao, Yichong Leng, Bingchuan Li, Gen Li, Haifeng Li, Huixia Li, Jiashi Li, Ming Li, Xiaojie Li, Xingxing Li, Yameng Li, Yiying Li, Yu Li, Yueyan Li, Chao Liang, Han Liang, Jianzhong Liang, Ying Liang, Wang Liao, J. H.
